findings.title: Web invite set-password flow is blocked by the auth proxy middleware: unauthenticated invitees always get 401
findings.evidence: SetPasswordForm.tsx:27 posts to fetch("/api/proxy/auth/set-password", {method:"POST", ...}). proxy.ts:17-24 intercepts every /api/proxy request: `const token = await getToken({ req }); if (!token) { return ... new NextResponse('Unauthorized', { status: 401 }) }`. An invited user activating their account has no NextAuth session (they have no password yet), so the POST never reaches the backend endpoint (AuthController.java:259 @PostMapping("/set-password")) and the form falls into the generic else branch "Could not set password. Please try again." (SetPasswordForm.tsx:40-42). This IS the primary invite path: PayloadVarsExtractor.java:54 builds the emailed link as `base + "/" + lang + "/auth/set-password?token=" + token`, i.e. the web page. Note the GET validate call works only because the server component (set-password/page.tsx:16-18) calls BACKEND_URL directly, bypassing the proxy — the client POST does not.
findings.recommendation: Exempt /api/proxy/auth/set-password (and any other pre-auth endpoints) from the token check in proxy.ts, or have the form POST to a server action / direct route that forwards to BACKEND_URL like the validate call does.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. The invite email (PayloadVarsExtractor.computeCtaUrl, USER_INVITED) links to /{lang}/auth/set-password?token=..., whose server component validates the token by calling BACKEND_URL directly (bypassing the proxy), so the page renders. But the client submit (SetPasswordForm.tsx:27) posts to /api/proxy/auth/set-password, and web/src/proxy.ts — the active Next.js 16 proxy/middleware file, matcher '/api/proxy/:path*' — returns 401 whenever getToken() is null (lines 21-24). Invitees have no NextAuth session by definition, so the POST never reaches the next.config.ts rewrite or the public backend endpoint (AuthController /api/auth/set-password, line 259, which authenticates solely via the body token). No rescue exists: no app/api/proxy route handler, no public-path allowlist, and /api/auth/set-password on the web origin is shadowed by the NextAuth catch-all. The 401 lands in the form's generic else branch. Severity downgraded from critical to high: it fully breaks web invite activation, but it is a functional regression with no security/data impact, mobile clients are unaffected, and admins have a workaround (superadmin user creation accepts an explicit password, superadmin/users/page.tsx:127).

findings.title: Manager app staff create/edit sends a User-shaped body to /v1/staff; nameEn is always null so every create/update violates the NOT NULL name_en column
findings.evidence: staff_screen.dart:333-339 creates via `service.createStaff({'name': ..., 'email': ..., 'phone': ..., 'role': role})` and staff_detail_screen.dart:229-235 updates via `service.updateStaff(widget.staffId, {'name': ..., 'email': ..., 'phone': ..., 'role': role})` with role values 'PROPERTY_MANAGER'/'TENANT_USER'. But StaffController.java:38 binds `@RequestBody Staff staff` — the Staff entity (Staff.java) has fields nameEn/nameAr/employeeId/designation/department/monthlySalary/phone/property/salaryAccount and NO name/email/role fields, and `@Column(name = "name_en", nullable = false) private String nameEn`. Jackson silently drops name/email/role, leaving nameEn null; repository.save() then hits the NOT NULL name_en column -> DataIntegrityViolationException -> 500 on every create. For update, StaffService.updateStaff copies `existing.setNameEn(updates.getNameEn())` (null) and fails the same way, and would also null out nameAr/employeeId/designation/property/salaryAccount if it saved. The screen was evidently written against /api/admin/users semantics (user accounts with roles) but wired to the HR staff endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Point these screens at the correct API (likely /admin/users if the intent is provisioning PROPERTY_MANAGER/TENANT_USER accounts) or rewrite the forms to send Staff fields (nameEn, nameAr, designation, phone, property:{id}, ...). Do not ship both a create and an edit path that can never succeed.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. The manager app's staff screens (staff_screen.dart:333-339, staff_detail_screen.dart:229-235) send {'name','email','phone','role'} through rentaxis_core StaffService, whose Dio (baseUrl ending in /api) POSTs/PUTs to /api/v1/staff — exactly StaffController. The controller binds @RequestBody Staff, and the Staff entity has nameEn/nameAr/employeeId/... with NO name/email/role fields; no @JsonAlias, RequestBodyAdvice, or fail-on-unknown-properties override exists, so Jackson silently drops those keys (only 'phone' maps). name_en is NOT NULL in both the entity (@Column nullable=false) and Liquibase changeset 21-staff-management.yaml, so every create fails with a not-null violation (500). updateStaff copies the null nameEn onto the existing row and fails identically (transaction rolls back, so no persisted corruption). Corroborating: the screens read s['name']/s['email']/s['role']/s['propertyIds'] from GET responses that actually serialize nameEn/nameAr/etc., so existing staff render as 'Unknown' — the screen was written for a user-account API shape but wired to the HR staff endpoint. Severity downgraded from critical to high: the feature is completely broken in the mobile admin app, but there is no data loss, no security/tenant-isolation impact, and the web client is unaffected.

findings.title: Manager app staff list/detail read nonexistent fields (name/email/role/propertyIds) from the Staff DTO — every row renders 'Unknown' and search/property filter never match
findings.evidence: staff_screen.dart:150-151 filters on `(s['name'] ?? '')` and `(s['email'] ?? '')`; :157-159 filters on `(s['propertyIds'] as List<dynamic>?)`; _StaffCard (:529-533) reads staff['name'], staff['email'], staff['role'], staff['propertyIds']. The backend returns the raw Staff entity whose JSON keys are nameEn, nameAr, employeeId, designation, department, monthlySalary, joinDate, phone, emiratesId, passportNumber, property (object), salaryAccount, active — none of name/email/role/propertyIds exist. Result: every card title is 'Unknown' (staff_screen.dart:529 `staff['name'] ?? l.unknown`), no role pill, any non-empty search returns zero rows (contains() on ''), and selecting a property filter chip excludes everything (propertyIds always []). staff_detail_screen.dart:115-121 prefills its edit form from the same nonexistent keys.
findings.recommendation: Render nameEn/nameAr (locale-aware), phone, designation and property.nameEn from the actual Staff DTO, and filter by `s['property']?['id']` — mirroring web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/staff/page.tsx which consumes the same endpoint correctly.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Mobile StaffService (rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/staff_service.dart) GETs /v1/staff on baseUrl .../api → StaffController (@RequestMapping "/api/v1/staff"), which returns raw Staff entities. Staff.java has only nameEn/nameAr/employeeId/designation/department/monthlySalary/joinDate/phone/emiratesId/passportNumber/property(object)/salaryAccount/isActive — no name, email, role, or propertyIds keys, and no Jackson renaming (no @JsonProperty, no naming strategy in config or yml). Dio interceptors (auth/tenant) only inject request headers; response.data is returned untransformed. Therefore staff_screen.dart:529 renders every card as 'Unknown' (staff['name'] null), no role pill (:532), search on :150-151 compares ''.contains(query) so any non-empty query returns zero rows, and the property chip filter (:157-159) reads propertyIds (always null→[]) so it excludes all rows — backend sends 'property' as a single object. staff_detail_screen.dart:115-121 prefills the edit form from the same nonexistent keys (only 'phone' matches a real key). Screen is reachable via router.dart '/staff'. The web staff page reads the correct keys (nameEn/designation/department/property), confirming the backend contract; the mobile screen was written against a user-account-shaped DTO that doesn't exist (its create sheet posts {name,email,role}, which can't satisfy the entity's non-null nameEn). Severity 'high' is appropriate: the entire staff feature in the manager app is nonfunctional (unreadable list, dead search/filter, blank edit prefill, create cannot succeed), and long-press delete still works on rows the user cannot identify, creating a misdelete hazard — though no data leak, crash, or security impact, and the web dashboard offers a working alternative.

findings.title: Mobile password login cannot complete the backend's 409 multi-tenant disambiguation flow — multi-tenant users are locked out with 'Invalid email or password'
findings.evidence: AuthController.java:44 documents `tenantId` as the disambiguator and :159-173 returns 409 CONFLICT with LoginAmbiguousResponse{tenants:[{tenantId,tenantName}]} when the password matches in multiple tenants, expecting the client to re-submit with tenantId. auth_service.dart:16-22 sends only `{'email': ..., 'password': ...}` — there is no tenantId parameter anywhere in the mobile stack — and auth_provider.dart:144-153 catches every DioException (including the 409) as `error: 'Invalid email or password'`. The web client implements the picker (web/src/auth.ts:53-57 parses the 409 body into LOGIN_AMBIGUOUS), so any email that exists in two tenants with the same password can log in on web but is permanently and misleadingly rejected by both Flutter apps.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional tenantId to AuthService.login, catch status 409 in AuthNotifier.login, surface the returned tenants list as a picker, and re-submit with the chosen tenantId — mirroring the web flow.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend: AuthController.java defines LoginRequest(email, password, tenantId) (line 44) and, when the submitted password matches candidate users in more than one tenant, returns 409 CONFLICT with LoginAmbiguousResponse{tenants:[{tenantId,tenantName}]} (lines 159-173), expecting the client to re-submit with tenantId to disambiguate. Mobile: AuthService.login (auth_service.dart:16-22) posts only {email, password} — grep across the entire mobile tree confirms no login call site or model handles tenantId at login or references the 409/ambiguous payload. Dio's default validateStatus throws a DioException for 409, and neither interceptor rescues it: AuthInterceptor.onError just calls handler.next(err) and TenantInterceptor is request-only (it adds X-Tenant-Id headers from post-login state, irrelevant to the login request body the backend parses). AuthNotifier.login (auth_provider.dart:143-155) catches ALL exceptions and sets error: 'Invalid email or password', so the 409 is swallowed and mislabeled. Both apps route through this one path (manager login_screen.dart:63, renter login_screen.dart:60). The web contrast also checks out: web/src/auth.ts optionally sends tenantId and converts the 409 body into a LOGIN_AMBIGUOUS signal the login page parses into a tenant picker. So the bug is real: a multi-tenant user (post-migration 59) whose password matches in >=2 tenants can log in on web but is rejected on both Flutter apps with a misleading credentials error. Severity corrected from high to medium: the affected population is narrow (requires the same email AND an identical matching password in two or more tenants), web login works as a complete alternative, and there is no security or data impact — single-tenant matches still log in fine because the 409 only fires on multiple password matches. It is a genuine functional gap with a deceptive error message (and likely support burden), but not a broad or security-relevant lockout. Fix surface: add optional tenantId to AuthService.login, stop blanket-catching in AuthNotifier.login, and surface a tenant picker on 409 mirroring web/src/auth.ts.

findings.title: Web registration page never calls POST /api/auth/register — it fakes a 1s delay and redirects to login as if the account was created
findings.evidence: register/page.tsx:41-46: `// For Phase 3, we'll just simulate registration for now ... await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000)); router.push("/auth/login?registered=true");` — formData (fullName, email, password, companyName) is collected then discarded. The backend endpoint exists and is fully functional (AuthController.java:202-226 provisions a LandlordOrg and a TENANT_ADMIN user) and its RegisterRequest record (:47) matches the form's field names exactly. A user who "registers" lands on the login page with a success banner and then cannot log in, because no account was ever created. No frontend calls this endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Wire the form to POST /api/auth/register (via a public route — note the /api/proxy middleware requires a session, so call BACKEND_URL from a server action or add a proxy exemption), or remove/disable the registration page until the flow is real.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. web/src/app/[locale]/auth/register/page.tsx:41-50 contains exactly the claimed code: after local password validation, it awaits a 1s setTimeout and pushes to /auth/login?registered=true under the comment "For Phase 3, we'll just simulate registration for now" — formData is never sent (no fetch/axios/server action). A repo-wide grep shows no web code calls POST /api/auth/register, so no interceptor, Next.js rewrite, or shared client rescues it. The page is reachable in production UX: login/page.tsx:221 links to it via "Create Account". The backend endpoint (AuthController.java:202-226) is real and functional, and RegisterRequest (line 47) matches the form fields, so wiring it up was possible but never done. One minor evidence overstatement: the login page never reads ?registered=true, so no success banner is shown — but the spinner-then-redirect still presents as success, so the substance (user believes an account was created; none was; login fails) holds. Severity 'high' stands: a publicly linked self-service signup flow silently no-ops and fakes success with no user workaround; it is functional/UX (not security/data-loss), so not critical, but it fully breaks a core flow.

findings.title: Ticket-detail 'Assign To...' silently broken for PROPERTY_MANAGER: page fetches /api/admin/users, which UserController restricts to SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN
findings.evidence: tickets/[id]/page.tsx:149-158: `if (userRole === "RENTER") return;` then `fetch("/api/proxy/admin/users")` with the failure swallowed (`catch { /* ignore */ }` and no else on !res.ok). UserController.java:21-22 is `@RequestMapping("/api/admin/users") @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN')")`, so a PROPERTY_MANAGER (or TENANT_USER) gets 403 on every ticket-detail load. Yet page.tsx:299 computes `canManage = isAdmin || isPM` and :522-527 renders the "Assign To..." dropdown only when `canManage && ... && staffUsers.length > 0` — for a PM, staffUsers is always [] so the assignment feature the page explicitly grants them never appears, with no error shown. The page's own gatepass sibling documents the same constraint (dashboard/gatepass/page.tsx:34 "...but not /api/admin/users, so this page cannot turn an id into a person itself").
findings.recommendation: Gate fetchStaff on hasRole(userRole, ['SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN']) and give PMs a PM-accessible assignee source (e.g. a tenant-scoped assignable-users endpoint), or widen the controller guard deliberately. Also stop hiding the 403: surface why assignment is unavailable.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. tickets/[id]/page.tsx:149-158 fetches /api/proxy/admin/users for any non-RENTER role and swallows failures (res.ok guard + empty catch). next.config.ts:25-26 rewrites this verbatim to backend /api/admin/users; no app route shadows it and web/src/proxy.ts only forwards the user's own role (X-User-Role), no elevation. UserController.java:21-22 gates the whole controller with hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN'); @EnableMethodSecurity is on (SecurityConfig.java:18) and ApiSecurityFilter.java:84 grants exactly ROLE_<userRole>, so PROPERTY_MANAGER gets 403 and staffUsers stays []. page.tsx:299 computes canManage = isAdmin || isPM, and the "Assign To..." dropdown at :522 also requires staffUsers.length > 0 — permanently false for a PM, so the feature the UI grants them never renders and no error is shown. Intent is corroborated: MaintenanceTicketController.java:46-47 explicitly permits PROPERTY_MANAGER on PUT /{id}/assign, and dashboard/gatepass/page.tsx:33-35 documents the same /api/admin/users restriction. Severity downgraded from high to medium: PMs retain a working "Assign to Me" button (page.tsx:517-520) and admins see the full dropdown, so only assign-to-others is silently missing for one role, with easy workarounds and no data-loss or security impact.

findings.title: Editing a PROPERTY_MANAGER and removing all their properties silently does nothing: empty propertyIds is omitted, and the backend treats null as 'skip sync'
findings.evidence: page.tsx:129-131: `if (role === 'PROPERTY_MANAGER' && selectedPropertyIds.length > 0) { bodyData.propertyIds = selectedPropertyIds; }` — an empty selection is never sent. UserController.java:101 only syncs when `request.propertyIds() != null`: removals are computed against the submitted list (:102-107), so a null list skips the whole block. Concrete scenario: admin edits a PM, removes the last assigned property chip, clicks Update — the PUT succeeds (200) and the UI closes, but userService.getAssignedPropertyIds still returns the old assignments; the PM keeps property access the admin believes was revoked.
findings.recommendation: Send `bodyData.propertyIds = selectedPropertyIds` unconditionally whenever role === 'PROPERTY_MANAGER' (including []), which the backend already interprets as 'remove everything not listed'.

findings.title: AuthNotifier._init falls back to tenants[0]['tenantId'], a field /api/auth/me/tenants does not return (keys are id/name/slug)
findings.evidence: auth_provider.dart:129-131 restores a session with `tenantId: savedTenantId ?? (tenants.isNotEmpty ? tenants[0]['tenantId'] : null)`. The endpoint's DTO is `record TenantInfo(String id, String name, String slug)` (AuthController.java:309), so `tenants[0]['tenantId']` is always null and the fallback can never produce a tenant. The correct key is used two functions away in resolveTenantSlug (auth_provider.dart:50 `t['id'] == auth.tenantId`). The fallback path triggers when secure storage has userId but no tenantId (e.g. an account whose AuthResponse.tenantId was null at login, since _establishSession:180-185 skips the write), leaving AuthState.tenantId null and TenantContext unset for the whole restored session.
findings.recommendation: Use `tenants[0]['id']` in the fallback, and consider persisting it back to storage so subsequent restores are consistent.

findings.title: Superadmin users page swallows all API errors: failed create/update/delete (400 duplicate email, guard-phone conflict, 403) leaves the form open with no message
findings.evidence: page.tsx:138-152 handleSubmitUser: `if (res.ok) { setShowForm(false); ... }` with no else branch — a 400 from IllegalArgumentException ("A user with this email already exists in this tenant.", UserService.createUser:187-192; guard-phone-taken :198-201) or a 403 from the role-hierarchy check produces no UI feedback at all; the spinner stops and the form sits there. Same pattern in confirmDelete (:159-171), where a failed DELETE just closes the dialog as if it worked. GlobalExceptionHandler maps these to 400/403 bodies containing a message field the page never reads. Contrast with the manager app's describeGuardCreateFailure (guard_admin_service.dart:153-177) which handles the identical statuses for the same endpoint.
findings.recommendation: On !res.ok, parse the JSON body's message/error field and render it in the form (and in the delete dialog); only close on success.

findings.title: Manager app 'Staff' menu entry is not role-gated: a PROPERTY_MANAGER always gets 403 from the TENANT_ADMIN-only StaffController and sees a bare 'Failed to load staff'
findings.evidence: StaffController.java:13 gates the whole controller with `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN')")`. more_screen.dart:41-46 shows the Staff row to every manager-app user with no role check (`_MenuRow(... label: l.staff, onTap: () => context.push('/staff'))`), and the manager app is also used by PROPERTY_MANAGERs (the same file's guard/gate sections exist for them). staff_screen.dart:146-147 renders the resulting 403 as the generic `ErrorState(message: l.loadFailed)` with a retry that can never succeed. The web sidebar gets this right: the staff link is gated by canAccessFinance = SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN (MvpSidebar.tsx:115-117).
findings.recommendation: Hide the Staff menu row unless authState.role is TENANT_ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN (the role is already in AuthState), matching the controller's guard.

findings.title: Mobile change-password ignores the backend's specific 400 error body ('Current password is incorrect'), showing a generic failure for every cause
findings.evidence: AuthController.java:393-394 returns 400 with `{"error": "Current password is incorrect"}` (and :396-397 a distinct too-short message). manager profile_screen.dart:165 calls service.changePassword and the catch at :183-193 shows only the blanket `l.passwordChangeFailed` snackbar regardless of status or body (renter profile_screen.dart mirrors this at :163+). The web page reads the same body correctly (dashboard/profile/page.tsx:106-108 `setPasswordError(data.error || ...)`), so mobile users typing a wrong current password get no hint which field is wrong.
findings.recommendation: In the catch, inspect DioException.response (status 400, data['error']) and show the backend message, falling back to the generic string otherwise.

findings.title: Mobile PUT /auth/me cannot clear the phone number: the key is omitted when empty and the backend only writes non-null phoneNumber
findings.evidence: auth_service.dart:40-45 builds the body with `if (phoneNumber != null) 'phoneNumber': phoneNumber` and manager profile_screen.dart:110-115 passes `phoneNumber: _phoneController.text.trim().isNotEmpty ? ... : null`, so emptying the field sends no key. AuthController.java:360-366 only updates when `request.phoneNumber() != null`, so the old number persists while the app shows a success snackbar ("Profile updated") — the next reload restores the number the user deleted. Web sends the empty string, which the backend does accept as a clear.
findings.recommendation: Send `'phoneNumber': ''` (or an explicit empty string sentinel) when the user clears the field, matching the web behavior the backend already supports.

findings.title: web/src/lib/rbac.ts ROLE_RANK orders SECURITY_GUARD/TENANT_USER/RENTER differently from UserController.privilegeRank despite claiming to mirror it
findings.evidence: rbac.ts:45-53 ranks SECURITY_GUARD: 3, TENANT_USER: 4, RENTER: 5 under the comment "Mirrors the backend hierarchy enforced in UserController"; UserController.java:197-206 ranks TENANT_USER -> 3, RENTER -> 4, SECURITY_GUARD -> 5. For the roles that can actually reach the endpoint (SUPER_ADMIN, TENANT_ADMIN) the assignable sets happen to coincide, so there is no runtime breakage today — but any future caller ranked between these roles (or a guard-facing admin UI) would let the web offer role options the backend rejects with 403, or vice versa.
findings.recommendation: Align ROLE_RANK's bottom three with privilegeRank (TENANT_USER 3, RENTER 4, SECURITY_GUARD 5) so the two tables stay a true mirror.

findings.title: Manager-app gateway screen reads four fields that do not exist in TenantGatewayConfigDTO — status badge always shows Inactive, provider always '-', Key ID row never renders
findings.evidence: Backend response DTO (TenantGatewayConfigDTO.java:8-20, populated by TenantGatewayConfigService.mapToDTO lines 89-115) serializes exactly: id, gatewayId, gatewayCode, gatewayName, apiKeyMasked, hasWebhookSecret, isActive, isTestMode (apiKey/apiSecret/webhookSecret nulled). The manager screen reads keys that are not in that set: gateway_config_screen.dart:202-204 `config['active'] == true || config['status']?.toString().toUpperCase() == 'ACTIVE'` (DTO key is 'isActive'; 'active'/'status' are always null, so isActive is always false and _StatusCard renders the red 'Inactive' badge for every configured, active gateway); lines 269-270 `config['providerType'] ?? config['provider']` (neither exists — DTO has 'gatewayCode' — so Provider Type always renders '-'); line 271 `config['keyId'] ?? config['key_id']` (DTO has 'apiKeyMasked' — keyId is always '' so the Key ID row at lines 311-317 is never shown). Verified call path: SettingsService.getGatewayConfig (rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/settings_service.dart:18-22) GETs '/v1/gateway-config' via Dio (baseUrl ends in '/api').
findings.recommendation: In _StatusCard use config['isActive'] == true; in _ConfigCard read config['gatewayCode'] for the provider row and config['apiKeyMasked'] for the key row (and drop the client-side re-masking — the backend already masks).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend GET /api/v1/gateway-config serializes TenantGatewayConfigDTO with camelCase keys (id, gatewayId, gatewayCode, gatewayName, apiKeyMasked, hasWebhookSecret, isActive, isTestMode; secrets nulled) — verified via the DTO (boxed Boolean isActive → Jackson "isActive"), no @JsonProperty/naming-strategy config, and the web page at web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/settings/gateway/page.tsx which reads exactly those keys. The mobile chain has no fix-up: SettingsService.getGatewayConfig returns response.data raw and ApiClient interceptors only add headers. gateway_config_screen.dart reads nonexistent keys: lines 202-204 'active'/'status' (so isActive is always false and the status badge always shows Inactive — doubly wrong since the endpoint only returns configs from findByIsActiveTrue), lines 269-270 'providerType'/'provider' (Provider Type always '-'; gatewayCode unused), line 271 'keyId'/'key_id' (empty, so the Key ID row guarded by keyId.isNotEmpty at line 311 never renders; apiKeyMasked unused). Only gatewayName coincidentally matches. Severity downgraded from critical to medium: this is a display-only defect on a read-only admin info screen — payment processing, configuration, and security are unaffected; the harm is a misleading "Inactive" label and missing provider/key details.

findings.title: Web gateway settings: saving without re-typing credentials overwrites the real API key with the masked placeholder and wipes the API secret
findings.evidence: GET response deliberately masks/omits secrets: mapToDTO sets apiKeyMasked = first8+'****' and apiKey/apiSecret = null (TenantGatewayConfigService.java:96-110). The web page pre-fills the API Key input with that masked value — page.tsx:88 `setApiKey(config.apiKeyMasked || "")` — and apiSecret starts as "" (page.tsx:52) and is never pre-filled. handleSave (page.tsx:122-131) POSTs `{ gatewayId, apiKey, apiSecret, webhookSecret, isTestMode }` verbatim. saveConfig persists both unconditionally: `config.setApiKeyEncrypted(encryptionService.encrypt(dto.getApiKey())); config.setApiSecretEncrypted(encryptionService.encrypt(dto.getApiSecret()))` (TenantGatewayConfigService.java:50-51) — only webhookSecret has keep-if-blank handling (lines 52-54, matching the UI hint at page.tsx:316-318). So a TENANT_ADMIN who opens the page with an existing config and clicks Save (e.g. just to flip test mode) stores 'rzp_test****' as the key and an encrypted empty string as the secret, breaking Razorpay payments until both are re-entered. The post-save refetch (page.tsx:135) re-fills the masked key, so repeat saves keep corrupting.
findings.recommendation: Backend: skip apiKey/apiSecret updates when blank or when apiKey equals the masked form (mirror the webhookSecret guard). Web: do not pre-fill the key field with apiKeyMasked (show it as a placeholder/hint instead) and omit blank credential fields from the POST body.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. GET /api/v1/gateway-config masks the key (TenantGatewayConfigService.mapToDTO lines 96-110: first8+"****", apiKey/apiSecret nulled). The web page pre-fills the API Key input with that mask (page.tsx:88 setApiKey(config.apiKeyMasked || "")) and never pre-fills apiSecret (starts ""). handleSave (page.tsx:122-131) POSTs state verbatim through a pure-passthrough Next.js rewrite (next.config.ts:25-26, no route handler). The controller (TenantGatewayConfigController:39) does no validation, and saveConfig (service lines 50-51) unconditionally encrypts and persists both apiKey and apiSecret — only webhookSecret has keep-if-blank handling (lines 52-54). EncryptionService.encrypt("") does not throw (AES/GCM doFinal on empty bytes is valid), so the empty secret is silently stored. Result: an admin who opens the page with an existing config and clicks Save (e.g., to flip test mode) stores "rzp_test****" as the key and an encrypted empty string as the secret, breaking Razorpay payments; the UI shows success and the post-save refetch (page.tsx:135) re-fills the mask so repeat saves keep corrupting. No wrapper, interceptor, or validation refutes any step. Severity "high" is right: silent corruption of payment credentials from a routine admin action that breaks all online rent collection, but not critical since it requires an authenticated admin action, is not a security/tenant-isolation issue, and is recoverable by re-entering credentials from the Razorpay dashboard.

findings.title: Superadmin 'Provision New Organization' form collects address, TRN, phone, logo and ticket-OTP toggle, but POST /api/admin/tenants persists only the name — all other entered values are silently dropped
findings.evidence: The create modal shows Logo upload, Address, TRN, Phone and the Ticket Closure OTP toggle in create mode too (page.tsx:188-268; only Status is edit-only, line 243), and handleSubmit POSTs the full formData `{ name, address, trn, status, logoUrl, ticketOtpRequired, phone }` to /api/proxy/admin/tenants (page.tsx:61-68 with formData defined at line 26). The backend create handler reads only `payload.get("name")` and calls `service.provisionTenant(name)` (LandlordOrgController.java:29-37), and provisionTenant sets only the name (LandlordOrgService.java:36-39). Everything else the super admin typed is discarded with a 200 response and no warning — the tenant appears in the list with blank address/TRN/phone/logo and ticketOtpRequired at its DB default, until someone re-enters the data via Edit (PUT does apply these fields, LandlordOrgController.java:44-75).
findings.recommendation: Make createTenant apply the same optional fields as updateTenant (or have the web client chain a PUT after create). Alternatively hide the extra fields in create mode so the UI matches the contract.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. The create modal in web/src/app/[locale]/superadmin/tenants/page.tsx renders Logo (line 192), Address (214), TRN (224), Phone (234), and the Ticket Closure OTP toggle (261) in create mode — only Status is edit-only (line 243) — and handleSubmit (lines 56-78) POSTs the full formData {name, address, trn, status, logoUrl, ticketOtpRequired, phone} to /api/proxy/admin/tenants. The proxy is a plain Next.js rewrite (next.config.ts:25) with no body transformation. The backend createTenant handler (LandlordOrgController.java:29-37) reads only payload.get("name") and calls provisionTenant(name), which sets only the name on a new LandlordOrg (LandlordOrgService.java:36-39) and returns 200. All other entered values are silently discarded; the PUT handler (lines 44-75) does persist them, confirming the create-path gap. Severity corrected to medium: no security/tenant-isolation impact, SUPER_ADMIN-only surface, the loss is immediately visible in the tenant list (blank address/TRN), and it is fully recoverable via the Edit flow — silent operator data loss, not high-impact breakage.

findings.title: Manager app lets PROPERTY_MANAGER open Settings > Payment Gateway, but both endpoints require SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN — guaranteed 403 shown as a generic load failure
findings.evidence: Both reads are role-guarded: `@GetMapping("/gateways") @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN')")` (TenantGatewayConfigController.java:21-22) and `@GetMapping @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN', 'RENTER')")` (lines 27-28). The manager app is also used by PROPERTY_MANAGER accounts (e.g. booking_approvals_screen.dart:129 checks `authProvider.role == 'PROPERTY_MANAGER'`; staff_screen.dart creates them), yet the settings hub tile is unconditional — settings_hub_screen.dart:31-36 pushes '/settings/gateway' with no role check, reached from more_screen.dart:139-143. For a PROPERTY_MANAGER both Dio GETs throw on 403 and the screen renders only the generic 'Failed to load gateway configuration' ErrorState with a Retry button (gateway_config_screen.dart:61-62), never a permission message. Web handles the same boundary correctly via canConfigureGateway (rbac.ts:108-110, gateway page.tsx:149-159).
findings.recommendation: Gate the gateway tile (and screen) on role == TENANT_ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN like the web sidebar does, or map DioException status 403 to a dedicated 'no permission' state instead of the retryable generic error.

findings.title: Superadmin tenants page swallows all API errors on create/update — non-2xx responses close nothing, show nothing
findings.evidence: handleSubmit (page.tsx:56-78) only handles success: `if (res.ok) { resetForm(); fetchTenants(); }` — the backend's documented failure statuses (400 from POST when name is blank, LandlordOrgController.java:32-34; 404 from PUT when the id no longer exists, LandlordOrgController.java:49-51; 401/403 on session expiry) leave the modal open with no error banner, no message, and the button simply stops spinning, so the admin cannot tell whether the save happened. fetchTenants (lines 40-54) likewise renders 'No organizations provisioned yet' on a 403 rather than an error. Contrast with the gateway page which surfaces `data.message` into an error banner (gateway/page.tsx:137-140).
findings.recommendation: On !res.ok set an error state rendered in the modal (mirroring the gateway page's error banner), at minimum distinguishing validation failure from permission/session failure.

findings.title: penaltyPaymentInstructions has a read UI but no write UI anywhere — PUT /api/v1/settings/org is dead surface, so renters can only ever see instructions seeded by hand
findings.evidence: The renter penalties page consumes the GET correctly (penalties/page.tsx:335-340 reads `d.penaltyPaymentInstructions`, matching OrgSettingsController.get at lines 21-27 which returns `{penaltyPaymentInstructions: string}`). But the TENANT_ADMIN-guarded PUT (OrgSettingsController.java:29-39) has zero call sites: grep for 'settings/org' and 'penaltyPaymentInstructions' across web/src, mobile/apps and mobile/packages finds only the renter-portal GET. No settings page in web or mobile writes the value, so it defaults to null/'' and the renter-facing instructions block can only be populated via curl.
findings.recommendation: Add the write field to an admin settings page (e.g. web /dashboard/settings) or, if intentionally API-only for now, document that on the controller like LandlordOrgController's DELETE does.

findings.title: Web feature-flag cache is module-global and never invalidated, and MvpSidebar's justification comment is stale now that superadmin can flip toggles
findings.evidence: useTenantFeatures.ts:6-7 declares `let featuresCache` / `let slugCache` at module scope and lines 17-27 return the cache without ever refetching or expiring, so within one SPA session a superadmin toggle (PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/features/{feature}, LandlordOrgController.java:112-126, wired to the working drawer at superadmin/tenants/page.tsx:113-130) is invisible until a hard reload, and the cache is keyed to nothing — it survives session changes on client-side navigation. Separately, MvpSidebar.tsx:78-89 justifies leaving GATEPASS un-gated with 'setEnabled() has no caller, for ANY of the five flags — so isEnabled('GATEPASS') is false for every tenant until someone writes a tenant_feature row by hand' — that premise is now false: the superadmin features drawer calls setEnabled, so the stated blocker ('add the wrapper when a toggle exists to flip it') has been satisfied without the wrapper being added.
findings.recommendation: Key/expire the cache (e.g. per session user id, or refetch on window focus), and revisit the GATEPASS gating decision plus its comment now that the toggle UI exists.

findings.title: Web Gateway type declares supportedCurrencies as string[] but backend PaymentGatewayDTO sends a plain String
findings.evidence: page.tsx:28 types `supportedCurrencies: string[]`, but the backend field is `private String supportedCurrencies` (PaymentGatewayDTO.java:15, copied from the String column PaymentGateway.java:36), so the runtime value is a string. No harm today only because the page never renders the field, but any future `.map`/`.join` on it will break at runtime despite type-checking cleanly.
findings.recommendation: Change the TS type to `string` (or parse the delimited value into an array at the fetch boundary).

findings.title: Tenant edit sends ticketOtpRequired as a JSON boolean into a backend Map<String,String> — works only via Jackson scalar-to-String coercion
findings.evidence: The web modal serializes formData with `ticketOtpRequired: true|false` as a real JSON boolean (page.tsx:26 and 64-68), while the backend binds the body as `@RequestBody Map<String, String>` and calls `Boolean.parseBoolean(payload.get("ticketOtpRequired"))` (LandlordOrgController.java:47 and 71-73). This currently works because Jackson's StringDeserializer coerces scalar booleans to "true"/"false", but the contract is accidental: a stricter deserialization config (FAIL_ON_... coercion settings) or a typed DTO refactor breaks the toggle silently, and any future non-scalar value would 400.
findings.recommendation: Bind the PUT body to a typed DTO (Map<String, Object> at minimum, ideally a TenantUpdateDTO with Boolean ticketOtpRequired) so the boolean crosses the wire as a boolean.

findings.title: Web gateway page's 204 handling for 'no config yet' depends on res.json() throwing, and the catch also swallows real network errors
findings.evidence: The backend returns 204 No Content when no active config exists (TenantGatewayConfigController.java:30-33). In fetchExistingConfig (page.tsx:81-94), a 204 passes `res.ok`, so `await res.json()` runs on an empty body and throws a SyntaxError that is only handled by the blanket `catch (err) { // No existing config — that's fine }`. The unconfigured path works purely by exception, and the same catch hides genuine failures (backend down, proxy error), leaving the page looking merely 'unconfigured'. The mobile service handles this explicitly instead (settings_service.dart:18-22 checks `statusCode == 204`).
findings.recommendation: Check `res.status === 204` explicitly before parsing (matching the mobile client) and keep the catch for transport errors only, ideally surfacing them.

findings.title: Mobile manager 'Create Property' always fails: sends 'name' instead of required 'nameEn' and omits required 'type'
findings.evidence: Backend PropertyController.java:29-31 binds @Valid CreatePropertyDTO; CreatePropertyDTO.java:11-17 declares `@NotBlank private String nameEn` and `@NotNull private PropertyType type`. Mobile properties_screen.dart:275-279 submits `service.createProperty({'name': nameCtrl.text.trim(), 'address': ..., 'emirate': selectedEmirate})` via property_service.dart:40 (`_dio.post('/v1/properties', ...)`). Jackson ignores the unknown 'name' key, leaving nameEn=null and type=null, so validation fails and GlobalExceptionHandler.java:59-69 returns 400 on every submission; the catch at properties_screen.dart:282-286 shows only a generic 'createPropertyFailed' snackbar. Additionally the sheet's add button (properties_screen.dart:67) is not role-gated, and the endpoint's @PreAuthorize allows only SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN, so PROPERTY_MANAGER users would get 403 even after the payload is fixed.
findings.recommendation: Send {'nameEn': ..., 'type': 'RESIDENTIAL' (or a picker value), 'emirate': ..., 'address': ...} from the mobile sheet (or accept 'name' as an alias in the DTO), and hide the create action for PROPERTY_MANAGER users to match the backend role guard.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. properties_screen.dart:275-279 posts {'name','address','emirate'} via PropertyService (raw _dio.post, no body transformation); the only Dio interceptors (auth/tenant/log in api_client.dart) touch headers only. CreatePropertyDTO is a plain Lombok @Data class with @NotBlank nameEn and @NotNull type and no @JsonAlias/@JsonProperty, and no custom Jackson unknown-property config exists, so 'name' is dropped, nameEn and type stay null, @Valid triggers MethodArgumentNotValidException, and GlobalExceptionHandler returns 400 — every mobile create attempt fails with the generic snackbar. The missing 'type' field alone guarantees failure since the sheet never collects it. The secondary claim also holds: the POST is @PreAuthorize'd to SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN while the add button is shown unconditionally, so PROPERTY_MANAGER would 403 even after a payload fix. Severity corrected from critical to high: the feature is 100% broken in the mobile manager app, but it fails cleanly with no data corruption or security/tenant-isolation impact, and the web frontend provides a working alternative for the same operation.

findings.title: Mobile manager 'Create Unit' always fails: payload uses nonexistent fields (propertyId/size/annualRent) and invalid UnitType values
findings.evidence: Backend UnitController.java:29-33 binds @RequestBody Unit directly; Unit.java has `property` (ManyToOne, nullable=false column), `sizeSqft`, `expectedRent`, and `type` (enum STUDIO,BHK1,BHK2,BHK3,PENTHOUSE,RETAIL,OFFICE per UnitType.java). Mobile property_detail_screen.dart:446-454 sends {'unitNumber':..., 'propertyId': widget.propertyId, 'type': unitType, 'size':..., 'annualRent':...} via unit_service.dart:17-20. 'propertyId', 'size', 'annualRent' are not Unit fields and are silently dropped, so unit.property is null and the insert violates the NOT NULL property_id column (500 via GlobalExceptionHandler RuntimeException catch-all); the type dropdown (property_detail_screen.dart:352-362) offers APARTMENT (default), VILLA, SHOP, WAREHOUSE, TOWNHOUSE which are not UnitType constants, so Jackson enum deserialization fails first with those values. Every submission fails; the user only sees the generic 'createUnitFailed' snackbar (lines 457-461).
findings.recommendation: Send {'unitNumber':..., 'property': {'id': widget.propertyId}, 'type': <valid UnitType>, 'sizeSqft':..., 'expectedRent':...} and replace the dropdown values with the backend enum (STUDIO, BHK1, BHK2, BHK3, PENTHOUSE, RETAIL, OFFICE), mirroring the working web form at web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/properties/[id]/page.tsx:595-611.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. UnitController.java:31 binds @RequestBody Unit (the JPA entity) and UnitService.createUnit just calls repository.save with no property resolution. Unit.java has property/sizeSqft/expectedRent/type — no propertyId/size/annualRent fields and no Jackson aliases; no spring.jackson config or ObjectMapper bean exists, so Spring Boot defaults drop the unknown keys silently. Mobile property_detail_screen.dart:446-454 sends {unitNumber, propertyId, type, size?, annualRent?} via unit_service.dart POST /v1/units; both Dio interceptors only add headers (no body rewrite). Result: invalid type values (APARTMENT default, VILLA, SHOP, WAREHOUSE, TOWNHOUSE — not in UnitType {STUDIO,BHK1,BHK2,BHK3,PENTHOUSE,RETAIL,OFFICE}) fail Jackson enum deserialization (400); valid ones (STUDIO/OFFICE/PENTHOUSE, which the auditor's evidence omitted from the dropdown list) still fail because property is null, violating the NOT NULL property_id JoinColumn → DataIntegrityViolationException → 500 via GlobalExceptionHandler's RuntimeException catch-all. Every submission fails and the user sees only the generic createUnitFailed snackbar. Severity corrected from critical to high: the mobile create-unit flow is completely broken, but there is no data corruption or security/tenant-isolation impact, and workarounds exist (web frontend, CSV bulk upload endpoint which does resolve propertyId).

findings.title: Mobile manager 'Add Contact' always fails: required 'category' never sent, nonexistent 'role' field sent instead
findings.evidence: Backend PropertyContactDTO.java:12-22 requires `@NotNull ContactCategory category`, `@NotBlank String name`, `@NotBlank String phone`. Mobile property_detail_screen.dart:560-569 submits {'name':..., 'role':... (optional), 'phone':... (only if non-empty), 'email':...} via property_contact_service.dart:12-15. 'category' is never sent (null -> @NotNull fails -> guaranteed 400 from GlobalExceptionHandler.java:59-69), 'role' is not a DTO field (ignored), and 'phone' has no client-side validator so it can also be omitted despite @NotBlank. The contact list rendering at property_detail_screen.dart:1053-1055 reads contact['role'], which never exists in the PropertyContact response (it serializes category/customLabel), so that line never renders either.
findings.recommendation: Add a category picker using the ContactCategory enum values (PLUMBER, ELECTRICIAN, HANDYMAN, SECURITY, HOSPITAL_CLINIC, PHARMACY, BUILDING_MAINTENANCE, CIVIL_DEFENSE, OTHER), make phone required in the form, map the free-text 'role' to category=OTHER + customLabel, and render category/customLabel instead of 'role'.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Mobile manager's Add Contact sheet (property_detail_screen.dart:561-569) posts {'name', optional 'role'/'phone'/'email'} and never sends 'category'. Backend PropertyContactController.createContact binds @Valid PropertyContactDTO whose 'category' is @NotNull (PropertyContactDTO.java:12-13), so every request fails MethodArgumentNotValidException -> guaranteed 400 from GlobalExceptionHandler.handleValidation; the screen then shows the generic addContactFailed snackbar. No rescue exists: Dio interceptors (AuthInterceptor/TenantInterceptor in rentaxis_core) only set headers, and there is no Jackson alias or custom config mapping 'role' to 'category' (Spring Boot default silently drops the unknown 'role' key). Secondary claims also verified: 'phone' is @NotBlank server-side but optional in the mobile form, and the list rendering at property_detail_screen.dart:1053-1055 reads contact['role'], which never exists in the PropertyContact response (entity serializes category/customLabel), so that subtitle never renders. The web frontend correctly sends 'category' and works, confirming the contract. Severity correction: feature is fully dead on mobile manager but fails gracefully with no data loss, corruption, or security/tenant impact, and a complete workaround exists on web for this ancillary feature — medium, not critical.

findings.title: Web property import always shows 'Import failed' — backend serializes errors:[] which is truthy in JS
findings.evidence: BulkPropertyImportResultDTO.java:15 initializes `private List<String> errors = new ArrayList<>()`, so a successful import (PropertyController.java:74-77 returns 200) still serializes `"errors": []`. Web properties/page.tsx:891 uses `importResult.errors || importResult.error || ...` to choose the red error style and line 895 `importResult.errors ? ("Import failed:" ...)` to choose the message — an empty array is truthy in JS, so every import, including successful ones, renders a red 'Import failed:' banner with zero bullet items. Also, when the backend rejects an invalid type/emirate via GlobalExceptionHandler (body {error: true, message: ...}), line 905 renders `{importResult.error}` — a boolean, which React renders as nothing — so the actual message in `importResult.message` is never shown.
findings.recommendation: Gate on `importResult.errors?.length > 0` instead of truthiness, and render `importResult.message` (not the boolean `error` flag) for global-handler error bodies.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend: BulkPropertyImportResultDTO.java:15 initializes errors to an empty ArrayList, has no @JsonInclude, and there is no global Jackson inclusion config (no spring.jackson.default-property-inclusion in resources; the ObjectMapper bean in ClockConfig sets no inclusion), so a successful import (PropertyController returns 200 at lines 74-77; the service only setErrors when non-empty) serializes "errors": []. The Next.js /api/proxy rewrite is a pass-through and handleImportSubmit stores res.json() raw. Frontend: page.tsx:891 uses `importResult.errors || importResult.error || ...` for the red style and :895 `importResult.errors ?` for the message — an empty array is truthy, so every successful import renders a red "Import failed:" banner with zero bullet items; the "Import successful!" branch is unreachable for the real success payload. Secondary claim also holds: GlobalExceptionHandler bodies are {error: true, message: ...}, and page.tsx:905 renders the boolean `error` (React renders booleans as nothing), so the actual message is never shown. Severity corrected to medium: the import itself succeeds and the property list refreshes, so this is a misleading-feedback UI defect (with some risk of users retrying and creating duplicate properties), not data corruption, data loss, or a security issue — "high" overstates it.

findings.title: Web unit dropdown in CreateMeetingModal calls GET /v1/units?propertyId=... but backend ignores the param and returns ALL tenant units
findings.evidence: Backend UnitController.java:35-39 `@GetMapping public ResponseEntity<List<Unit>> getAllUnits()` declares no query parameters and returns every unit in the tenant. CreateMeetingModal.tsx:199 calls `fetch(`/api/proxy/v1/units?propertyId=${propertyId}`)` expecting a property-filtered list and puts the result straight into the unit picker (line 203). The propertyId query string is silently ignored, so the property-visit unit dropdown lists units belonging to every property, letting users book a visit against a unit of a different property. A correct filtered endpoint exists: UnitController.java:41-45 GET /api/v1/units/property/{propertyId}.
findings.recommendation: Change the call to `/api/proxy/v1/units/property/${propertyId}` (as done in properties/[id]/page.tsx:108 and finance/transactions/page.tsx:196).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. CreateMeetingModal.tsx:199 fetches /api/proxy/v1/units?propertyId=... ; the Next.js rewrite (/api/proxy/:path* -> ${backendUrl}/api/:path*) and proxy.ts middleware pass the query string through untouched (middleware only adds auth headers). UnitController.getAllUnits() (lines 35-39) declares no query parameter, so Spring silently ignores propertyId and returns UnitService.getAllUnits() -> repository.findAll(), which is tenant-scoped via TenantAspect/BaseTenantEntity but NOT property-scoped — the dropdown lists every unit in the tenant. The correct endpoint GET /api/v1/units/property/{propertyId} exists (lines 41-45) and is unused here. The downstream effect also holds: MeetingService (lines 104-106) loads the submitted unitId without validating it belongs to the meeting's propertyId, so a cross-property booking is persisted. Severity correction: the endpoint requires SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN/PROPERTY_MANAGER, so renters get a 403 and an empty (not mis-populated) dropdown; the leak is confined to one tenant's own data, the unit field is optional, and the impact is a confusing picker plus possible mismatched unit-property meeting records — a functional/data-consistency bug, not a security or tenant-isolation issue. 'high' overstates it; 'medium' is appropriate.

findings.title: Web 'Add Project' and 'Import Property' forms offer INDUSTRIAL, not a valid PropertyType — selection guarantees request failure, silently swallowed
findings.evidence: PropertyType.java defines only COMMERCIAL, RESIDENTIAL, MIXED. Web properties/page.tsx:538 (create form) and :939 (import form) both render `["RESIDENTIAL", "COMMERCIAL", "MIXED", "INDUSTRIAL"]` options. Selecting Industrial on create makes Jackson fail to deserialize CreatePropertyDTO.type (HttpMessageNotReadableException -> GlobalExceptionHandler.java:133 RuntimeException handler -> 500); handleProjectSubmit (page.tsx:154-178) has no !res.ok branch, so the modal just stays open with no feedback. On import, PropertyService.java:207 `PropertyType.valueOf(type.toUpperCase())` throws IllegalArgumentException -> 400 whose message is then lost by the boolean-error rendering bug.
findings.recommendation: Remove INDUSTRIAL from both selects (or add it to the PropertyType enum + a Liquibase-safe migration), and surface non-OK responses in handleProjectSubmit/handleImportSubmit.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. PropertyType.java has only COMMERCIAL/RESIDENTIAL/MIXED; both web forms (properties/page.tsx:538 create, :939 import) offer INDUSTRIAL. Create: CreatePropertyDTO.type is the PropertyType enum, no Jackson enum leniency exists (application.yml has no jackson config; ClockConfig's ObjectMapper bean only adds JavaTimeModule), so "INDUSTRIAL" causes HttpMessageNotReadableException; GlobalExceptionHandler lacks a handler for it and the RuntimeException catch-all (line 133) returns 500. handleProjectSubmit (page.tsx:154-178) has no !res.ok branch — modal stays open with zero feedback. Import: PropertyService.java:207 PropertyType.valueOf("INDUSTRIAL") throws IllegalArgumentException outside the CSV try/catch → 400 with {error:true, message:"No enum constant..."}; the frontend result renderer (page.tsx:895-905) falls to the `importResult.error` branch and renders the boolean true, which React renders as nothing — the user sees an empty red box and the message is lost. The next.config.ts rewrite is a transparent pass-through; no interceptor rescues either path. Severity correction: only the one invalid dropdown option fails, all valid types work, no data corruption or security impact, trivial workaround — a guaranteed silent-failure UX bug, medium rather than high.

findings.title: Web dashboard 'Add Property' (unit) modal offers BHK4, SHOP, WAREHOUSE — invalid UnitType values that guarantee failure, silently swallowed
findings.evidence: UnitType.java defines STUDIO, BHK1, BHK2, BHK3, PENTHOUSE, RETAIL, OFFICE. Web properties/page.tsx:604 renders options `["STUDIO", "BHK1", "BHK2", "BHK3", "BHK4", "PENTHOUSE", "SHOP", "OFFICE", "WAREHOUSE"]` for the POST /api/proxy/v1/units call at lines 183-196. BHK4, SHOP and WAREHOUSE cannot be deserialized into Unit.type, so those submissions always fail (RuntimeException catch-all -> 500) and handlePropertySubmit (lines 180-214) has no error branch — nothing happens visibly. The sibling form on the property detail page uses the correct list (properties/[id]/page.tsx:595 `const unitTypes = ["STUDIO", "BHK1", "BHK2", "BHK3", "PENTHOUSE", "RETAIL", "OFFICE"]`), so the two web forms disagree about the same endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the valid list from properties/[id]/page.tsx:595 (including RETAIL, which this form is missing) and add an error branch to handlePropertySubmit.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. UnitType.java defines only STUDIO/BHK1/BHK2/BHK3/PENTHOUSE/RETAIL/OFFICE, while the dashboard Add Property modal (properties/page.tsx:604) offers BHK4, SHOP, WAREHOUSE (and omits RETAIL). The value is POSTed unmodified via the next.config.ts rewrite (/api/proxy/:path* -> /api/:path*) to UnitController.createUnit(@RequestBody Unit), where Unit.type is the UnitType enum with no custom deserializer or lenient Jackson config anywhere in the backend — so those three values always fail deserialization. handlePropertySubmit (lines 180-214) only acts on res.ok and fetch never throws on non-2xx, so the failure is fully silent (modal stays open, no message, nothing created). Minor correction to the evidence: the failure is an HttpMessageNotReadableException -> HTTP 400, not a RuntimeException-500 (GlobalExceptionHandler has no handler for it); outcome is identical. Severity downgraded from high to medium: it silently breaks a third of the dropdown in a core flow and blocks RETAIL creation from this modal, but the sibling form on properties/[id]/page.tsx:595 uses the correct type list and provides a complete workaround, and there is no data-integrity, tenant-isolation, or security impact.

findings.title: Web 'Fixed Expenses' field on Add Project is silently discarded — CreatePropertyDTO has no fixedExpenses and no update endpoint exists
findings.evidence: Web properties/page.tsx:561 collects a 'Fixed Expenses' number into projectFormData (line 91) and POSTs the whole object at lines 157-161. CreatePropertyDTO.java:10-22 has no fixedExpenses field and PropertyController.java:31-39 maps only nameEn/nameAr/type/emirate/address/makaniNumber, so Jackson drops the value (Spring Boot ignores unknown JSON properties by default). Property.java:40-41 does have a fixed_expenses column, and the properties list renders `s.property.fixedExpenses` at page.tsx:1214-1217 — but since PropertyController exposes no PUT/PATCH either, no frontend path can ever set it; the form field is dead and the card value is always 0.
findings.recommendation: Add fixedExpenses to CreatePropertyDTO and map it in the controller (or remove the input from the form until a property-update endpoint exists).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Web properties/page.tsx collects fixedExpenses into projectFormData (line 91, input at 561) and POSTs the raw object via plain fetch to /api/proxy/v1/properties (157-161); the proxy is a transparent next.config.ts rewrite that cannot alter the body, and no client wrapper transforms it. CreatePropertyDTO has no fixedExpenses field, PropertyController.createProperty maps only nameEn/nameAr/type/emirate/address/makaniNumber, and no fail-on-unknown-properties Jackson override exists, so Spring Boot silently drops the value. PropertyController/PropertyService have no PUT/PATCH/updateProperty at all, and the only setFixedExpenses call in the backend is a test sentinel — no production path ever sets the column, which defaults to ZERO. The card display at page.tsx:1214 is gated on > 0 so it never renders. Severity downgraded to medium: it is silent loss of a single optional, display-only field with no financial-calculation, security, or tenant-isolation impact.

findings.title: CreateMeetingModal PM dropdown reads fullName/firstName/lastName which do not exist on the User response — labels render as '(email)'
findings.evidence: Backend PropertyController.java:54-58 returns List<User>; User.java:35-36 exposes `private String name` (no fullName/firstName/lastName). CreateMeetingModal.tsx:216 maps `fullName: u.fullName ?? `${u.firstName ?? ""} ${u.lastName ?? ""}`.trim()`, which always evaluates to the empty string, and line 571 renders `{u.fullName} ({u.email})` — so every PM option shows only the parenthesized email. The property detail page consumes the same endpoint correctly with m.name/m.email/m.phoneNumber (properties/[id]/page.tsx:283-289).
findings.recommendation: Map `fullName: u.name ?? u.fullName ?? ...` in fetchPmUsers to match the actual User serialization.

findings.title: CreateMeetingModal reads managerId/propertyManagerId from GET /v1/properties rows — fields do not exist, so host auto-derivation for property visits never works
findings.evidence: PropertyStatsDTO.java:11-18 serializes {property, propertyCount, revenueAtCapacity, actualRevenue, vacancies, assignedManagers} — there is no managerId or propertyManagerId. CreateMeetingModal.tsx:190 maps `managerId: p.managerId ?? p.propertyManagerId` (always undefined), so deriveHostUserId (lines 261-263) never finds a host from the property and needsPmPicker (lines 275-277) is always true for PROPERTY_VISIT, forcing the manual PM picker every time even though the response already carries assignedManagers.
findings.recommendation: Map `managerId: p.assignedManagers?.[0]?.id` (the field the DTO actually provides) so host auto-derivation works as designed.

findings.title: POST /api/v1/units/bulk returns 500 for malformed CSV content (bad enum/number) and web bulk upload swallows all failures silently
findings.evidence: UnitController.java:59-84 parses the CSV inside a try/catch where any UnitType.valueOf / UnitStatus.valueOf / BigDecimal parse failure hits `catch (Exception e) { return ResponseEntity.internalServerError().build(); }` — a bodyless 500 for what is client input error (contrast with POST /api/v1/properties/import, which returns a 400 with row-level errors). Web handleBulkUpload (properties/[id]/page.tsx:627-650) only acts on res.ok (line 642) with no else branch, so a user uploading a CSV with e.g. type 'BHK4' gets no feedback at all — the form just stays open.
findings.recommendation: Return 400 with row-level error messages from the controller (mirroring importPropertyWithUnits validation), and surface non-OK responses in handleBulkUpload.

findings.title: Web create/edit forms for properties, units, buildings and contacts silently ignore non-OK responses, discarding the backend's structured error message
findings.evidence: The backend returns actionable JSON on failure — e.g. PropertyService.java:62-83 translates the duplicate-name unique index into IllegalArgumentException, which GlobalExceptionHandler.java:71-78 maps to 400 {error:true, message: "A property named 'X' already exists..."}. But every consumer only checks res.ok with no else: properties/page.tsx:162-174 (handleProjectSubmit) and :197-210 (handlePropertySubmit), properties/[id]/page.tsx:163-168 (handleContactSubmit), :517-521 (building create), :617-621 (handleAddUnit), and properties/[id]/units/page.tsx:67-80. A TENANT_ADMIN creating a duplicate-named property sees nothing happen and the message the backend crafted for exactly this case is never shown; validation 400s and role-guard 403s are equally invisible.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared error helper (the codebase already introduced one for the listings pages per commit 2207d66) that parses {message} from non-OK responses and shows it near the submit button.

findings.title: Manager app penalties screen calls two nonexistent lease-scoped penalty endpoints — guaranteed 404 on every load
findings.controller: LeaseController path space (no such mappings exist; the real endpoint is PenaltyController at /api/v1/penalties)
findings.evidence: penalty_service.dart:29 `await _dio.get('/v1/leases/$leaseId/penalties')` and :41 `await _dio.post('/v1/leases/$leaseId/penalties/recalculate')`. No controller maps these paths: LeaseController/LeaseAttachmentController/LeaseInteractionController are the only classes on "/api/v1/leases" and define no penalties routes; PenaltyController.java:32 is `@RequestMapping("/api/v1/penalties")` with only GET (list, takes `leaseId` query param, line 43-46), POST /{id}/payments (line 79) and POST /{id}/waive (line 91) — `PenaltyService.recalculateForLease` (PenaltyService.java:188) is never exposed via any mapping. The screen is live: manager router.dart:127 routes path 'penalties', lease_detail_screen.dart:1127 pushes '/leases/{id}/penalties', and lease_penalties_screen.dart:76 calls `service.getPenalties(widget.leaseId)` on initState → Dio throws on 404 → the screen always shows the _error state (lines 82-88); :122-124 calls recalculatePenalties → always the failure snackbar. The web already fixed the same bug and left a comment: web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/leases/[id]/page.tsx:252-254 "there is no /leases/{id}/penalties route, the previous URL silently 404'd" and uses `/api/proxy/v1/penalties?leaseId=`.
findings.recommendation: In penalty_service.dart change getPenalties to GET /v1/penalties?leaseId={leaseId} (unwrap the Spring Page `content` array, as listPenalties at line 17-25 already does), and either remove the Recalculate action or add a backend mapping (e.g. POST /api/v1/penalties/recalculate?leaseId=) that calls PenaltyService.recalculateForLease.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. penalty_service.dart:29/:41 call GET /v1/leases/{id}/penalties and POST /v1/leases/{id}/penalties/recalculate on a Dio whose baseUrl ends in /api with default validateStatus (throws on 404) and only auth/tenant header interceptors — no path rewriting. Backend has exactly three controllers on /api/v1/leases (Lease, LeaseAttachment, LeaseInteraction); enumerating every mapping shows no penalties sub-route, and grep for "recalculate" across the api package is empty — PenaltyController is mounted at /api/v1/penalties with only GET list (leaseId query param), POST /{id}/payments, POST /{id}/waive. The screen is reachable (lease_detail_screen.dart:1127 pushes /leases/{id}/penalties; router.dart:127 builds LeasePenaltiesScreen) and calls getPenalties in initState, so every load throws → permanent error state; recalculate always shows the failure snackbar. Severity corrected from critical to high: the feature is 100% broken in the manager app, but it fails closed (error UI, no wrong data, no security/tenant-isolation or data-integrity impact), and the correct endpoint exists (the same service's listPenalties already uses /v1/penalties?leaseId=), making the fix trivial. Incidental related bug outside this claim: waivePenalty uses PUT but the controller maps POST /{id}/waive.

findings.title: Penalty waive called with PUT but backend maps POST — waiving from the lease detail screen always fails with 405
findings.endpoint: POST /api/v1/penalties/{id}/waive (called as PUT by both web and mobile)
findings.controller: PenaltyController (adjacent controller; call sites discovered while auditing the lease detail screens)
findings.evidence: Backend: PenaltyController.java:91 `@PostMapping("/{id}/waive")` (roles SUPER_ADMIN, TENANT_ADMIN; body WaivePenaltyRequestDTO with `reason`). Web lease detail page [id]/page.tsx:285-289 sends `fetch('/api/proxy/v1/penalties/${waiveModalPenalty.id}/waive', { method: "PUT", ... body: JSON.stringify({ reason: ... }) })` → Spring returns 405 Method Not Allowed; the handler only acts `if (res.ok)` so the waive modal silently does nothing. Mobile penalty_service.dart:34 `await _dio.put('/v1/penalties/$penaltyId/waive', ...)` is called from lease_penalties_screen.dart:193 — same guaranteed 405 (that screen is additionally broken by the 404 finding above).
findings.recommendation: Change both call sites to POST (or add @PutMapping alongside @PostMapping on the backend). Also surface the failure in the web modal instead of silently ignoring non-ok responses.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend PenaltyController.java:91 maps @PostMapping("/{id}/waive") (only mapping for this path anywhere in the backend). Web leases/[id]/page.tsx:285-289 sends method "PUT" through /api/proxy, which is a plain Next.js rewrite in next.config.ts (/api/proxy/:path* -> ${backendUrl}/api/:path*) that preserves the HTTP method — no route handler exists to translate it — so Spring returns 405; the handler only acts if res.ok with an empty catch, so the web waive modal fails silently. Mobile penalty_service.dart:34 uses _dio.put for the same path; the Dio interceptors (Auth/Tenant/Log) only add headers, so it also gets a 405 — Dio throws and lease_penalties_screen.dart shows a "Failed to waive penalty" snackbar. Severity corrected from critical to high: the waive feature is completely broken on both frontends (silent on web), but there is no data corruption, security, or tenant-isolation impact, which is what this project reserves critical/P0 for.

findings.title: GET lease documents/download excludes PROPERTY_MANAGER — the manager app's lease detail screen fails entirely for PM users
findings.evidence: LeaseController.java:201 getDocuments and :207 downloadDocument are `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN', 'RENTER')")` — PROPERTY_MANAGER is missing, even though GET /{id} (line 77), settlement (128-166) and LeaseAttachmentController list/download (lines 34, 40) all include PROPERTY_MANAGER. The manager app is used by PROPERTY_MANAGER users (staff_detail_screen.dart:211 creates them, profile_screen.dart:651 renders the role, guard_admin_service.dart:102 comments on PM 403s) and lease_detail_screen.dart:112-117 loads the screen with `Future.wait([getLeaseById, getPayments, getLeaseDocuments, getAttachments])` — the 403 on getLeaseDocuments rejects the whole Future.wait, so the catch at lines 129-135 sets `_error = failedToLoad` and a PM can never open ANY lease detail screen. On web, PMs get a silent no-op: dashboard/leases/page.tsx:341-345 and [id]/page.tsx:515-529 fetch documents/download inside `if (res.ok)` with no else branch.
findings.recommendation: Add 'PROPERTY_MANAGER' to the @PreAuthorize lists of getDocuments and downloadDocument (consistent with the lease read and attachment endpoints), or stop fetching documents for PM sessions in the manager app. Also make lease_detail_screen load documents outside the all-or-nothing Future.wait.

verdict.explanation: Verified end-to-end. LeaseController.java:200-207: getDocuments and downloadDocument use hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN','RENTER') — PROPERTY_MANAGER is missing, while GET /{id} (77), settlement (129-157), events (177), bulk-attach (237), and all LeaseAttachmentController endpoints (34, 40 include PM+RENTER) allow PM, so it is an oversight not policy. No rescue exists: ApiSecurityFilter grants exactly one authority ROLE_<role> (line 84) and no RoleHierarchy bean is configured, so a PM request 403s. Mobile: lease_service.dart:51-54 is a bare Dio get with no catch, AuthInterceptor.onError just forwards, and lease_detail_screen.dart:112-117 wraps it in Future.wait — the 403 rejects the wait, the catch (129-135) sets _error, and build (507/517) replaces the whole screen with ErrorState. PMs demonstrably use the manager app (PM-specific branch at booking_approvals_screen.dart:129, PM staff creation) and no router gate blocks /leases/:id, so a PROPERTY_MANAGER cannot open ANY lease detail in the manager app. Web: both handleDownloadContract functions (leases/page.tsx ~341, [id]/page.tsx ~514) fetch inside if(res.ok) with no else — silent no-op for PM; the web detail page itself still loads since its fetch uses GET /{id}. Severity: 'critical' is overblown — no data loss, no security/tenant-isolation impact, TENANT_ADMIN unaffected, and PMs can still view leases on web. It is a role-scoped outage of a core mobile workflow: high, not critical.

findings.title: Manager app exposes TENANT_ADMIN-only lease actions (activate, extend, generate/preview contract) to PROPERTY_MANAGER with no role gating
findings.evidence: Backend restricts all four to SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN only: LeaseController.java:102 (activate), :169 (extend), :185 (generate-contract), :191 (preview). The manager app renders these actions unconditionally — lease_detail_screen.dart:148 `activateLease(widget.leaseId)` behind the Activate button (line 566), :437-439 extendLease from the extend dialog (menu item at 671/692), :289-290 previewContract and :340 generateContract behind the contract buttons — and the file contains zero role checks (grep for 'role' in lease_detail_screen.dart returns nothing). Mobile requests carry the real role via X-User-Role (auth_interceptor.dart:18), so a PROPERTY_MANAGER tapping any of these gets a guaranteed 403, surfaced only as a generic snackbar ('failedToActivate' at line 159, 'failedToExtend' at 450, etc.).
findings.recommendation: Either add PROPERTY_MANAGER to these @PreAuthorize lists if PMs are meant to perform them (the web wizard flow suggests they are TA-only by design), or hide/disable the buttons in the manager app when the stored role is PROPERTY_MANAGER, and map 403 to a permission-specific message.

verdict.explanation: Verified end-to-end. Backend LeaseController restricts all four actions to SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN via @PreAuthorize (lines 102, 169, 185, 191) while allowing PROPERTY_MANAGER on the read endpoints (GET /leases/{id}:77, settlement, events), so a PM can reach the lease detail screen. ApiSecurityFilter (lines 38, 84) maps X-User-Role to ROLE_<role>, so the 403 is real. The manager app's lease_detail_screen.dart renders Activate/Generate Contract gated only by lease status (546-575) and Extend only by status==ACTIVE (674-691), with zero role checks anywhere in the file, router, or shell; auth_provider stores any role at login and auth_interceptor forwards it. Errors surface as generic snackbars (e.g. failedToActivate at 159). The web app's lease detail page (leases/[id]/page.tsx:154-157) explicitly gates the same actions with a comment that it matches the backend "so PROPERTY_MANAGER doesn't see a button that 403s" — confirming the mobile screen diverged from intended behavior, and PROPERTY_MANAGER is a real creatable role (staff_screen defaults to it). However, severity 'high' is overblown: backend authorization is correctly enforced, so there is no privilege escalation or data impact — this is a client-side UX defect (dead-end buttons + misleading generic errors for one role in a core workflow), which merits medium.

findings.title: Web interactions panel has no response/error handling — spinner sticks forever on failure, silently empty on 403
findings.evidence: LeaseInteractionsPanel.tsx:27-33: `const res = await fetch(...); const body = await res.json(); setItems(body.content ?? []); setLoading(false);` — no res.ok check and no try/catch, invoked as `void load()` (line 35). A network error or a non-JSON error response (e.g. proxy 502 HTML makes res.json() throw) rejects the promise before `setLoading(false)`, leaving the panel on the loading state permanently with an unhandled rejection; a 403/500 JSON error body silently renders as 'no interactions'. The backend returns Page<InteractionDTO>, so the happy-path `body.content` unwrap and the `?size=50&sort=occurredAt,desc` Pageable params are otherwise correct.
findings.recommendation: Wrap load() in try/catch/finally, check res.ok, and render an error state distinct from the empty state.

findings.title: Settlement fetch conflates every failure with 'no settlement yet' and silently swaps in the blank preview flow
findings.evidence: Backend getSettlement (LeaseController.java:134-142) returns 404 only for NotFoundException; other failures are 5xx/403. But web settlement/page.tsx:254-307 falls through to the preview branch on ANY non-ok or thrown error, and lease_settlement_screen.dart:205-237 does the same with a bare `catch (_) { // No settlement yet — load preview }`. On a transient 500/403 while a DRAFT settlement exists, the user is shown a fresh preview-based editor (deductions with `id: null`, notes lost); pressing Save Draft then POSTs deductions without ids to /settlement/draft, where SaveSettlementDTO treats id-less rows as new deductions (SaveSettlementDTO.java:23 comment: 'if set, updates existing') — duplicating or replacing the existing draft's rows without the user knowing.
findings.recommendation: Only fall back to the preview flow on an actual 404 (web: `res.status === 404`; mobile: check `DioException.response?.statusCode == 404`); surface every other failure as an error state.

findings.title: Mobile terminateLease sends notes as a query parameter the backend never reads — silently dropped (latent, currently uncalled)
findings.evidence: lease_service.dart:37-41 `await _dio.post('/v1/leases/$id/terminate', queryParameters: { if (notes != null) 'notes': notes })` — but the backend (LeaseController.java:117-126) reads `@RequestBody(required = false) TerminateWithSettlementDTO dto` (fields notes, deductions) and declares no @RequestParam, so query-string notes are ignored and settlement notes would be silently lost. The web's (dead) legacy caller correctly posts a JSON body `{ notes: ... }` (dashboard/leases/page.tsx:297-301), confirming the body is the intended transport. No mobile screen currently calls terminateLease (termination goes through the settlement screen's finalize), so this is a landmine for future callers rather than a live bug.
findings.recommendation: Change terminateLease to send `data: {'notes': notes}` as the request body, or delete the method since the endpoint is otherwise unused.

findings.title: Web sorts lease documents by a createdAt field that does not exist in LeaseDocumentDTO — 'newest first' logic is a silent no-op
findings.evidence: [id]/page.tsx:523-527 sorts docs with `new Date(a.createdAt || 0).getTime()` claiming to pick 'the most recently created CONTRACT document', but LeaseDocumentDTO.java:9-14 exposes only id, leaseId, documentUrl, type — createdAt is always undefined, so every sort key is epoch 0 and the order is whatever the unordered repository query returns (LeaseDocumentRepository.findByLeaseId has no ORDER BY). Harmless today because regeneration deletes all prior documents (ContractGenerationService.java:136-141), but the stated defensive guarantee does not exist. The renter portal (renter-portal/page.tsx:204) and leases list (page.tsx:345) just take docs[0] with the same implicit assumption.
findings.recommendation: Add createdAt to LeaseDocumentDTO (entity almost certainly has it) or drop the misleading sort and rely on the type filter alone.

findings.title: CreateMeetingModal reads nonexistent propertyManagerId from the lease list response — lease-derived meeting host never works
findings.evidence: CreateMeetingModal.tsx:168 maps `propertyManagerId: l.propertyManagerId` from the /v1/leases (or my-leases) response and uses it at :259 (`return lease?.propertyManagerId || selectedPmId || defaultHostId`) and :273 (`return !lease?.propertyManagerId` to decide whether the PM picker is needed). LeaseDTO.java:13-38 has no propertyManagerId field, so the value is always undefined: for OFFICE_VISIT meetings the host can never be derived from the lease, needsPmPicker() is always true for staff, and renters always fall through to the default-host endpoint. Degrades gracefully (extra picker step / default host) but the code path is dead.
findings.recommendation: Either add propertyManagerId to LeaseDTO (resolvable from the lease's property manager) or remove the dead derivation and always show the picker/default host.

findings.title: Public renewal-intent endpoint is unreachable for logged-out renters: web routes it through the auth-gated /api/proxy middleware
findings.evidence: Backend deliberately makes this endpoint anonymous: SecurityConfig.java:36 permits "/api/v1/public/**" (permitAll) and ApiSecurityFilter.java:31 skips it; PublicRenewalController does a cross-tenant token lookup (findByIdAcrossTenants, line 42) precisely so no session is needed. The renewal reminder email (lease_renewal_reminder.html) links to '{portalBaseUrl}/{lang}/dashboard/renter-portal/renewal-intent?token=...&intent=...'. That page's component posts via the proxy: RenewalIntentConfirm.tsx:12 `fetch("/api/proxy/v1/public/renewal-intent", { method: "POST", ... })`. But web/src/proxy.ts:19-24 rejects EVERY /api/proxy request without a NextAuth session: `if (isApiProxy) { const token = await getToken({ req }); if (!token) { return ... new NextResponse('Unauthorized', { status: 401 }) } }` (matcher line 53 includes '/api/proxy/:path*').
