Additionally the page sits under the auth-gated dashboard layout (AuthenticatedLayout.tsx:25-27 pushes unauthenticated users to /auth/login, dropping the token/intent query). So a renter clicking the email CTA while not logged into the web portal — the primary use case for a signed-token public endpoint — gets a 401 from Next middleware (surfaced as the generic error state at RenewalIntentConfirm.tsx:18) and can never confirm.
findings.recommendation: Serve the confirm page outside the authenticated dashboard layout (e.g. a public /[locale]/renewal-intent route) and either exempt /api/proxy/v1/public/* from the session check in web/src/proxy.ts or add a dedicated rewrite (like the existing /api/marketplace/* and /public/l/* rewrites in next.config.ts) that forwards /api/v1/public/* to the backend without requiring a NextAuth token.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend: SecurityConfig permits /api/v1/public/** (permitAll) and ApiSecurityFilter skips /api/v1/public/ paths; PublicRenewalController verifies a signed token and uses findByIdAcrossTenants — deliberately sessionless. Email CTA links to /{lang}/dashboard/renter-portal/renewal-intent?token=...&intent=.... Two independent web-side gates break it for logged-out renters: (1) the page sits under dashboard/layout.tsx → AuthenticatedLayout, which router.push("/auth/login")s unauthenticated users with no callbackUrl, dropping token/intent; (2) even if reached, RenewalIntentConfirm.tsx posts to /api/proxy/v1/public/renewal-intent, and web/src/proxy.ts (middleware, matcher '/api/proxy/:path*') returns 401 when getToken() is null — middleware runs before the next.config.ts rewrite, so the request never reaches the backend. Refutation attempts failed: no app/api/proxy route handler, no alternate rewrite covering /api/v1/public, no other call site, no wrapper/interceptor. Severity 'high' stands: the signed-token flow's primary audience (renters without an active web session, incl. mobile-only renters with no workaround) cannot complete it at all; not critical since no security/data-loss impact.

findings.title: Post-confirm redirect targets a locale-less path that matches no Next.js route — user lands on 404 after successful intent capture
findings.evidence: PublicRenewalController.java:50-53 returns `new RenewalIntentResponse(updated.getIntent().name(), updated.getLease().getId(), "/dashboard/renter-portal/renewals")`, and RenewalIntentConfirm.tsx:22 navigates there on success: `window.location.href = body.redirectTo ?? "/dashboard/renter-portal/renewals"` (the fallback has the same defect). Every web page lives under app/[locale]/ (web/src/app contains only [locale], api, l) with next-intl defineRouting using the default localePrefix 'always' (i18n/routing.ts has no localePrefix override), so the real route is /en/dashboard/renter-portal/renewals or /ar/.... The middleware matcher in proxy.ts:53 is ['/', '/(ar|en)/:path*', '/api/proxy/:path*'], so the unprefixed /dashboard/renter-portal/renewals never reaches the intl middleware to be redirected, and no app route matches it ([locale] would consume the 'dashboard' segment) — the browser gets Next's 404 page 1.2s after the success message. The email link itself correctly includes the locale ('${portalBaseUrl} + '/' + ${#locale.language} + '/dashboard/...' in lease_renewal_reminder.html), confirming the prefix is required. RenewalIntentConfirm.test.tsx:72 asserts the redirect equals the unprefixed path, so tests encode the bug.
findings.recommendation: Make the redirect locale-aware on the client: ignore or localize the backend-provided path (e.g. use next-intl's router/redirect from @/i18n/routing with the current locale) instead of assigning window.location.href to the raw backend value; alternatively stop sending a web-specific path from the backend DTO altogether.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end from real code. (1) Backend: PublicRenewalController.java:50-53 returns RenewalIntentResponse with redirectTo="/dashboard/renter-portal/renewals" (DTO record confirmed: `record RenewalIntentResponse(String intent, UUID leaseId, String redirectTo)`). (2) Frontend: RenewalIntentConfirm.tsx:22 does `window.location.href = body.redirectTo ?? "/dashboard/renter-portal/renewals"` after 1.2s — both branches unprefixed. (3) Routing: web/src/app contains only [locale]/, api/, l/ (l/ is [tenantSlug] short links, unrelated); the real page is app/[locale]/dashboard/renter-portal/renewals. i18n/routing.ts uses defineRouting with no localePrefix override → default 'always'. (4) No rescue: proxy.ts matcher ['/', '/(ar|en)/:path*', '/api/proxy/:path*'] excludes unprefixed /dashboard/*, so the intl middleware never runs to add the locale prefix; next.config.ts has no redirects() and its rewrites cover only /api/proxy, assets, marketplace, /public/l; no basePath; no root not-found redirect. The unprefixed path matches [locale]='dashboard', and [locale]/layout.tsx:24-25 calls notFound() for invalid locales (and no [locale]/renter-portal route exists anyway) → Next 404. (5) Supporting evidence checks out: RenewalIntentConfirm.test.tsx:72 asserts capturedHref equals the unprefixed path (test encodes the bug), and both lease_renewal_reminder templates build links as portalBaseUrl + '/' + locale.language + '/dashboard/...', confirming the prefix is required. Severity corrected to medium: the intent capture itself succeeds and persists before the redirect, so there is no data loss or failed business operation — the defect is a post-success navigation to a 404, recoverable by manual navigation, though it hits every user of the email renewal flow and may cause confusion/retries (retry yields 409 ALREADY_RESOLVED shown as a generic error). That is a user-visible UX defect in a primary flow, not a high-severity functional/security failure.

findings.title: Renter setIntent POST ignores response status — 400 'already resolved' and 404 fail silently, UI just reloads
findings.evidence: renewals/page.tsx:29-36: `const setIntent = async (opportunityId, intent) => { await fetch(`/api/proxy/v1/me/renewals/${opportunityId}/intent`, { method: "POST", ... body: JSON.stringify({ intent }) }); await load(); }` — the response is never inspected (no res.ok check, no user feedback). The backend really does fail on realistic inputs: RenewalIntentService.captureIntentFromRenter (lines 52-54) throws BusinessRuleViolationException("Renewal is already resolved") when the manager has closed the opportunity (stage CLOSED_WON/CLOSED_LOST), which GlobalExceptionHandler.java:41-48 maps to 400; a stale opportunityId or another renter's opportunity yields NotFoundException → 404 (handler lines 32-39). In all these cases the page silently reloads showing the unchanged intent with zero indication the click did nothing. (Method, path, and the {"intent": "RENEW"|"MOVE_OUT"|"DISCUSS"} body sent by RenewalCard.tsx:33-42 all match the backend contract — only error handling is missing.)
findings.recommendation: Check res.ok in setIntent and surface a toast/message for the 400 already-resolved and 404 cases (the backend returns {error, message, status} JSON), then reload; optionally use the returned {intent, stage} to update state instead of a blind refetch.

findings.title: Mobile renter app dead-ends the in-app renewal reminder: 'Tap to choose your renewal option' but the app never calls any /v1/me/renewals endpoint
findings.evidence: For the non-EMAIL reminder channel, RenewalReminderService.java:132-138 sends an in-app notification to the renter: notifyInAppInNewTx(..., "LEASE_RENEWAL_REMINDER", "Your lease ends in " + slot + " days", "Lease ends ... Tap to choose your renewal option.", "LEASE", leaseId). But grep across mobile/apps/renter, mobile/apps/manager, mobile/apps/security, and mobile/packages/rentaxis_core returns zero call sites for 'me/renewals', 'renewal-intent', or 'renewals/follow-ups' (0 matches for me/renewals in all .dart files), and the renter app's notification handling only maps type 'LEASE' to an icon (notifications_screen.dart:263-266) with no navigation to any renewal/intent screen — no such screen exists. A renter who only uses the mobile app is prompted to act but has no way to set intent (RenterRenewalController POST .../intent is web-only), so the opportunity stays OPEN unless they switch to the web portal.
findings.recommendation: Add a renewal summary/intent screen to the renter Flutter app backed by GET /api/v1/me/renewals and POST /api/v1/me/renewals/{opportunityId}/intent (a rentaxis_core service), and deep-link the LEASE_RENEWAL_REMINDER notification to it; until then, change the in-app copy so it doesn't instruct an impossible tap action.

findings.title: Renter renewals page renders empty buckets on any fetch failure — errors indistinguishable from 'no renewals'
findings.evidence: renewals/page.tsx:23-25: `const res = await fetch("/api/proxy/v1/me/renewals"); if (!res.ok) { setData({ leases: [] }); return; }` — any 401 (expired session at the proxy, proxy.ts:23), 403 (non-RENTER role hitting the @PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ROLE_RENTER')") guard at RenterRenewalController.java:52), 404 (user with no Renter record, controller line 56-57), or 500 is rendered as four 'emptyBucket' sections — exactly what a renter with no upcoming renewals sees. A renter whose lease genuinely ends in 20 days would see nothing actionable during a transient backend error with no retry or error message. Response-shape handling is otherwise correct: the page reads {leases:[...]} matching RenewalSummaryDTO and all LeaseRenewalView field names match.
findings.recommendation: Track an error state separately from empty data (e.g. setError on !res.ok) and render a retry affordance instead of the empty-bucket copy.

findings.title: 409 ALREADY_RESOLVED from public renewal-intent is collapsed into the generic error message
findings.evidence: The backend distinguishes four failure modes: 410 {error:TOKEN_EXPIRED} (PublicRenewalController.java:37), 400 {error:TOKEN_INVALID} (line 39), 404 {error:NOT_FOUND} (line 44), and 409 {error:ALREADY_RESOLVED} (line 55, thrown when the opportunity is CLOSED_WON/CLOSED_LOST). RenewalIntentConfirm.tsx:17-18 only special-cases 410 (`if (res.status === 410) setStatus("expired"); else if (!res.ok) setStatus("error")`), so a renter clicking an old email link after the renewal was finalized sees the generic 'genericError' text implying something went wrong, when the accurate message is 'this renewal has already been handled'. The response body's error code is never read.
findings.recommendation: Handle res.status === 409 (or read body.error === 'ALREADY_RESOLVED') with a dedicated 'already handled' message and hide the confirm button, mirroring the existing 410 branch.

findings.title: FollowUpsWidget silently shows the empty state on non-OK responses
findings.evidence: FollowUpsWidget.tsx:20-21: `const res = await fetch("/api/proxy/v1/renewals/follow-ups"); if (!res.ok) return;` — a 403 (endpoint guard is @PreAuthorize("hasAnyAuthority('ROLE_TENANT_ADMIN','ROLE_PROPERTY_MANAGER')") at PendingFollowUpsController.java:25, while the widget is mounted unconditionally on the shared dashboard at dashboard/page.tsx:364, which SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_USER sessions can also load) or any 5xx renders the t("empty") state, hiding overdue follow-ups from a PM during transient failures. Contract usage is otherwise correct: GET with no params (optional ?date defaults to today at controller line 27), top-level JSON array handled via Array.isArray (line 23), and the fields read (id, leaseId, summary, followUpDate) all exist on InteractionDTO; followUpDate is guaranteed non-null by the repository query (LeaseInteractionRepository.java:26 'i.followUpDate IS NOT NULL').
findings.recommendation: Distinguish error from empty (at minimum skip rendering the widget or show a muted 'couldn't load' line on !res.ok instead of the empty message).

findings.title: Web types declare unitNumber/propertyNameEn as non-nullable strings though the backend can return null
findings.evidence: RenterRenewalController.java:85-88 builds LeaseRenewalView with `l.getUnit() != null ? l.getUnit().getUnitNumber() : null` and `(l.getUnit() != null && l.getUnit().getProperty() != null) ? ...getNameEn() : null`, so both fields are nullable in the JSON. The web types declare them non-nullable: renewals/page.tsx:8-9 (`unitNumber: string; propertyNameEn: string;`) and RenewalCard.tsx:6-7 Props. RenewalCard.tsx:29 renders `{p.propertyNameEn} · {p.unitNumber}` — React tolerates null (renders a bare ' · '), so today this is a type-safety/consistency issue rather than a crash, but any future .toUpperCase()/format call on these fields would throw at runtime while the compiler stays silent.
findings.recommendation: Change the TypeScript types to `string | null` to match RenewalSummaryDTO.LeaseRenewalView and add a fallback label when both are null.

findings.title: Web aging report reads buckets as a keyed object with 'items', but backend returns an array with 'details' — bucket breakdown never renders
findings.evidence: Backend AgingReportDTO declares 'private List<AgingBucket> buckets' where AgingBucket has fields label/amount/count/details (AgingReportDTO.java:12-31), and PaymentScheduleService.getAgingReport builds it as an ordered list with labels {"Current", "1-30 Days", ...} (PaymentScheduleService.java:1039-1046), so the JSON is buckets: [{label, amount, count, details:[...]}, ...]. The web reports page instead types it as an object: 'buckets: { current: AgingBucket; days1to30: AgingBucket; ... }' with 'items: AgingItem[]' (reports/page.tsx:64-80) and indexes it with string keys: 'const bucket = agingData.buckets?.[cfg.key as keyof typeof agingData.buckets]' where cfg.key is "current"/"days1to30"/... (reports/page.tsx:561 and 575), then reads 'bucket.items' (line 576/601). Indexing a JSON array with "current" is always undefined, so every bucket card hits 'if (!bucket) return null' (line 562) and every detail table hits 'if (!bucket?.items ...) return null' (line 576). Only totalOutstanding (line 555) ever renders; the entire bucket summary and per-renter detail tables are guaranteed never to appear on the Finance > Reports > Aging tab.
findings.recommendation: Fix the web page to consume the actual shape: map over agingData.buckets (array) by index or by matching bucket.label, and rename items -> details (and AgingItem's fields already match AgingDetail: renterName, propertyName, unitNumber, amount, daysOverdue, dueDate). Alternatively change AgingReportDTO to a keyed map, but the array fix on the frontend is non-breaking.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend GET /api/v1/payments/aging-report (PaymentScheduleController.java:153-157) returns AgingReportDTO whose buckets field is List<AgingBucket> (AgingReportDTO.java:11), each bucket having label/amount/count/details; PaymentScheduleService.getAgingReport (lines 1039-1082) builds an ordered 5-element list, so the JSON is buckets: [{label, amount, count, details:[...]}]. The Next.js proxy (next.config.ts:25-26) is a verbatim rewrite with no body transformation, and no route handler intercepts /api/proxy. The web page (reports/page.tsx:181-182) stores res.json() untransformed, then indexes agingData.buckets?.["current"/"days1to30"/...] at lines 561/575 — string-indexing a JSON array yields undefined, so every bucket card hits the null-return at line 562 and every detail table hits line 576 (which also reads the nonexistent 'items' field instead of 'details'). Only totalOutstanding (line 555) renders; the bucket summary and per-renter detail tables can never appear regardless of data. No wrapper, interceptor, or serializer rescues it. Severity corrected from critical to high: the aging breakdown is completely non-functional and silently missing (user-facing finance reporting), but there is no data corruption, security/tenant-isolation impact, or crash.

findings.title: Manager app status strip reads nonexistent summary fields depositedAmount and bouncedAmount — always displays AED 0
findings.evidence: PaymentSummaryDTO's only amount fields are totalAmount, pendingAmount, collectedAmount, clearedAmount, overdueAmount (PaymentSummaryDTO.java:9-21); the service populates exactly those setters (PaymentScheduleService.java:450-461) — there is no depositedAmount or bouncedAmount in the response. The manager payments screen's _StatusStrip reads "((summary['depositedAmount'] ?? 0) as num).toDouble()" (payments_screen.dart:769) for the Deposited tile and "((summary['bouncedAmount'] ?? 0) as num).toDouble()" (payments_screen.dart:787) for the Bounced tile. Both lookups are always null, so the '?? 0' fallback makes those two tiles permanently show a 0 amount even when the counts beside them (depositedCount/bouncedCount, which DO exist) are non-zero. The web page reads only fields that exist (finance/payments/page.tsx:353-356), confirming mobile is the outlier.
findings.recommendation: Either add depositedAmount and bouncedAmount to PaymentSummaryDTO and populate them in PaymentScheduleService.getSummary (counts are already tracked, so the amounts are cheap to accumulate), or drop the amount line from those two tiles in the mobile status strip. Adding the DTO fields is the better fix since the UI clearly intends to show them.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. PaymentSummaryDTO.java (lines 8-21) has no depositedAmount/bouncedAmount fields, and PaymentScheduleService.getSummary never computes them (DEPOSITED and BOUNCED switch arms increment only counts; the setter block populates exactly totalAmount/pendingAmount/collectedAmount/clearedAmount/overdueAmount). The controller returns the DTO directly, and the mobile PaymentService.getSummary (rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/payment_service.dart:49-55) returns response.data raw — the shared Dio client's only interceptors are Auth/Tenant/Log, none of which transform bodies. So payments_screen.dart:769 and :787 read keys that are always null, and the '?? 0' fallback makes the Deposited and Bounced tiles in _StatusStrip permanently render a 0 amount (via Formatters.currencyCompact) even when their counts are non-zero. Severity downgraded from high to medium: it is a display-only bug on two tiles of one mobile screen — counts are correct, no crash, no data/tenant impact, web unaffected — though the zero amounts are genuinely misleading for a rent-collection workflow and the proper fix needs new backend aggregation fields.

findings.title: Manager app fetches the tenant-wide payments list as a single 500-row page and filters client-side — data silently truncated beyond 500 schedules
findings.evidence: Backend GET /api/v1/payments is a Spring Page endpoint with @PageableDefault(size = 25) and server-side filters propertyId/status/renterName/overdue (PaymentScheduleController.java:45-59), and a dedicated unpaginated per-lease endpoint GET /lease/{leaseId} exists (PaymentScheduleController.java:61-65). PaymentService.getPayments defaults to a single request with 'size': 500 and unwraps only data['content'], discarding totalElements/totalPages (payment_service.dart:32-47). Three manager screens rely on that one page being the whole tenant: (1) lease_detail_screen.dart:114+122-124 calls paymentService.getPayments() and filters '.where((p) => p['leaseId'] == widget.leaseId)' instead of calling /lease/{id} — installments of the viewed lease that fall outside the first 500 rows (sorted dueDate DESC) silently disappear from the schedule tab; (2) payments_screen.dart:28-33 loads getPayments() with no filters and does all property/status/overdue filtering plus its own show-more pagination client-side over those 500 rows (payments_screen.dart:157-238), so the Paid/Overdue/All tabs under-report; (3) cheque_scan_flow_screen.dart:71-88 fetches the full list just to find one payment by id. The web equivalents pass propertyId/status/renterName/page/size server-side (finance/payments/page.tsx:170-189) and use the lease-scoped endpoint, with a comment warning about exactly this truncation (PaymentScheduleEditor.tsx:104-108). A portfolio of ~42 leases x 12 cheques exceeds 500 rows.
findings.recommendation: In the manager app, use GET /v1/payments/lease/{leaseId} for the lease detail screen (add a wrapper to PaymentService), pass propertyId/status/overdue and real page/size to GET /v1/payments from the payments screen instead of client-side filtering, and fetch the single payment via the lease-scoped list in the scan flow. At minimum, surface totalElements so truncation is detectable.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend GET /api/v1/payments is a paginated Spring Page endpoint (PaymentScheduleController.java:45-59, @PageableDefault size=25, sort dueDate DESC) with server-side propertyId/status/renterName/overdue filters, and an unpaginated per-lease endpoint GET /lease/{leaseId} exists (lines 61-65). PaymentService.getPayments (payment_service.dart:32-47) makes exactly one request with size=500 and unwraps only data['content'], discarding totalElements/totalPages; no page loop, and the Dio client has only Auth/Tenant/Log interceptors — nothing auto-paginates. No Spring max-page-size cap is configured, so 500 is honored. All three manager call sites behave as claimed: lease_detail_screen.dart:114,122-124 filters the tenant-wide 500-row page by leaseId client-side instead of calling /lease/{id}; payments_screen.dart:28-33 loads unfiltered and does all property/status/overdue filtering plus show-more pagination client-side (lines 158-238); cheque_scan_flow_screen.dart:71-88 scans the full list for one id (explicitly best-effort). The web app corroborates: it uses /v1/payments/lease/{id} everywhere and PaymentScheduleEditor.tsx:104-107 has a comment warning about this exact truncation. Aggravating detail: dueDate DESC means overdue installments (oldest due dates) are truncated first, so the Overdue tab under-reports first. Trigger threshold (>500 schedule rows tenant-wide, e.g. ~42 leases x 12 cheques) is realistic for the target market. Severity 'high' is appropriate: silent financial data loss in the manager app with no error surfaced, though not critical (no corruption or tenant-isolation breach; web unaffected). Minor citation inaccuracies (web file paths) do not affect validity.

findings.title: Finance payments page inline collect/replace modal and deposit/clear handlers swallow error responses — silent failure on 400s
findings.evidence: These endpoints return 400 with {"message": ...} via GlobalExceptionHandler's BusinessRuleViolationException handler (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:41-47) for state-machine violations (e.g. depositing a non-COLLECTED cheque, clearing a non-DEPOSITED one). The finance payments page renders its own inline modal (page.tsx:681, not the shared CollectChequeDialog) whose submitCollect only does 'if (res.ok) { ...close+refresh }' with no else branch (page.tsx:247-256), submitReplace likewise (page.tsx:314-323), and handleDeposit/handleClear do 'if (res.ok) refreshData();' (page.tsx:266-271, 286-291). On a non-OK response the modal stays open (or nothing happens) with zero feedback. The lease detail page's handleDeposit/handleClear have the same silent 'if (res.ok) fetchPayments();' pattern (leases/[id]/page.tsx:543-548, 559-564). The shared CollectChequeDialog (CollectChequeDialog.tsx:81-88) and MarkChequeFailedDialog (MarkChequeFailedDialog.tsx:91-98) both parse data?.message || data?.error and display it — the correct pattern already exists in the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Replace the finance page's inline modal with the shared CollectChequeDialog (its stated purpose per its own doc comment), and add the message||error extraction + toast to handleDeposit/handleClear on both pages, matching MarkChequeFailedDialog's error handling.

findings.title: Manager payments screen never scopes GET /summary by the selected property, unlike web — stat tiles contradict the filtered list
findings.evidence: The backend accepts an optional propertyId on /summary (PaymentScheduleController.java:67-72) and the mobile wrapper supports it (payment_service.dart:49-55), but the manager screen's provider calls 'service.getSummary()' with no arguments (payments_screen.dart:22-26) and never invalidates on property selection — the property filter chip only affects the client-side list filter (payments_screen.dart:158-162). The web page refetches the summary with propertyId whenever the filter changes (finance/payments/page.tsx:163-165, 207-216). Result: after picking a property in the mobile filter, the top cells and status strip still show tenant-wide totals above a property-scoped list.
findings.recommendation: Convert _paymentSummaryProvider to a family keyed by the selected propertyId (mirroring the web behavior) so the tiles re-query GET /v1/payments/summary?propertyId=... when the filter changes, or visually label the tiles as portfolio-wide.

findings.title: Entire online-payment initiation flow (create-order / verify / cancel) is unreachable from every frontend despite full backend + webhook support
findings.evidence: OnlinePaymentController exposes create-order/verify/cancel for RENTER (OnlinePaymentController.java:29-46) and WebhookController + the ONLINE_PENDING status exist to support the flow, but no frontend calls them: grep of web/src finds only /v1/online-payments/my-payments (renter-portal/page.tsx:122, renter-portal/payments/page.tsx:104); in mobile, the rentaxis_core wrappers createOrder/verifyPayment/cancelPayment (payment_service.dart:13-29) have zero call sites in the renter, manager, or security apps. The renter payments screen explicitly says 'Cards are non-interactive — the renter app is informational; cheque submission is handled offline' (renter payments_screen.dart:34-36), yet web help articles still tell renters payments are processed through Razorpay (web/src/lib/helpArticles.ts:576, 639). Not a runtime bug, but the frontends and docs disagree about whether online payment exists, and web UIs still special-case ONLINE_PENDING rows that can no longer be produced.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether online payments are shipped: if deliberately deferred, update the renter help articles and consider removing the dead Dart wrappers; if it is a regression, re-wire a pay button in the renter surfaces to createOrder -> gateway SDK -> verify, with cancel on abandonment.

findings.title: Mobile admin transactions tab reads nonexistent debitAmount/creditAmount/transactionDate fields — amounts and dates never render
findings.evidence: Backend FinancialTransaction.java serializes `date` (line 25 `private LocalDate date;`), `debit` (line 42) and `credit` (line 45). finance_screen.dart lines 328-329 read `final debit = (tx['debitAmount'] ?? 0).toDouble(); final credit = (tx['creditAmount'] ?? 0).toDouble();` — both keys never exist, so debit=credit=0, `isDebit` is always false, neither amount Text renders (guarded by `if (debit > 0)` / `if (credit > 0)` at lines 411/420) and every row is labeled 'Credit' (line 430). Line 381 reads `tx['transactionDate'] ?? tx['createdAt']` — neither exists (BaseTenantEntity has no createdAt; only @JsonIgnore tenantId), so Formatters.date(null) renders '-' for every row.
findings.recommendation: Change finance_screen.dart to read tx['debit'], tx['credit'] and tx['date'] (the actual JSON keys produced by the entity).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end with no rescuing wrapper anywhere in the chain. (1) Backend: FinancialTransactionController.getTransactions (/Users/kunalsharma/datagami/rentaxis/backend/src/main/java/com/datagami/rentaxis/api/FinancialTransactionController.java:31-39) returns raw List<FinancialTransaction> entities; the entity (/Users/kunalsharma/datagami/rentaxis/backend/src/main/java/com/datagami/rentaxis/domain/entity/FinancialTransaction.java) serializes `date` (line 25), `debit` (line 42), `credit` (line 45) under Jackson default naming — no @JsonProperty renames, no PropertyNamingStrategy in application.yml, no mixin/ObjectMapper customization for this entity. BaseTenantEntity contributes only @JsonIgnore'd tenantId — there is no createdAt anywhere in the payload. (2) Transport: FinanceService.getTransactions (/Users/kunalsharma/datagami/rentaxis/mobile/packages/rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/finance_service.dart:12-26) hits /v1/finance/transactions and returns response.data untouched; the only Dio interceptors (auth_interceptor.dart, tenant_interceptor.dart) add headers / handle onError and never reshape response bodies. (3) UI: finance_screen.dart lines 328-330 read tx['debitAmount']/tx['creditAmount'] — keys that never exist — so debit=credit=0.0, the `if (debit > 0)` / `if (credit > 0)` guards at lines 411/420 are always false (no amount ever renders), isDebit is always false so every row shows the green down-arrow and 'Credit' label (line 430). Line 381 reads tx['transactionDate'] ?? tx['createdAt'] — both absent — and Formatters.date(null) returns '-' (formatters.dart:27). The screen is reachable at the /finance route in the manager app. However, 'critical' is overblown: this is a display-only defect on a read-only mobile admin tab — no data corruption, no incorrect write path, no security/tenant impact — and the same data renders correctly elsewhere (web dashboard). The tab is effectively useless (no amounts, no dates, wrong labels), which merits 'medium' (arguably 'high' if the mobile finance tab is a primary surface, but it is secondary to the web finance module).

findings.title: Mobile admin P&L reports read totalExpense/netIncome/incomeAccounts/expenseAccounts — expenses always show 0 and net income equals total income
findings.evidence: ReportDTO.java exposes `totalExpenses` (line 25), `netProfit` (line 34), and Map<String,BigDecimal> `incomeBreakdown`/`directExpenseBreakdown`/`indirectExpenseBreakdown` (lines 28-30). finance_screen.dart lines 472-480 and report_detail_screen.dart lines 61-70 read `data['totalExpense']` (singular — always 0), `data['netIncome'] ?? totalIncome - totalExpense` (netIncome doesn't exist, and since totalExpense misreads as 0 the fallback equals totalIncome), and `data['incomeAccounts']` / `data['expenseAccounts']` (nonexistent — breakdown sections never render). Result: the Expenses card always shows AED 0 and Net Income always equals Total Income on the Organisation, Property and Unit report screens.
findings.recommendation: Read totalExpenses and netProfit, and render the incomeBreakdown/directExpenseBreakdown/indirectExpenseBreakdown maps (key = 'code - name', value = amount) instead of the nonexistent incomeAccounts/expenseAccounts lists.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend: FinancialTransactionController returns ReportDTO directly for /reports/organisation, /reports/property/{id}, /reports/unit/{id}; ReportDTO (Lombok @Getter, no @JsonProperty, no Jackson naming strategy in application.yml) serializes keys as totalExpenses (plural), netOperatingIncome/netProfit, and Map-typed incomeBreakdown/directExpenseBreakdown/indirectExpenseBreakdown. Client: FinanceService/ReportService return raw response.data; the only Dio interceptors (Auth, Tenant, Log) have no response transformation; finance_reports_screen.dart passes the raw map to ReportDetailScreen unchanged. Frontend: finance_screen.dart lines 472-481 and report_detail_screen.dart lines 61-70 read data['totalExpense'] (nonexistent, defaults to 0), data['netIncome'] (nonexistent, fallback totalIncome - 0 = totalIncome), and data['incomeAccounts']/data['expenseAccounts'] (nonexistent, so breakdown sections never render). Only totalIncome matches. So the Expenses card always shows AED 0, Net Income always equals Total Income, and income/expense breakdowns never appear on the mobile admin Organisation P&L tab and Organisation/Property/Unit report screens. Severity corrected from critical to high: it silently shows wrong financial figures to landlords (serious for a finance product), but it is a display-only key mismatch scoped to mobile admin — no data corruption, no security/tenant-isolation impact, correct data intact server-side.

findings.title: Web bank-accounts page uses 'isDefault' but Jackson serializes/deserializes the property as 'default' — default flag can never be set and is silently cleared on edit
findings.evidence: BankAccount.java line 42 `private boolean isDefault` with Lombok @Getter/@Setter yields `isDefault()`/`setDefault()`, so Jackson names the JSON property `default` (BankAccountService.java line 48 confirms: `existing.setDefault(updates.isDefault());`). page.tsx line 313 renders the badge from `ba.isDefault` (always undefined — badge never shows) and lines 139-147 send `isDefault: formData.isDefault` in the POST/PUT body — an unknown property Jackson ignores (no fail-on-unknown-properties config exists in backend/src/main/resources). On PUT, the deserialized entity's isDefault defaults to false and the service unconditionally copies it, so editing a bank account that is currently default silently clears the flag.
findings.recommendation: Either add @JsonProperty("isDefault") on the entity field (and keep web as-is), or change the web page to read/send `default`. Same for the web `active` display which relies on the correctly-named `active` property (that one is fine).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed empirically. BankAccount.java uses `private boolean isDefault` with Lombok, yielding isDefault()/setDefault(); the controller binds the raw entity (no DTO). A probe compiled against the real entity and runtime classpath shows the JSON property is "default" under both Jackson 2.20.2 and Jackson 3.0.4 (known properties: {..., "default", "active"} — no "isDefault"). Spring Boot 4.0.3's HTTP layer uses only the Jackson 3 converter (spring-boot-http-converter has JacksonJsonHttpMessageConverterConfiguration only; ClockConfig's Jackson 2 bean is a different type used internally), and Jackson 3 ignores unknown properties by default — probe-verified: deserializing {"isDefault":true} succeeds with isDefault=false. Web page.tsx reads ba.isDefault (line 313 badge, line 129 form seed — always undefined) and sends isDefault in POST/PUT (ignored); it reads ba.active correctly, proving the mismatch is field-specific. BankAccountService.updateBankAccount:48 unconditionally copies the deserialized false, so any edit silently clears a flag set out-of-band. The proxy is a pure Next.js rewrite; no wrapper fixes anything. Severity corrected to medium: no backend logic consumes isDefault (no repository query, no payment/invoice routing off the default account), and the mobile app only reads the same wrong key — so the impact is a fully non-functional flag/badge plus silent clearing of out-of-band-set values, not financial misbehavior.

findings.title: Web bank-account form has a Notes field that does not exist on the backend entity — user-entered notes are silently discarded
findings.evidence: page.tsx renders a Notes textarea (lines 497-507), includes `notes` in the POST/PUT body (line 146) and declares `notes: string` on the BankAccount type (line 37). BankAccount.java (lines 18-45) has no notes field — only bankName, accountNumber, iban, branchName, currency, property, coaAccount, isDefault, isActive. Jackson silently drops the unknown property, the value is never persisted, and openEditModal (line 130) always repopulates the field as empty — silent data loss with no error.
findings.recommendation: Either add a `notes` column/field to BankAccount (with a Liquibase changeset) or remove the Notes field from the web form.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. The web page (web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/finance/bank-accounts/page.tsx) renders a Notes textarea (lines 497-507), sends `notes` in the POST/PUT body (line 146) via the /api/proxy rewrite (no body transformation), and repopulates the edit form from `ba.notes || ""` (line 130). The backend BankAccountController binds @RequestBody directly to the BankAccount JPA entity, which has no `notes` field (nor does BaseTenantEntity); BankAccountService.updateBankAccount copies only the known fields; no Liquibase changeset adds a notes column to bank_accounts; and there is no Jackson fail-on-unknown-properties override, so Spring Boot's default silently drops the unknown `notes` property with a 200 response. User-entered notes are therefore silently discarded and the field always reopens empty. Severity corrected from high to medium: it is genuine silent data loss, but limited to one optional free-text annotation field on an admin-only finance settings page, with no security, tenant-isolation, or financial-data impact.

Backend: FinancialTransactionController GET /api/v1/finance/reports/trial-balance returns TrialBalanceDTO directly (no envelope); the DTO field is `lines` with plain Lombok getters and no @JsonProperty rename, so the JSON key is `lines`. Mobile: FinanceService.getTrialBalance returns response.data raw; the only Dio interceptors (AuthInterceptor, TenantInterceptor) are request-header-only with no response transformation; finance_reports_screen.dart passes the map unmodified to ReportDetailScreen. report_detail_screen.dart line 186 reads data['accounts'] ?? data['rows'] ?? [] — neither key exists, so the account list is always empty and the per-row renderer (lines 235-280) never executes. Only the header row and totalDebit/totalCredit (correctly named keys) display, silently showing an empty trial balance. Severity downgraded to medium: rendering-only defect on one mobile admin report screen — no data corruption, no security/tenant impact, totals still correct, web unaffected — though it is misleading since the empty table can read as 'no account activity'.

findings.title: Mobile admin VAT return screen reads outputVat/inputVat/details — Output and Input VAT cards always show 0 and line details never render
findings.evidence: VatReturnDTO.java exposes `totalOutputVat` (line 12), `totalInputVat` (line 13), `salesLines` (line 17) and `purchaseLines` (line 18). report_detail_screen.dart lines 326-333 read `data['outputVat'] ?? data['vatOutput'] ?? 0` and `data['inputVat'] ?? data['vatInput'] ?? 0` (both always 0) and `data['details'] ?? data['rows'] ?? []` (always empty). Only `netVatPayable` matches via the fallback at line 329, so the screen shows Output VAT 0, Input VAT 0, yet a non-zero Net VAT Payable — internally inconsistent figures.
findings.recommendation: Read totalOutputVat/totalInputVat and render salesLines + purchaseLines (fields: description, taxableAmount, vatAmount).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end with no rescuing layer. (1) Backend: FinancialTransactionController.java:79-85 returns VatReturnDTO directly via ResponseEntity.ok; the DTO (backend/src/main/java/com/datagami/rentaxis/api/dto/VatReturnDTO.java) has plain Lombok getters with no @JsonProperty, and no global Jackson property-naming-strategy exists in backend resources/config, so JSON keys are exactly totalOutputVat, totalInputVat, netVatPayable, totalTaxableSales, totalTaxablePurchases, salesLines, purchaseLines. (2) Transport: mobile/packages/rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/report_service.dart:23-29 returns response.data raw; the only Dio interceptors in rentaxis_core (auth_interceptor, tenant_interceptor, LogInterceptor in api_client.dart) add request headers/log only — none touch response bodies. finance_reports_screen.dart passes the map straight into ReportDetailScreen.reportData. (3) Screen: report_detail_screen.dart:326-333 reads data['outputVat'] ?? data['vatOutput'] ?? 0 and data['inputVat'] ?? data['vatInput'] ?? 0 — neither key exists, so both cards always render 0; data['details'] ?? data['rows'] ?? [] never matches salesLines/purchaseLines, so the details section (guarded by details.isNotEmpty at line 387) never renders. Only netVatPayable matches via the second fallback at line 329, so the screen shows Output VAT 0.00, Input VAT 0.00, but a correct non-zero Net VAT Payable — exactly the internal inconsistency claimed. Severity correction: 'high' is overblown. This is a display-only defect confined to one report screen in the mobile admin app — no data corruption, no tenant-isolation or security impact, the authoritative net figure is still correct, and the web app has its own VAT report rendering. Misleading component figures on a tax report warrant medium, not high.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. BankAccountController returns the raw BankAccount entity (no DTO), so JSON keys are: branchName (entity line 28), nested property object (line 35), and default (Lombok isDefault() getter on boolean isDefault, line 42, Jackson strips the is- prefix; no @JsonProperty or naming strategy anywhere overrides this). No swift field exists on the entity at all. The mobile screen reads swiftCode (line 40), branch (line 41), propertyName (lines 42/216) and isDefault (line 217) — all four always null, silently hidden by isNotEmpty/==true guards, so branch, linked property and the Default badge never display. No rescue layer exists: rentaxis_core BankAccountService returns response.data verbatim and the Dio client has no response-transforming interceptor. The web page independently confirms the real contract (reads ba.branchName and ba.property?.id). findings.title: Manager app exposes all finance screens to PROPERTY_MANAGER users, but every endpoint requires SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN — guaranteed 403s with a generic error
findings.endpoint: All endpoints of AccountController, AccountMappingController, BankAccountController, FinancialTransactionController
findings.evidence: All four controllers carry class-level @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN')") (AccountController.java:17, AccountMappingController.java:19, BankAccountController.java:13, FinancialTransactionController.java:22). The manager app is used by PROPERTY_MANAGER accounts (more_screen.dart lines 679-680 render that role's label) yet the Finance menu (more_screen.dart lines 94-116: /finance, /bank-accounts, /finance-reports) is shown unconditionally with no role gating, so a PM gets 403 on every call and only a generic 'Failed to load' ErrorState. The web frontend, by contrast, hides these pages via canAccessFinance = ['SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN'] (rbac.ts line 16) — mobile and web disagree, and mobile is the wrong one.
findings.recommendation: Gate the Finance section of more_screen (and the /finance, /bank-accounts, /finance-reports, /settings/mappings routes) on authState.role in {SUPER_ADMIN, TENANT_ADMIN}, mirroring web's canAccessFinance.

verdict.explanation: Verified end-to-end. All four controllers carry class-level @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN')") at the cited lines, and ApiSecurityFilter.java:84 maps roles as ROLE_<userRole>, so a PROPERTY_MANAGER is 403'd on every endpoint. The manager app's Finance menu (more_screen.dart:94-118) is rendered with zero role gating, router.dart's redirect checks only isAuthenticated, finance_service.dart hits exactly the locked paths (/v1/finance/accounts, /v1/finance/transactions, /v1/finance/reports/*), and AuthInterceptor.onError passes errors straight through — no interceptor, rewrite, or wrapper rescues the 403. PROPERTY_MANAGER users genuinely use this app: AuthController's login excludes only SECURITY_GUARD, the app creates PM staff, and booking_approvals_screen.dart:129 already has explicit isPM handling (with a comment acknowledging PM 403s on /v1/bookings), proving the team role-gates elsewhere but missed Finance. Web rbac.ts:16 (canAccessFinance = SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN) confirms the intended policy that mobile violates. Severity correction: the backend denies access correctly, so this is not a security hole, data leak, or data-integrity issue — it is a UI role-gating inconsistency that shows PMs dead menu items ending in generic error states, while core PM workflows remain functional. That is a medium-severity UX/consistency defect, not high.

findings.title: Web account edit modal lets users change code/accountType/parentCode/group but AccountService.updateAccount silently ignores those fields
findings.evidence: accounts/page.tsx handleUpdate (lines 242-252) sends code, accountType, parentCode and group in the PUT body via the shared edit form (all editable, lines 333-417). AccountService.updateAccount (lines 186-201) copies only name/nameEn/nameAr/description/accountSubType/active/displayOrder — code, accountType, parentCode and group changes are silently dropped, and the page shows success (modal closes, list refetches with the unchanged values). Additionally the body omits `active`/`displayOrder`, so the deserialized entity defaults (true/0) overwrite whatever was stored — currently benign because no frontend or import sets those, but a latent reset.
findings.recommendation: Either apply code/accountType/parentCode/group in updateAccount (with validation) or make those inputs read-only in the edit modal; consider making updateAccount ignore absent fields instead of copying defaults.

findings.title: Transactions list filters are silently ignored by the backend for realistic combinations (accountType with propertyId; single-sided date range)
findings.evidence: FinancialTransactionService.getTransactions (lines 239-263) applies filters in exclusive priority order: date filters only apply when BOTH startDate and endDate are present, and accountType is only consulted when propertyId/unitId are absent. The web filter UI (transactions/page.tsx lines 151-170, 494-519) lets the user set propertyId + accountType, or a startDate alone, and sends whatever is set; the backend then silently drops accountType (when property chosen) or the lone date, returning data the UI presents as filtered. Same param contract is exposed by rentaxis_core FinanceService.getTransactions (finance_service.dart lines 12-26).
findings.recommendation: Either implement combinable filtering in the backend (Specification/QueryDSL) or have the frontends enforce the supported combinations (require both dates, disable accountType when property selected).

findings.title: Web chart-of-accounts CRUD shows no error feedback — realistic failures (delete with children, edit system account) return 500 and the UI does nothing
findings.evidence: AccountService throws bare RuntimeException for 'System accounts cannot be modified/deleted' and 'Cannot delete account with child accounts' (AccountService.java lines 191, 208, 211), which GlobalExceptionHandler maps to 500 with a message body (lines 133-142). accounts/page.tsx handleCreate/handleUpdate/handleDelete/handleSeedDefaults/handleImport (lines 189-319) only act `if (res.ok)` and never read the error body or set any error state — on failure the modal stays open (or the row stays) with zero user feedback. Contrast with transactions/page.tsx which does surface errData?.message (lines 258-261).
findings.recommendation: Surface the response `message` field on failure (the backend always returns {error, message, status}); ideally also convert those service RuntimeExceptions to BusinessRuleViolationException for proper 400/409 codes.

findings.title: Mobile admin vendor ledger shows a Balance column that always reads 0.00 — no balance field exists in the response
findings.evidence: getVendorLedger (FinancialTransactionService.java lines 558-564) returns raw FinancialTransaction entities — there is no balance or runningBalance field on the entity. report_detail_screen.dart line 420 reads `(tx['balance'] ?? tx['runningBalance'] ?? 0).toDouble()` and renders it under a 'Balance' label (lines 486-509), so every ledger row shows Balance 0.00 next to correct debit/credit values — misleading financial display.
findings.recommendation: Compute the running balance client-side from debit/credit, or drop the Balance column, or add a running balance to the backend response.

findings.title: Web bank-accounts save/delete failures are silent (no error message shown)
findings.evidence: handleSubmit (lines 160-176) and the delete confirm handler (lines 185-194) only act `if (res.ok)`; on a non-2xx response (e.g. 500 'Bank account not found' from BankAccountService.java line 30, or an FK violation on delete) nothing is displayed and the modal stays open with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: Read the error body ({error, message, status}) and show the message near the form/confirm dialog.

findings.title: Manager app fetches lease penalties from a nonexistent endpoint (GET /api/v1/leases/{id}/penalties)
findings.endpoint: GET /api/v1/leases/{leaseId}/penalties (does not exist; real endpoint is GET /api/v1/penalties?leaseId=)
findings.evidence: penalty_service.dart:29 `final response = await _dio.get('/v1/leases/$leaseId/penalties');` is called from lease_penalties_screen.dart:76 `final penalties = await service.getPenalties(widget.leaseId);` (screen routed at manager router.dart:127 path 'penalties', linked from lease_detail_screen.dart:1127). Backend has no such mapping: PenaltyController.java:32 maps `@RequestMapping("/api/v1/penalties")` with only a root `@GetMapping` (line 43), and LeaseController.java (@RequestMapping("/api/v1/leases")) has no penalties route. The web codebase confirms this route never existed: leases/[id]/page.tsx:252-253 comment 'there is no /leases/{id}/penalties route, the previous URL silently 404'd'. Result: guaranteed 404, caught at lease_penalties_screen.dart:82-88 which permanently shows 'Failed to load penalties'. The card also reads `penalty['status'] == 'ACTIVE'` (line 296-297) — a value PenaltyDTO.status() never returns (OPEN/CLEARED/WAIVED), showing the screen was written against a phantom API.
findings.recommendation: Change PenaltyService.getPenalties to GET /v1/penalties with queryParameters {leaseId: leaseId, size: ...} (as listPenalties already does) and unwrap the Spring Page `content` array; update _PenaltyCard status handling to OPEN/CLEARED/WAIVED.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end from the real code. Client side: /Users/kunalsharma/datagami/rentaxis/mobile/packages/rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/penalty_service.dart:29 issues `_dio.get('/v1/leases/$leaseId/penalties')`; Dio baseUrl is `<host>/api` (api_client.dart:16), so the request goes to /api/v1/leases/{id}/penalties. Both Dio interceptors (auth_interceptor.dart, tenant_interceptor.dart) only add headers — nothing rewrites paths, and infra/caddy/Caddyfile.template proxies /api/v1/* verbatim. Backend side: the only penalty mappings in the entire backend are in PenaltyController.java (@RequestMapping "/api/v1/penalties" with a root @GetMapping taking `leaseId` as a query param, plus POST /{id}/payments and POST /{id}/waive); a repo-wide grep confirms no controller maps a lease-nested penalties path, and LeaseController has no penalties route. So the call is a guaranteed 404, which Dio surfaces as an exception caught at lease_penalties_screen.dart:82-88, permanently rendering "Failed to load penalties". The screen is genuinely reachable: router.dart registers `leases/:id/penalties` and lease_detail_screen.dart pushes '/leases/${leaseId}/penalties' from a visible Penalties link card. Corroborating evidence all checks out: PenaltyDTO.status() returns only OPEN/CLEARED/WAIVED (never the 'ACTIVE' the card checks at lease_penalties_screen.dart:297-298), and the web fix comment at web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/leases/[id]/page.tsx:253 explicitly notes the nested route never existed and previously 404'd. (The same service is broken further: recalculatePenalties posts to /v1/leases/{id}/penalties/recalculate which also has no mapping, and waivePenalty uses PUT where the controller maps POST /waive.) Severity: real but 'critical' is overblown — no data loss, no security/tenant-isolation impact, no crash; the error is handled gracefully, the renter app's listPenalties path works, and managers have a working web-dashboard alternative (GET /penalties?leaseId=). It is a shipped manager-app feature that is 100% non-functional, which merits 'high', not 'critical'.

findings.title: Manager app recalculate-penalties calls a nonexistent endpoint (POST /api/v1/leases/{id}/penalties/recalculate)
findings.evidence: penalty_service.dart:41 `final response = await _dio.post('/v1/leases/$leaseId/penalties/recalculate');` invoked from lease_penalties_screen.dart:122-124 (_recalculatePenalties, wired to an AppBar action at line 233). No controller in backend/src/main/java/com/datagami/rentaxis/api maps any 'recalculate' path — grep for 'recalculate' only matches the service method PenaltyService.recalculateForLease (core/service/PenaltyService.java:188), which is never exposed via REST. Every tap returns 404; the catch at lease_penalties_screen.dart:131-136 shows 'Failed to recalculate penalties'.
findings.recommendation: Either add a backend endpoint (e.g. POST /api/v1/penalties/recalculate?leaseId= delegating to PenaltyService.recalculateForLease with an SA/TA/PM guard) or remove the recalculate action from the manager app.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. penalty_service.dart:41 posts '/v1/leases/$leaseId/penalties/recalculate' on a Dio whose baseUrl ends in '/api' (api_client.dart:16), producing POST /api/v1/leases/{id}/penalties/recalculate; interceptors (Auth/Tenant/Log) only add headers, no path rewrite. The screen wires this to an AppBar action (lease_penalties_screen.dart:233 -> _recalculatePenalties at 122-124) with the failure snackbar at 131-136. Backend-side, PenaltyController maps only /api/v1/penalties (GET list, POST {id}/payments, POST {id}/waive) and LeaseController has no penalties subpath; grep for 'recalculate' across backend sources matches only the unexposed service method PenaltyService.recalculateForLease (core/service/PenaltyService.java:188), which has no callers anywhere. Every tap therefore 404s. Severity 'critical' is overblown: the failure is handled gracefully (snackbar, no crash), there is no data corruption or tenant-isolation impact, and the same screen's list call (GET /v1/leases/{id}/penalties) also has no backend mapping — the feature appears never to have worked, i.e. a dead feature on one manager-app screen, not a regression in a critical path. Corrected severity: medium.

findings.title: Web waive-penalty uses PUT but backend endpoint is POST — guaranteed 405 with silent UI failure
findings.evidence: Backend: PenaltyController.java:91 `@PostMapping("/{id}/waive")` (POST only). Web: leases/[id]/page.tsx:285-289 `fetch(`/api/proxy/v1/penalties/${waiveModalPenalty.id}/waive`, { method: "PUT", ... body: JSON.stringify({ reason: waiveReason.trim() }) })`. Next.js proxy rewrites preserve the HTTP method, so Spring returns 405 Method Not Allowed. handleWaivePenalty (lines 281-296) only acts on `res.ok` and has no else/error branch — the modal stays open with no message, so waiving is both broken and silent. The request body itself ({reason}) matches WaivePenaltyRequestDTO.
findings.recommendation: Change method to "POST" in handleWaivePenalty, and add an else branch surfacing the error (400/403/404/409 BusinessRuleViolation messages such as 'Penalty already cleared').

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend PenaltyController.java:91 maps waive as @PostMapping("/{id}/waive") only (no @PutMapping anywhere; no other controller maps this path). Web leases/[id]/page.tsx:285-289 calls /api/proxy/v1/penalties/{id}/waive with method: "PUT". The path between them cannot fix it: web/src/proxy.ts middleware only auth-checks and adds X-User-* headers then NextResponse.next(), and next.config.ts uses a plain rewrite (/api/proxy/:path* -> ${backendUrl}/api/:path*) which preserves the HTTP method — there is no route handler under app/api/proxy to translate the verb. Spring therefore returns 405. The handler (lines 290-295) only acts on res.ok, has no else branch and an empty catch {}, so the modal stays open with no error — broken and silent, exactly as claimed. Additionally, the mobile shared client (rentaxis_core penalty_service.dart:34) also uses _dio.put for the same endpoint, so no client can waive penalties at all. Severity correction: "critical" is overblown — this repo reserves P0/critical for tenant-isolation/security/data-loss issues; this is a fully broken, silently failing user-facing workflow (financial-adjacent, all clients affected) with no data corruption or security impact, which is "high".

findings.title: Manager app waive-penalty uses PUT but backend endpoint is POST — guaranteed 405
findings.evidence: penalty_service.dart:34 `final response = await _dio.put('/v1/penalties/$penaltyId/waive', data: {...});` vs backend PenaltyController.java:91 `@PostMapping("/{id}/waive")`. Dio PUT to a POST-only mapping returns 405, caught at lease_penalties_screen.dart:203-208 as generic 'Failed to waive penalty'. (Screen currently never reaches this point because the list itself 404s, but the call is independently broken.)
findings.recommendation: Change _dio.put to _dio.post in PenaltyService.waivePenalty.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. penalty_service.dart:34 issues _dio.put('/v1/penalties/$penaltyId/waive') against baseUrl ending in /api, resolving to PUT /api/v1/penalties/{id}/waive. PenaltyController.java:91 maps that path only as @PostMapping (git -S shows it was never PUT). No mitigating layer exists: Dio interceptors (Auth/Tenant/Log) do not rewrite methods, and no other controller exposes a PUT waive route — Spring returns 405, caught generically at lease_penalties_screen.dart:203-208. Corroborating: the web frontend (dashboard/leases/[id]/page.tsx:286) also uses PUT through a method-preserving next.config.ts rewrite, so waive is broken from every client. Severity corrected from critical to high: it is a functional defect with graceful failure — no data loss, security, or tenant-isolation impact — and the mobile call is currently unreachable anyway (the screen's list GET /v1/leases/{id}/penalties has no backend mapping and 404s first). It stays high rather than medium because the waive capability has no working client anywhere, and even after fixing the method the mobile app would 400 on empty reason (WaivePenaltyRequestDTO requires @NotBlank reason while the app sends {}).

findings.title: Manager waive sends empty body when reason is blank, but backend requires @NotBlank reason
findings.evidence: Backend contract: WaivePenaltyRequestDTO is `record WaivePenaltyRequestDTO(@NotBlank String reason)` and the controller validates with @Valid (PenaltyController.java:95). Mobile: penalty_service.dart:34-36 sends `{ if (reason != null) 'reason': reason }` — i.e. `{}` when reason is null — and the screen passes `reason: reasonCtrl.text.isNotEmpty ? reasonCtrl.text : null` (lease_penalties_screen.dart:195) with the reason TextField presented as optional (hint text only, no validation, lines 159-168). Once the PUT→POST method bug is fixed, any waive submitted with a blank reason gets a 400 validation error, shown only as the generic 'Failed to waive penalty'. Web correctly requires the reason (leases/[id]/page.tsx:282 `if (!waiveModalPenalty || !waiveReason.trim()) return;` and disabled button at line 1267).
findings.recommendation: Make the reason mandatory in the manager waive dialog (disable confirm until non-empty) and always send the 'reason' key; align with the web dialog behavior.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend (PenaltyController.java:91-96) validates @Valid @RequestBody WaivePenaltyRequestDTO, and the DTO is record WaivePenaltyRequestDTO(@NotBlank String reason) — an empty body {} yields reason=null and a 400. Mobile (penalty_service.dart:34-36) sends `{ if (reason != null) 'reason': reason }`, i.e. {} when reason is null, and the screen (lease_penalties_screen.dart:195) passes null for empty input while the TextField hint explicitly says "Reason (optional)" with no validation (lines 159-168, 483). Failures surface only as the generic 'Failed to waive penalty' snackbar. Adversarial checks found no rescue: the shared Dio client's interceptors (AuthInterceptor, TenantInterceptor) are header-only and never rewrite bodies; whitespace-only input also fails @NotBlank. Caveat: the service uses _dio.put against a @PostMapping, so every mobile waive currently 405s — this bug is latent until that method mismatch is fixed (the claim acknowledges this). Severity downgraded from high to medium: real functional defect on a common path with misleading UI, but trivially worked around by typing any reason, no data loss/corruption or security impact, and currently masked by the PUT/POST bug.

findings.title: Manager rent-settings screen renders fields that do not exist in RentCollectionSettingsDTO
findings.evidence: RentCollectionSettingsDTO fields are id, propertyId, dueDayOfMonth, gracePeriodDays, penaltyType, penaltyAmount, onlinePaymentEnabled plus five fine* override fields. rent_settings_screen.dart reads `settings['penaltyRate']` (line 325) — always null, so the 'Late Payment Penalty Rate' row permanently renders '-%' via `percent(dynamic n) => '${n ?? '-'}%'` (line 436) even when penaltyType is FIXED_PER_DAY/PERCENTAGE with a configured penaltyAmount. It also gates rows on `settings['autoApplyPenalty']` (line 333) and `settings['reminderDaysBefore']` (line 339), fields the DTO never returns, so those rows never appear. Meanwhile the real fields penaltyAmount, dueDayOfMonth and onlinePaymentEnabled are never displayed.
findings.recommendation: Read penaltyAmount (labelled per penaltyType: AED/day vs %/day), and drop or re-source the autoApplyPenalty/reminderDaysBefore rows; consider also showing dueDayOfMonth and onlinePaymentEnabled.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. RentCollectionSettingsDTO (backend/src/main/java/com/datagami/rentaxis/api/dto/RentCollectionSettingsDTO.java) contains only id, propertyId, dueDayOfMonth, gracePeriodDays, penaltyType, penaltyAmount, onlinePaymentEnabled and five fine* override fields; RentCollectionSettingsService.mapToDTO sets exactly those and grep shows penaltyRate/autoApplyPenalty/reminderDaysBefore exist nowhere in the rent-settings backend path. The Flutter SettingsService.getRentSettings (mobile/packages/rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/settings_service.dart) returns raw response.data with no transformation, and all Dio interceptors are request-side only. Therefore in rent_settings_screen.dart: line 325's settings['penaltyRate'] is always null so the 'Late Payment Penalty Rate' row permanently shows '-%' via percent() (line 436) even when a penalty is configured; the rows gated on settings['autoApplyPenalty'] (line 333) and settings['reminderDaysBefore'] (line 339) can never render; and penaltyAmount, dueDayOfMonth, onlinePaymentEnabled, and the fine* overrides are never displayed. The screen is reachable (router.dart:324). Severity corrected to medium: it is a display-only defect on a read-only admin screen — misleading (implies no penalty configured) but causes no data corruption, no wrong penalty computation, and no security impact.

findings.title: Web lease page 'Total Outstanding Penalties' banner sums base fines and includes cleared penalties instead of using the DTO's outstanding field
findings.evidence: leases/[id]/page.tsx:797-804: `const activePenalties = penalties.filter(p => !p.waived); const totalOutstanding = activePenalties.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.penaltyAmount, 0);` rendered as 'Total Outstanding Penalties: {formatCurrency(totalOutstanding)}'. PenaltyDTO provides `outstanding` (currentTotal minus recorded payments; 0 once cleared) and `clearedAt`. This banner (a) counts fully-paid CLEARED penalties because the filter only excludes waived ones, (b) ignores per-day accrual (currentTotal > penaltyAmount when finePerDayRate applies), and (c) ignores partial payments. Any lease with a cleared or partially-paid penalty shows an inflated 'outstanding' figure; the same page's cheque-penalties section correctly uses pen.outstanding (line 1185).
findings.recommendation: Compute the banner from the DTO: filter on derived status OPEN (clearedAt == null) and sum p.outstanding (or p.currentTotal).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. fetchPenalties (web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/leases/[id]/page.tsx:254) hits /api/proxy/v1/penalties?leaseId&size=200 with no status param; the proxy is a plain rewrite (next.config.ts:25) and PenaltyController.list defaults status="all" (PenaltyController.java:47), so the penalties state contains OPEN, CLEARED, and WAIVED rows. The banner (page.tsx:797-803) filters only !p.waived and sums p.penaltyAmount, so it (a) includes fully-paid CLEARED penalties, (b) uses the base fine instead of currentTotal (which adds daysOverdue*finePerDayRate per PenaltyPaymentService.currentTotal, lines 171-176), and (c) ignores partial payments. The DTO's outstanding field (PenaltyDTO.java:22, computed in PenaltyPaymentService.outstanding lines 183-189: zero when cleared/waived, else currentTotal minus receipts) is the correct value and is already used correctly at page.tsx:1185 in the cheque-penalties section. No interceptor or wrapper corrects the sum. Severity downgraded from high to medium: it is a display-only banner — no financial write path consumes the number, and the accurate outstanding figure appears in the adjacent cheque-penalties section — but it does show a misleading inflated financial figure (and shows a warning banner even when all penalties are fully paid).

findings.title: Web shows the Waive button to PROPERTY_MANAGER but the endpoint only allows SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN
findings.evidence: Backend: PenaltyController.java:92 `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN')")` on waive. Web: leases/[id]/page.tsx:153 `const isAdmin = hasRole(userRole, ["SUPER_ADMIN", "TENANT_ADMIN", "PROPERTY_MANAGER"]);` and the Waive button is rendered behind `isAdmin` (lines 909-915). A PROPERTY_MANAGER therefore sees and can submit the waive modal but the backend will reject with 403 (once the PUT/POST method bug is fixed), and handleWaivePenalty has no error rendering, so it fails silently.
findings.recommendation: Gate the Waive button (and modal) on hasRole(userRole, ['SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN']) to match the endpoint, or relax the backend guard if PMs are meant to waive.

findings.title: Manager app exposes Rent Collection Settings to PROPERTY_MANAGER, but the endpoint is SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN-only
findings.evidence: RentCollectionSettingsController.java:20 `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN')")` on GET. The manager app serves PROPERTY_MANAGER users (staff created with role PROPERTY_MANAGER, staff_screen.dart:225) and the navigation path more_screen.dart:142 (`context.push('/settings')`) → settings_hub_screen.dart:29 (`context.push('/settings/rent')`) → rent_settings_screen.dart:45 (`service.getRentSettings(propertyId)` → GET /v1/rent-settings/{id}) has no role gating anywhere.
