The web equivalent gates correctly via canConfigureRentSettings (rbac.ts:112-114, SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN only).
findings.recommendation: Hide the Rent Collection Settings row in SettingsHubScreen for non-TENANT_ADMIN roles (authState.role), or add PROPERTY_MANAGER to the backend guard if this read-only view is intended for PMs; at minimum map 403 to a distinct 'no permission' message.

findings.title: Web rent-settings page depends on res.json() throwing to handle the documented 204 No Content response
findings.evidence: Backend returns 204 with an empty body when no settings exist: RentCollectionSettingsController.java:23-25 `if (settings == null) { return ResponseEntity.noContent().build(); }`. Web fetchSettings (rent-settings/page.tsx:139-163): `if (res.ok) { const data = await res.json(); ... }` — 204 satisfies res.ok, res.json() then rejects on the empty body, and only the catch block (lines 155-160, commented 'Treat network errors as no settings') applies the defaults. The explicit `res.status === 404` branch (line 146) is dead code — this endpoint never returns 404. The correct outcome currently happens by accident via the exception path, conflating 'no settings yet' with genuine network failures. The mobile service handles this properly (settings_service.dart:9 `if (response.statusCode == 204) return null;`).
findings.recommendation: Handle 204 explicitly before parsing: `if (res.status === 204) { setSettings({...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, propertyId}); return; }`, and drop the dead 404 branch.

findings.title: Manager Arabic penalty-type label maps PERCENTAGE_OF_RENT but backend enum value is PERCENTAGE
findings.evidence: Backend PenaltyType.java:4 enum values are `NONE, FIXED_PER_DAY, PERCENTAGE` (serialized via .name() in RentCollectionSettingsService.mapToDTO). rent_settings_screen.dart:439-443 arMap keys are 'NONE', 'FIXED_PER_DAY', 'PERCENTAGE_OF_RENT' — the last key never matches, so an Arabic-locale user sees the raw English 'PERCENTAGE' (fallback line 444) instead of 'نسبة من الإيجار'. Web uses the correct values (rent-settings/page.tsx:378-381: NONE / FIXED_PER_DAY / PERCENTAGE).
findings.recommendation: Rename the map key to 'PERCENTAGE' in _L.penaltyTypeLabel.

findings.title: Registered gate vendors can never be revoked or time-bounded from any frontend
findings.evidence: Backend: GateWalkInController.java:215-224 `@PutMapping("/visitors/{profileId}/registration") public void registerVisitor(@PathVariable UUID profileId, @RequestBody RegistrationRequest request)` with `RegistrationRequest(UUID unitId, Instant validFrom, Instant validTo, boolean active)` (GateWalkInDtos.java:67) is the ONLY API that can set `active=false` or add validFrom/validTo bounds to an existing registration. Grep of all four frontends finds no caller; rentaxis_core's GatePassApiService (gate_pass_service.dart) exposes only `registerGateVisitor` → POST /v1/gatepass/visitors/registration. The one frontend writer, register_gate_vendor_screen.dart:99-108, always sends `'validFrom': null, 'validTo': null, 'active': true`, so every registration created from the manager app is unbounded and permanently active. GateWalkInService.create:105-107 then routes registered visitors through `policy.requireRegisteredApproval()` (default false per effectivePolicy:62), meaning a once-registered maid/vendor skips resident approval at that unit indefinitely with no UI anywhere to turn it off.
findings.recommendation: Add a manager surface (mobile_admin, and/or web) that lists a unit's visitor registrations and calls PUT /v1/gatepass/visitors/{profileId}/registration with active=false or explicit validFrom/validTo — add the corresponding wrapper to rentaxis_core's GatePassApiService. If revocation is intentionally out of scope for now, document the gap; do not delete the endpoint, since it is the only revoke mechanism.

findings.title: Resident-approval avatar refetches walk-in photo on every widget rebuild
findings.evidence: resident_approvals_screen.dart:214-215: `FutureBuilder(future: ref.read(gatePassServiceProvider).walkInPhoto(passId!), ...)` creates a new Future inside build(). The enclosing _ApprovalCardState calls setState twice per decision (`setState(() => _busy = true)` at line 119 and `setState(() => _busy = false)` at line 135), and each rebuild re-invokes walkInPhoto — GET /v1/gatepass/walk-in/{id}/photo returns the full image bytes (GateWalkInController.java:105-124, Cache-Control private max-age=300 which Dio does not honor), so the photo is re-downloaded and the CircleAvatar flickers back to the placeholder mid-decision. Correct endpoint/method/role (RENTER is permitted and residentUnitIds is enforced server-side), so this is an efficiency/UX defect, not a contract mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Create the photo Future once (StatefulWidget initState, a memoized field, or a FutureProvider.autoDispose.family keyed by pass id) so each card downloads its photo exactly once per screen visit.

findings.title: Web renter portal leaves stale actionable rows after 400 on cancel/release
findings.evidence: web page.tsx runPendingAction lines 199-204: `} catch (err) { setPendingAction(null); setActionLoading(false); setError(err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : t("requestError")); return; }` — the error path returns without calling loadFacilities()/loadBookings() (the refresh at lines 207-211 only runs on success). Backend BookingService.java: cancel() line 236 calls requirePending(booking), which at lines 333-336 throws BusinessRuleViolationException("Booking is not pending") -> 400 whenever an admin decided the request while the page sat open; release() line 251 similarly throws "Only approved bookings can be released" -> 400. So the web row keeps its stale PENDING/APPROVED status and its Cancel/Release button, and every retry re-fails with the same raw 400 message until a full page reload — there is no manual refresh control on this page. The mobile renter app handles the identical case correctly: my_requests_screen.dart lines 213-221 branch on `error.response?.statusCode == 400`, invalidate BOTH myBookingRequestsProvider and myFacilitiesProvider, and toast a localized 'request changed state' message (comment: "a 400 means server state already moved, so the held/pendingCount facts below are stale too").
findings.recommendation: In runPendingAction's catch, when err is an ApiError with status 400 (and 409), re-run Promise.all([loadFacilities(), loadBookings()]) before returning, and show a localized 'this request changed state' message instead of the raw backend English string — mirroring the mobile renter app's 400 branch.

findings.title: Admin booking drawer shows stale otherRequests after 409 on approve
findings.evidence: BookingDetailDrawer.tsx act() lines 82-93: on 409 it only does `setError(t("spotConflict"))` — it never re-fetches the detail (load() is not called), so detail.otherRequests keeps showing the competitor that just won the spot with a PENDING badge, and the Approve/Reject footer stays enabled against data known to be stale. Backend BookingService.approve() lines 215-221 throws SlotConflictException("Parking spot is already assigned to another renter") -> 409 exactly when a competing request was APPROVED. The mobile manager app refreshes for this precise reason: booking_approvals_screen.dart line 561 `ref.invalidate(bookingDetailProvider(widget.bookingId));` with the comment "the competitor that just won the race now belongs in otherRequests with an APPROVED badge instead of the stale PENDING one".
findings.recommendation: In BookingDetailDrawer.act(), call load() (re-fetch the detail) after receiving a 409, matching the mobile manager sheet's invalidate-on-409 behavior.

findings.title: Renter request dialog does not refresh facilities after a 409 spot conflict
findings.evidence: page.tsx submitRequest lines 170-179: on ApiError 409 it does `setDialogError(tB("spotConflict")); setSubmitting(false); return;` — the refresh (Promise.all([loadFacilities(), loadBookings()]) at line 187) only runs on success, and closing the dialog (setTarget(null), lines 495/558) triggers no refetch either. Backend BookingService.create() line 122 throws SlotConflictException("Parking spot is already assigned") -> 409 because the spot became APPROVED for someone else after the page's data was fetched, so the card behind the dialog keeps `held: false` (rendered as "Available" at lines 380-383) and its enabled Request button invites another guaranteed 409. The mobile renter app invalidates myFacilitiesProvider and myBookingRequestsProvider unconditionally when the request sheet closes (facilities_screen.dart lines 596-597, comment "belt and braces").
findings.recommendation: Refresh myFacilities (and myBookings) whenever the request dialog closes after an error — or at minimum on a 409 — so the card's held/Available state resyncs with the server, matching the mobile renter app.

findings.title: Manager bulk-add comment misstates backend collision behavior
findings.evidence: facilities_screen.dart lines 1008-1011 justify popping created.length with: "bulk requests can silently produce fewer rows than expected if entries collide with existing spots". The backend does the opposite: FacilityService.bulkCreateParkingSpots() validates every number BEFORE creating any (line 216 `requireSpotNumberFree(tenantId, req.propertyId(), number)` inside a loop preceded by the comment "validate every number before creating any"), and requireSpotNumberFree (lines 359-363) throws BusinessRuleViolationException("Spot number already exists: " + spotNumber) -> 400, making collisions all-or-nothing, never a silent partial create. Runtime behavior of the app is still correct (on success created.length always equals the deduped request size; on 400 the catch shows the backend message), so only the comment misleads future maintainers.
findings.recommendation: Fix the comment to say collisions fail the whole batch with a 400 naming the duplicate spot number; the created-count toast is still useful because parseSpotNumbers dedupes ranges client-side.

findings.title: Web media reorder sends a raw JSON array but backend expects {"mediaIds": [...]} — guaranteed 400, silently swallowed
findings.evidence: Backend UnitListingController.java:149-157: `@PutMapping("/{id}/media/reorder") public ResponseEntity<Void> reorderMedia(@PathVariable UUID id, @RequestBody ReorderRequest body)` with `public record ReorderRequest(List<UUID> mediaIds)` — Jackson deserializes records in properties mode, so the payload must be an object `{"mediaIds": [...]}`. Web listings.ts:241-245 sends `body: JSON.stringify(mediaIds)` — a bare array `["uuid1","uuid2"]` — which fails deserialization with HttpMessageNotReadableException -> 400 on every call. The mobile service proves the correct shape: listing_api_service.dart:135-138 sends `data: {'mediaIds': mediaIds}`. The only web call site, dashboard/listings/[id]/page.tsx:332-334 `await reorderMedia(listing.id, newMedia.map(m => m.id), token)` inside `try {...} catch {}`, swallows the 400: the UI shows the optimistically swapped order (line 331 setMedia) but it is never persisted and reverts on reload.
findings.recommendation: Change web reorderMedia to send `body: JSON.stringify({ mediaIds })`, and surface the error in handleMoveMedia instead of the empty catch (revert local state on failure). Add a backend controller test covering the reorder payload shape.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend UnitListingController.java:149-158 binds @RequestBody to record ReorderRequest(List<UUID> mediaIds) with no @JsonCreator(DELEGATING) or @JsonFormat(shape=ARRAY), and the app's ObjectMapper (ClockConfig.java) adds no deserialization features — so Jackson requires {"mediaIds":[...]} and a bare JSON array yields HttpMessageNotReadableException → 400. Web listings.ts:244 sends JSON.stringify(mediaIds), a bare array; the Next.js proxy (next.config.ts:25-26) is a pure rewrite with no body transformation and no /api/proxy route handler exists. The only web call site (dashboard/listings/[id]/page.tsx:331-334) optimistically swaps state then swallows the thrown error in an empty catch, so the reorder appears to work but never persists and reverts on reload. Mobile (listing_api_service.dart:133-139) sends the correct {'mediaIds': ...} shape, confirming the contract. Severity corrected from critical to medium: every web reorder fails, but there is no data loss, corruption, or security impact — it is a single silently-broken UI control (listing photo order) with a working mobile workaround.

findings.title: Mobile admin create-listing payload never includes required unitId — create always fails (403 for PROPERTY_MANAGER, 500 for TENANT_ADMIN)
findings.evidence: The create flow is reachable: listings_list_screen.dart:142 `context.push('/listings/new')` -> ListingEditScreen with `_listingId == null` -> listing_edit_screen.dart:351 `await service.createListing(data)`. The payload builder `_buildPayload()` (listing_edit_screen.dart:404-437) contains titleEn, furnishing, rent, amenities, etc. but `grep -n unitId listing_edit_screen.dart` returns zero matches — unitId is never collected or sent, and there is no unit picker in the screen. Backend UnitListingCreateRequest.unitId is required in practice: UnitListingController.java:87 `checkPropertyManagerAccess(req.unitId())` throws AccessDeniedException("Unit must be specified") -> 403 (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:50-52) when unitId is null for PROPERTY_MANAGER; for TENANT_ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN the check is skipped and UnitListingService.create (UnitListingService.java:113-116) saves `listing.setUnitId(null)` into column unit_id declared `nullable: false` (37-unit-listings.yaml:22-25) -> DataIntegrityViolationException -> 500. Web sends unitId correctly (web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/listings/[id]/page.tsx:206 `unitId: form.unitId`), confirming the mobile payload is the wrong one.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit selector to the mobile listing_edit_screen create flow (fetch units via unit_service) and include `'unitId': _unitId` in _buildPayload for creates. Backend should also validate unitId with a 400 instead of leaking a 500 for admins.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Mobile create flow is reachable (listings_list_screen.dart:142 -> /listings/new -> ListingEditScreen with _listingId=null -> createListing at line 351). _buildPayload() (lines 404-437) never includes unitId, the screen has no unit picker, and grep finds zero unitId references in the manager listings screens or rentaxis_core. ListingApiService.createListing posts the map verbatim; Dio interceptors (Auth/Tenant) only add headers. Backend UnitListingController.create:87 calls checkPropertyManagerAccess(req.unitId()); for PROPERTY_MANAGER a null unitId throws AccessDeniedException("Unit must be specified") mapped to 403 (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:50-57, located at api/GlobalExceptionHandler.java, not api/exception/ as cited — trivial path error). For TENANT_ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN the check is skipped and UnitListingService.create saves unitId=null into a column that is nullable:false both in the entity (UnitListing.java:25 @Column(nullable=false)) and DB (37-unit-listings.yaml), producing a RuntimeException caught by the 500 catch-all. No bean validation returns an earlier 400 (UnitListingCreateRequest has no @NotNull). Web sends unitId (page.tsx:206) confirming the contract; mobile update (PUT) is unaffected. Severity corrected from critical to high: the create-listing feature is completely broken on mobile admin for all roles, but there is no security impact, no data loss (failed insert persists nothing), no tenant-isolation breach, and the web dashboard offers a full workaround.

findings.title: Web marketplace bedrooms filter sends query param 'bedrooms' but backend reads 'minBedrooms' — filter is silently ignored
findings.evidence: Backend MarketplaceController.java:72 declares `@RequestParam(required = false) Integer minBedrooms`; there is no 'bedrooms' parameter. Web listings.ts:56 sends `q.set('bedrooms', String(params.bedrooms))`, driven by the filter UI in marketplace/[tenantSlug]/page.tsx:387 `bedrooms: bedroomsParam ? Number(bedroomsParam) : undefined`. Spring silently drops the unknown parameter, so a renter selecting '3 beds' still sees all listings. The mobile renter app uses the correct name (listing_api_service.dart:26 `'minBedrooms': minBedrooms`), confirming the web param is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Rename the web query param to `minBedrooms` in fetchMarketplaceListings (and decide whether the UI semantic is exact-match or minimum; backend implements >= minBedrooms).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Web sends 'bedrooms' (web/src/lib/api/listings.ts:56, driven by page.tsx:359/387), the Next.js rewrite (/api/proxy/:path* -> ${BACKEND_URL}/api/:path* in web/next.config.ts:25-26) forwards the query string verbatim with no remapping, and there is no route handler under web/src/app/api that intercepts marketplace calls. Backend MarketplaceController.java:72 declares only @RequestParam(required=false) Integer minBedrooms; Spring silently drops the unknown 'bedrooms' param, minBedrooms binds null, and MarketplaceService.java:83-84 skips the bedrooms predicate — so the filter returns unfiltered results with no error. No client-side post-filtering masks it. Mobile (listing_api_service.dart:26) uses the correct 'minBedrooms' name, confirming the backend contract. Severity downgraded from high to medium: it is a silently broken renter-facing filter, but there is no security/data/financial impact, other filters work, and the fix is a one-line param rename.

findings.title: Web marketplace furnishing multi-select joins values with commas into a single-enum param — guaranteed 400 when 2+ options checked
findings.evidence: The FilterPanel renders furnishing as checkboxes allowing multiple selections (marketplace/[tenantSlug]/page.tsx:203-205 toggleFurnishing, 260-272), and handleApplyFilters line 458 sends `furnishing: filters.furnishing.join(',')`; listings.ts:59 passes it as one query param. Backend MarketplaceController.java:75 declares `@RequestParam(required = false) Furnishing furnishing` — a single enum. Spring's String->Furnishing conversion of 'UNFURNISHED,SEMI_FURNISHED' throws MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException -> 400, so checking two furnishing boxes makes the entire listings load fail and the page shows the generic errorLoad banner. One checked box works (values match enum UNFURNISHED|SEMI_FURNISHED|FULLY_FURNISHED).
findings.recommendation: Either make the UI single-select, or change the backend param to `List<Furnishing> furnishing` (IN predicate) and keep the comma-joined value.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. FilterPanel checkboxes allow multi-select (page.tsx:203-205, 261-271); handleApplyFilters joins with commas (page.tsx:458); the param is passed verbatim through loadListings (page.tsx:390) and set as a single query param in listings.ts:59. The /api/proxy rewrite in next.config.ts:25-26 forwards the query string unchanged and there is no proxy route handler that could transform it. Backend MarketplaceController.java:75 binds a single Furnishing enum; the repo has no custom Converter/ConversionService/@InitBinder (grep verified), and Spring only comma-splits for collection/array targets, so "UNFURNISHED,SEMI_FURNISHED" fails Enum.valueOf → MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException → 400 (GlobalExceptionHandler has no handler for it; default Spring behavior applies). The frontend fetch throws on !res.ok and the page shows the generic errorLoad banner. Single selection works since values match the enum exactly. Severity corrected to medium: the whole listings load fails, but only when 2+ furnishing boxes are checked, recovery is trivial (uncheck/clear filters), and there is no data, security, or tenant-isolation impact.

findings.title: Web marketplace 'Nearest first' sort sends sort=distance,asc — no such entity property, backend returns 500
findings.evidence: marketplace/[tenantSlug]/page.tsx:480-485 adds `{ value: 'distance,asc', label: t('sortNearest') }` to sortOptions whenever geolocation succeeds, and the selected sort is sent verbatim (listings.ts:61 `q.set('sort', params.sort)`; loadListings line 392). The backend applies the Pageable sort directly to the JPA Specification query: MarketplaceService.java:43-46 `return listingRepository.findAll(spec, pageable)`. UnitListing has lat/lng columns but no `distance` attribute, so QueryUtils.toOrders fails with PropertyReferenceException -> 500, and the page falls into the generic error banner. The frontend also never sends nearLat/nearLng/radiusKm, so no distance semantics exist server-side at all.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 'distance,asc' sort option (or implement server-side distance ordering using nearLat/nearLng); the backend should also whitelist sortable properties to avoid 500s on arbitrary sort params.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end from real code. (1) web/src/app/[locale]/marketplace/[tenantSlug]/page.tsx:484 adds { value: 'distance,asc' } to sortOptions whenever geolocation succeeds (userPos set), and line 392 sends sortParam verbatim; web/src/lib/api/listings.ts:61 does q.set('sort', params.sort) with no rewriting, and fetchMarketplaceListings never sends nearLat/nearLng/radiusKm (the params interface at listings.ts:37-46 doesn't even have them). (2) The Next.js rewrite (web/next.config.ts:25) forwards /api/proxy/:path* to the backend with the query string intact — no interceptor touches sort. (3) MarketplaceController.listListings (line 81) binds a plain @PageableDefault Pageable with no sort whitelist, and MarketplaceService.java:43-46 passes it straight into listingRepository.findAll(spec, pageable) (UnitListingRepository extends JpaSpecificationExecutor). (4) UnitListing has lat/lng fields but no 'distance' attribute. (5) Verified in the actual resolved jars (spring-data-jpa 4.0.3 / spring-data-commons 4.0.3): QueryUtils.toJpaOrder calls PropertyPath.from("distance", UnitListing.class), which throws PropertyReferenceException, and javap shows org.springframework.data.core.PropertyReferenceException extends java.lang.RuntimeException directly — so it bypasses GlobalExceptionHandler's IllegalArgumentException→400 handler and hits the RuntimeException catch-all (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:133) → HTTP 500. The frontend's catch at page.tsx:414 then shows the generic error banner. There is no client-side fallback: distanceKm is computed only for display badges, not for sorting. Severity correction: 'high' is overblown — the bug triggers only when a renter grants geolocation AND manually selects 'Nearest first', the default and other sorts work, no data/security impact, and the user can recover by switching the sort back (the sort select stays visible in the error state). It is a fully broken user-facing feature with a 500, but a self-recoverable, opt-in one: medium.

findings.title: Map/distance features read lat/lng from UnitListingSummaryDTO, which has no such fields — renter map shows zero markers, web distance chips never render
findings.evidence: UnitListingSummaryDTO.java defines exactly: id, title, propertyName, bedrooms, annualRent, status, coverPhotoUrl, interestsCount, updatedAt, slug — no lat/lng/bathrooms (see also MarketplaceController.java:174-199 toSummary). The renter app map builds markers from these summary maps: browse_map.dart:52-55 `final lat = listing['lat'] as num?; final lng = listing['lng'] as num?; ... if (lat == null || lng == null || id == null) continue;` — lat/lng are always null, so map mode (browse_screen.dart:187-188 BrowseMap(listings: items)) never shows a single marker. Web does the same: marketplace/[tenantSlug]/page.tsx:35-40 casts summaries to `ListingWithDistance` with `lat?/lng?/bathrooms?` and lines 396-402 compute distanceKm only `if (userPos && ext.lat != null && ext.lng != null)` — never true, so the distance chip (line 105-110) and bathrooms fact (line 140) never render.
findings.recommendation: Add lat/lng (and bathrooms) to UnitListingSummaryDTO for the marketplace list response (they are already on the entity and exposed in the detail DTO), or have the map/distance features fetch detail data. Until then the renter map view is dead weight.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. UnitListingSummaryDTO (backend/src/main/java/com/datagami/rentaxis/api/dto/UnitListingSummaryDTO.java) has exactly the 10 claimed fields and MarketplaceController.toSummary (lines 174-199) populates only those — no lat/lng/bathrooms, even though the entity has them (toDetail line 223 proves getLat()/getLng() exist). No layer repairs this: the mobile ListingApiService returns Dio response.data verbatim and the only interceptors (Auth/Tenant/Log) touch request headers, not bodies; the web /api/proxy is a next.config.ts rewrite (no route handler), and fetchMarketplaceListings returns res.json() untouched. Consequences verified: browse_map.dart:52-55 skips every listing (lat/lng always null) so the renter map mode (reachable via toggle, browse_screen.dart:161,188) always renders zero markers; web page.tsx:396-402 never computes distanceKm so the distance chip (105-110) and bathrooms fact (76,140) never render. Severity downgraded to medium: the web map is an explicit "coming soon" placeholder so no web map depends on this; web losses are silent cosmetic enhancements; server-side near-me filtering (nearLat/nearLng/radiusKm query params) still works; and the only true break — the empty mobile map — is a secondary view of data fully available in the working list view, with no crash, data, or tenant-isolation impact.

findings.title: Dashboard listings search box does nothing: web sends 'search', backend declares 'q' — and the backend ignores both q and propertyId anyway
findings.evidence: Backend UnitListingController.java:59-67 declares `@RequestParam(required = false) UUID propertyId, @RequestParam(required = false) String q` but calls `service.list(tenantId, status, pageable)` — UnitListingService.java:96 `public Page<UnitListing> list(UUID tenantId, ListingStatus statusFilter, Pageable pageable)` has no q/propertyId, so both params are dead. Web additionally sends the wrong name: listings.ts:127 `q.set('search', params.search)`, fed by the visible search input at dashboard/listings/page.tsx:288-294 (updateUrlParam('search', ...)) and line 106 `search: searchQuery || undefined`. Net effect: typing in the Listings search box triggers a reload but always returns the unfiltered list, with no error. The status filter (line 105 -> backend `status`) works correctly.
findings.recommendation: Implement q (title search) and propertyId filtering in UnitListingService.list, and rename the web param from 'search' to 'q' — or remove the dead params and the search box until implemented.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. UnitListingController.java:59-74 declares `q` and `propertyId` as optional @RequestParams but calls service.list(tenantId, status, pageable), and UnitListingService.list (lines 96-101) only branches on status (findByTenantIdAndStatus/findByTenantId) — both params are dead. The web client compounds it by sending the wrong name: listings.ts:127 sets 'search' (not 'q'), fed by the visible input at dashboard/listings/page.tsx:288-294 and line 106. No middleware fixes this: next.config.ts proxies /api/proxy/:path* to the backend via a plain rewrite that preserves query strings verbatim, and there is no route handler under web/src/app/api/proxy/ that could rename params. Spring silently ignores unknown/unbound optional params, so typing in the search box refetches and always returns the unfiltered tenant listing page with HTTP 200. The status filter does work as claimed. Severity corrected from high to medium: it is a silently broken search box on one dashboard page — no data loss, no cross-tenant leak, no blocked workflow (status filter, sort, and pagination still function), so listings remain reachable by other means.

findings.title: Web marketplace pages call the auth-gated proxy for logged-out visitors — middleware 401 surfaces as a generic 'failed to load' with no login redirect
findings.evidence: proxy.ts:19-24: every /api/proxy request without a NextAuth token gets `new NextResponse('Unauthorized', { status: 401 })`. The marketplace browse page runs loadListings unconditionally on mount (marketplace/[tenantSlug]/page.tsx:379-421) even when `session` is null, so an unauthenticated visitor (e.g. following a shared /en/marketplace/<slug> URL) always gets the catch-all `setError(t('errorLoad'))` banner (line 414-415) instead of being sent to login — the backend is renter-only by design (@PreAuthorize("hasRole('RENTER')"), MarketplaceController.java:42). The wishlist page handles this correctly by redirecting unauthenticated users (wishlist/page.tsx:199-203); the browse and detail pages do not.
findings.recommendation: On the marketplace browse/detail pages, detect sessionStatus === 'unauthenticated' and redirect to login with returnTo (matching the wishlist page), or route anonymous visitors to the public /l/{tenantSlug} pages which are designed for logged-out browsing.

findings.title: Renter app auto-applies a 10 km near-me filter whose backend predicate silently excludes all listings without coordinates
findings.evidence: browse_screen.dart:109-126 `_seedLocation()` sets nearLat/nearLng/radiusKm=10 automatically whenever the device grants location, and these are always sent (lines 75-77). Backend MarketplaceService.java:109-119 then adds `cb.between(root.get("lat"), latMin, latMax)` and the same for lng — SQL BETWEEN on a NULL lat/lng is never true, so every listing whose lat/lng was left empty (both optional in UnitListingCreateRequest and the manager edit screens) disappears from browse for location-enabled renters. The only cue is a small removable 'near me 10km' chip (browse_screen.dart:396-403); the landlord just sees their listing not appearing.
findings.recommendation: Either include null-coordinate listings when a radius filter is active (add `cb.isNull(root.get("lat"))` OR-branch), or don't auto-seed the radius filter — require an explicit user opt-in to 'near me'.

findings.title: Mobile admin fetches listings and interests as a single page of 100 with no pagination — data beyond 100 rows is silently truncated
findings.evidence: Both endpoints return a Spring Page. listings_list_screen.dart:12-13: `final data = await service.getListings(size: 100); return (data['content'] as List? ?? [])...` — totalElements/totalPages are never read and there is no page control, so a tenant with more than 100 listings can never see the rest. Same pattern in listing_interests_screen.dart:12-13 with `getInterests(listingId, size: 100)`. Contrast with the renter browse screen, which at least surfaces truncation (browse_screen.dart:195 `truncated: allItems.length >= 50`).
findings.recommendation: Add paging (infinite scroll or page controls) using the Page metadata already returned, or at minimum surface a truncation indicator when content.length == size.

findings.title: Web wishlist page reads interestStatus/bathrooms/availableFrom from the wishlist response — none exist in UnitListingSummaryDTO, so the NOTIFIED badge and bath count never render
findings.evidence: The endpoint returns List<UnitListingSummaryDTO> (MarketplaceController.java:122-157) with only id/title/propertyName/bedrooms/annualRent/status/coverPhotoUrl/interestsCount/updatedAt/slug. wishlist/page.tsx:19-24 declares `interface WishlistItem extends UnitListingSummaryDTO { bathrooms?; availableFrom?; interestStatus?; }` (comment admits 'API may return it' — it does not), then line 144 passes `interestStatus={item.interestStatus}` to StatusBadge whose NOTIFIED branch (lines 32-38) is therefore unreachable, and lines 156-159 render bathrooms which is always undefined. Note the wishlist also hardcodes interestsCount=0 in toSummary (MarketplaceController.java:195), so that field is unusable here too. No crash — purely dead UI.
findings.recommendation: Either extend the wishlist response with interest status (the InterestService already tracks NOTIFIED) and bathrooms, or delete the phantom fields and the dead badge branch from the page.

findings.title: Dashboard listings 'Created' column sorts by createdAt but displays updatedAt
findings.evidence: dashboard/listings/page.tsx:107 requests `sort: 'createdAt,' + sortDir` and the sortable column header is labeled colCreated (lines 379-387), but the cell renders `new Date(listing.updatedAt).toLocaleDateString()` (line 452) because UnitListingSummaryDTO only carries updatedAt, not createdAt. Rows can therefore appear out of order relative to the dates shown whenever a listing has been edited after creation.
findings.recommendation: Add createdAt to UnitListingSummaryDTO and display it, or relabel the column and sort key to Updated.

findings.title: Backend sitemap emits relative <loc> URLs, served verbatim by the web sitemap route — invalid per the sitemap protocol
findings.evidence: PublicListingController.java:102-104 writes `<loc>/l/%s/%s</loc>` — a path with no scheme/host. The sitemaps.org protocol requires fully-qualified absolute URLs in <loc>. The web route handler (app/l/[tenantSlug]/sitemap.xml/route.ts:14-27) fetches and returns the XML unchanged, so crawlers receive an invalid sitemap and the SEO purpose of the endpoint is defeated.
findings.recommendation: Pass the public base URL to the backend (config property) and emit absolute URLs, or rewrite the loc values in the Next.js route handler using the request host.

findings.title: Dead /api/marketplace rewrite in next.config bypasses the auth-header middleware — any future caller gets guaranteed 401/403
findings.evidence: next.config.ts:32-35 rewrites `/api/marketplace/:path*` straight to the backend, but the auth middleware matcher (proxy.ts:51-54) only covers `/api/proxy/:path*`, so requests via this rewrite carry no X-User-Id/X-User-Role headers and the RENTER guard on MarketplaceController rejects them. Nothing in web/src currently uses it (grep for '/api/marketplace' outside the proxy base returns no hits — all helpers use MARKET_BASE = '/api/proxy/marketplace', listings.ts:12), making it a trap for future code and an inconsistency with how the same endpoints are actually reached.
findings.recommendation: Delete the /api/marketplace rewrite, or add it to the middleware matcher so auth context is injected consistently.

findings.title: Manager app create-renter payload uses wrong field names; POST /v1/renters always fails 400
findings.evidence: renters_screen.dart:275-281 sends {'name': ..., 'email': ..., 'phoneNumber': ..., 'preferredLanguage': 'ENGLISH'|'ARABIC'}. CreateRenterDTO.java declares @NotBlank String nameEn (plus nameAr, phone, Language primaryLanguage with values EN/AR). RenterController.createRenter is @Valid, so a body without nameEn is rejected by GlobalExceptionHandler.handleValidation (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:59-69) with 400 'Validation failed: nameEn: must not be blank' — on every submission. Even if it passed, 'phoneNumber'/'preferredLanguage' are unknown properties (silently dropped) so phone/language would never persist. Additionally the endpoint is @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN','TENANT_ADMIN')") (RenterController.java:36) while the FAB at renters_screen.dart:111-115 is shown to every manager-app user, so a PROPERTY_MANAGER would get 403 even with a correct payload. The response's portalPassword (RenterDTO.java:16) is also never surfaced, unlike web (renters/page.tsx:84-86).
findings.recommendation: Send {'nameEn': name, 'email': email, 'phone': phone, 'primaryLanguage': 'EN'|'AR'} (optionally nameAr, createPortalAccount). Hide or disable the create FAB for PROPERTY_MANAGER, and show the returned portalPassword to the admin like the web app does.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. renters_screen.dart:275-281 posts {'name','email','phoneNumber','preferredLanguage':'ENGLISH'|'ARABIC'}; RenterService (rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/renter_service.dart) forwards the map verbatim to POST /v1/renters, and the only Dio interceptors (AuthInterceptor, TenantInterceptor) add headers without touching the body — no remapping layer exists. Backend CreateRenterDTO requires @NotBlank nameEn (expects nameEn/nameAr/phone/primaryLanguage with enum EN/AR), has no @JsonAlias or custom deserializer, and no fail-on-unknown-properties config, so the unknown keys are dropped, nameEn is null, and @Valid triggers MethodArgumentNotValidException → GlobalExceptionHandler.handleValidation → 400 on every submission; the app shows only a generic 'Failed to create renter' snackbar. Secondary claims also verified: phone/language would never persist even if validation passed; POST is @PreAuthorize SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN while the FAB shows for all users (PROPERTY_MANAGER → 403); the response's portalPassword is discarded (web surfaces it in renters/page.tsx). Severity downgraded from critical to high: the mobile create-renter flow is completely broken, but it fails visibly, causes no data corruption or security/tenant-isolation impact, and the web dashboard offers a fully working path for the same operation.

findings.title: Manager app create-ticket default category MAINTENANCE (and GENERAL) not in TicketCategory enum — 400 on submit
findings.evidence: create_ticket_screen.dart:119 initialises _selectedCategory = 'MAINTENANCE' and the chip list (lines 125-135) offers 'MAINTENANCE' and 'GENERAL'. Backend enum TicketCategory is {PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, HVAC, STRUCTURAL, PEST_CONTROL, CLEANING, APPLIANCE, SECURITY, OTHER}; MaintenanceTicketService.java:93-94 does TicketCategory.valueOf(dto.getCategory()) which throws IllegalArgumentException for MAINTENANCE/GENERAL → 400 via GlobalExceptionHandler.handleIllegalArgument. Submitting with the pre-selected default therefore always fails ('Failed to create ticket' snackbar, create_ticket_screen.dart:302-310). The renter app (renter/lib/screens/create_ticket_screen.dart:121-139) and web (tickets/page.tsx:68-78) use only valid enum values, so only the manager app is broken. STRUCTURAL and APPLIANCE are also missing from the manager list.
findings.recommendation: Replace the manager app's category list with the backend enum values (drop MAINTENANCE/GENERAL, add STRUCTURAL/APPLIANCE), mirroring the renter app. Consider backend-side: return 400 with a clear message instead of relying on valueOf.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Manager app create_ticket_screen.dart:119 defaults _selectedCategory='MAINTENANCE' and the chip list (lines 125-135) offers 'MAINTENANCE' and 'GENERAL'. _submit() (line 277) sends the value verbatim; rentaxis_core TicketService.createTicket posts the raw map to POST /v1/tickets with no transformation, and the Dio interceptors (AuthInterceptor, TenantInterceptor) only add headers. Backend CreateTicketDTO.category is a plain String; MaintenanceTicketService.java:93-94 calls TicketCategory.valueOf(category), and the enum {PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, HVAC, STRUCTURAL, PEST_CONTROL, CLEANING, APPLIANCE, SECURITY, OTHER} lacks MAINTENANCE and GENERAL, so valueOf throws IllegalArgumentException, mapped to HTTP 400 by GlobalExceptionHandler (lines 71-78). The app shows only a generic 'Failed to create ticket' snackbar (lines 302-310). Severity corrected from critical to high: submitting with the pre-selected default always fails, breaking the happy path of a core manager flow with a misleading error, but 7 of 9 offered categories are valid so a workaround exists, and there is no data loss, security, or tenant-isolation impact.

findings.title: Manager app renters directory reads nonexistent RenterDTO fields — every row renders 'Unknown'
findings.evidence: RenterDTO returns {id, nameEn, nameAr, email, phone, primaryLanguage, userId, portalPassword}. renters_screen.dart reads r['name'] for display/sort/search (lines 61, 75, 135, 430), r['unitNumber']/r['unit'] (line 431), r['propertyName']/r['property'] (line 432), r['status'] (line 438) and r['balance'] (line 439) — none of which exist in the DTO. Result: every renter row shows the l.unknown fallback (line 478), all rows group under the '#' section (line 136), name search never matches, and the trailing widget always shows a green '0 balance' (lines 533-535). Same class of bug in create_ticket_screen.dart:424 where the on-behalf-of dropdown reads r['name'] ?? r['email'] and so shows emails only.
findings.recommendation: Read nameEn/nameAr (locale-aware) and phone from RenterDTO; drop unit/property/status/balance until the API actually provides them (or enrich the DTO backend-side).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. GET /api/v1/renters returns List<RenterDTO> whose only fields are {id, nameEn, nameAr, email, phone, primaryLanguage, userId, portalPassword} (RenterController.java, RenterDTO.java; mapToDTO sets nameEn/nameAr; no Jackson renames). The mobile chain has no fixup layer: rentaxis_core RenterService.getRenters() returns response.data raw, and ApiClient registers only request-side interceptors (AuthInterceptor, TenantInterceptor) — no response transformation. renters_screen.dart (routed live at /renters in router.dart:197) reads r['name'] (lines 61/75/135/430), r['unitNumber']/r['unit'], r['propertyName']/r['property'], r['status'], r['balance'] — none exist — so every row renders the 'Unknown' fallback (line 478) with '?' initials, all rows group under '#', name sort/search are no-ops, subtitle is empty, and the trailing widget always shows a green '0 balance' (status '' forces the balance branch, null balance parses to 0). create_ticket_screen.dart:424 similarly falls back to email-only labels (its _renters come from the same getRenters()). Minor evidence nits: search by email/phone still works since those keys exist, and the balance fallback spans lines 533-544, not 533-535 — neither changes the verdict. Severity 'critical' is overblown: no crash, data loss, security/tenant issue, and web is unaffected — but the manager app's renter directory is useless for identifying renters with no in-app workaround, so 'high' is the right rating.

findings.title: Create ticket without a property triggers findById(null) server error; web even offers 'General (no specific property)'
findings.evidence: MaintenanceTicketService.java:71-72 unconditionally calls propertyRepository.findById(dto.getPropertyId()); CreateTicketDTO.propertyId has no @NotNull and the controller has no @Valid, so a null propertyId reaches Spring Data's findById(null), which throws IllegalArgumentException/InvalidDataAccessApiUsageException ('The given id must not be null') → an obscure 400 or 500, never a ticket. All three creators can send it null: web tickets/page.tsx:203 sends 'propertyId: form.propertyId || undefined' and the property dropdown's default option is literally 'General (no specific property)' (line 487) with no client-side requirement (handleCreate line 194 only checks title); manager create_ticket_screen.dart:279 ('if (_selectedPropertyId != null)') has no property validator; renter create_ticket_screen.dart:234 same pattern when the renter has no/malformed lease data. Web then swallows the failure (only 'if (res.ok)', line 210) so the modal appears to do nothing.
findings.recommendation: Backend: validate propertyId (@NotNull or explicit BusinessRuleViolationException 'propertyId is required'). Frontends: make property selection required (remove/repurpose the 'General' option or add a general-property concept), and show the API error message on failure.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend: MaintenanceTicketService.java:71 unconditionally calls propertyRepository.findById(dto.getPropertyId()); CreateTicketDTO has no @NotNull and the controller's @RequestBody has no @Valid, so a missing propertyId reaches Spring Data's findById(null), which throws "The given id must not be null". GlobalExceptionHandler has no InvalidDataAccessApiUsageException handler, so it lands in the RuntimeException catch-all (500) or the IllegalArgumentException handler (400 with the raw Spring message) — never a created ticket. All three creators can send it null: web tickets/page.tsx sends propertyId: form.propertyId || undefined (dropped by JSON.stringify), validates only title (line 194), and its default admin/PM dropdown option is "General (no specific property)" (line 487) — meaning the default web selection always fails, and line 210's bare if(res.ok) swallows the failure so the modal silently does nothing. Manager mobile's property dropdown has no validator and omits propertyId when unselected (line 279); renter mobile only sets propertyId from lease data and omits it when the renter has no leases (line 234). No interceptor, proxy rewrite, or envelope unwrapping repairs the request. Severity downgraded from high to medium: no security or data-integrity impact, ticket creation works whenever a property is selected, and the failure is scoped to the no-property path (albeit the web default) with an easy workaround and trivial fix.

findings.title: Renter app reads 'closingOtp'/'otp' instead of 'closureOtp' — resolution OTP never shown, OTP close flow broken on mobile
findings.evidence: MaintenanceTicketDTO.java:27 names the field 'closureOtp' (set at MaintenanceTicketService.java:557). The renter app's RESOLVED-state OTP card passes otp: ticket['closingOtp'] ?? ticket['otp'] (ticket_detail_screen.dart:410) — both keys nonexistent — and _OtpSection returns SizedBox.shrink() when otp is null/empty (line 1149). So a renter using the mobile app never sees the 6-digit code the PM needs to close the ticket (PUT /{id}/close validates it at MaintenanceTicketService.java:283-287). The web renter view reads ticket.closureOtp correctly (web tickets/[id]/page.tsx:407-411), confirming which side is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Change line 410 to ticket['closureOtp'] (keep the old keys as fallbacks if desired).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend: GET /api/v1/tickets/{id} returns MaintenanceTicketDTO directly (MaintenanceTicketController.java:40-44, no envelope); the DTO field is `closureOtp` (MaintenanceTicketDTO.java:25, Lombok @Data, no @JsonProperty, and no Jackson PropertyNamingStrategy override anywhere in backend config), so the JSON key is exactly `closureOtp`. It is populated in mapToDTO (MaintenanceTicketService.java:557), generated on RESOLVED (lines 215-216), and validated on PUT /{id}/close (lines 283-287, required unless tenant sets ticketOtpRequired=false, default true). Mobile: TicketService.getTicketById returns raw response.data (rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/ticket_service.dart:12-15) and ApiClient's interceptors (Auth, Tenant, Log) are request-side only — no onResponse key remapping. The renter screen reads `ticket['closingOtp'] ?? ticket['otp']` (ticket_detail_screen.dart:410); neither key ever exists, so _OtpSection gets null and silently renders SizedBox.shrink() (line 1149). Grep confirms `closureOtp` appears nowhere in the entire mobile tree, and the TICKET_RESOLVED notification text does not include the code, so a mobile-only renter has no in-app way to obtain it. Both PM close surfaces are OTP-gated in UI: the manager app prompts 'Enter renter OTP' and calls closeTicket (manager ticket_detail_screen.dart:271-284) and the web dashboard close button requires a 6-digit OTP (web tickets/[id]/page.tsx:210,553). The web renter view reads ticket.closureOtp correctly (page.tsx:407-411), confirming the mobile side has the wrong key. Severity 'high' is fair: with default settings the renter-mobile→PM close flow is broken end-to-end and fails silently; the only workarounds are out-of-surface (renter logs into the web portal, tenant disables the OTP requirement, or an admin bypasses via PUT /{id}/status RESOLVED→CLOSED which skips OTP validation). Not critical since tickets can still be closed via those fallbacks and there is no data loss or security impact.

findings.title: Manager app shows 'Start Work' on OPEN (unassigned) tickets — backend always rejects with 400
findings.evidence: _ActionsPanel renders the primary 'Start Work' button when status == 'OPEN' || 'ASSIGNED' (ticket_detail_screen.dart:1113-1138), wired to _updateStatus('IN_PROGRESS') (line 579). MaintenanceTicketService.java:220-222 throws BusinessRuleViolationException('Ticket must be assigned before moving to IN_PROGRESS') when assignedTo == null — which is the normal state of an OPEN ticket (assignTicket flips OPEN→ASSIGNED at lines 173-175). So tapping the main CTA on any OPEN ticket yields 400 and the generic 'Failed to update status' snackbar. The web UI is correct (Start Work only for ASSIGNED/REOPENED, tickets/[id]/page.tsx:536-540). Additionally the panel renders no actions at all for REOPENED status even though the backend allows REOPENED→ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS/CLOSED (MaintenanceTicketService.java:529).
findings.recommendation: Only show Start Work once the ticket is ASSIGNED (or auto-assign-to-me first), and add an actions branch for REOPENED mirroring OPEN/ASSIGNED.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end from real code. (1) Frontend: /Users/kunalsharma/datagami/rentaxis/mobile/apps/manager/lib/screens/ticket_detail_screen.dart line 1113 renders the panel branch for `status == 'OPEN' || status == 'ASSIGNED'`, whose primary CTA is GoldButton 'Start Work' (line 1138) wired to `onStartWork: () => _updateStatus('IN_PROGRESS')` (line 579). (2) `_updateStatus` (line 211) calls TicketService.updateStatus, which in /Users/kunalsharma/datagami/rentaxis/mobile/packages/rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/ticket_service.dart line 27-29 is a bare `PUT /v1/tickets/{id}/status` with `{'status': ...}` — no auto-assign, no interceptor fixup. (3) Backend: MaintenanceTicketService.updateStatus passes validateStatusTransition (OPEN → IN_PROGRESS is allowed, line 524) but then throws BusinessRuleViolationException('Ticket must be assigned before moving to IN_PROGRESS') at lines 220-222 because assignedTo is null — tickets are created OPEN with no assignee (line 79; assignedTo is only ever set by assignTicket, which simultaneously flips OPEN→ASSIGNED at lines 172-175), so a normally-OPEN ticket always trips this guard. (4) GlobalExceptionHandler.java lines 41-46 maps it to HTTP 400. (5) The Dart catch shows the generic 'failed to update status' snackbar (lines 224-232), hiding the real reason. Secondary claim also verified: _ActionsPanel branches only on OPEN/ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, and CLOSED (line 1219) — REOPENED renders a header with zero actions despite backend allowing REOPENED→ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS/CLOSED (line 529). Severity correction: 'high' is overblown. The same panel offers a one-tap workaround ('Assign to me' → status becomes ASSIGNED → Start Work then succeeds), there is no data loss/corruption or security impact, and the web UI is correct. It is a confusing dead-end on the primary CTA plus a mobile-only action gap for REOPENED tickets — a real functional/UX defect in a core manager workflow, but recoverable in-app: medium.

findings.title: Web meetings page combines server-side and client-side pagination — meetings beyond the first 20 are unreachable
findings.evidence: fetchMeetings requests page=currentPage-1&size=itemsPerPage from the paginated backend (meetings/page.tsx:92-96) and stores only data.content (line 102-104). The component then re-paginates client-side: paginated = filtered.slice((currentPage-1)*itemsPerPage, currentPage*itemsPerPage) (lines 125-128) — on page 2 this slices indices 20..40 of a 20-element array (empty). Worse, Pagination receives totalItems={filtered.length} (line 343) which is at most one server page (20), so Pagination.tsx:24 computes totalPages = 1 and the user can never navigate past page 1. Net effect: with more than itemsPerPage meetings, the list view and the calendar view (calendarEvents built from the same 'filtered', line 132) silently show only the first 20; client-side status/type/purpose filters also only filter within that first page. The renter-portal page handles the same endpoint correctly by reading data.totalPages (renter-portal/page.tsx:87-97).
findings.recommendation: Either fetch all pages / a large size for the calendar and paginate purely client-side, or drop the client slice and drive Pagination from the backend's totalElements/totalPages.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. MeetingController (lines 35-53) returns Page<MeetingDTO> (default size 20, sorted slotStart ASC); the Next.js /api/proxy rewrite is a plain passthrough and the page uses native fetch, so nothing unwraps or fixes the envelope. meetings/page.tsx requests page/size server-side (lines 92-96) but stores only data.content (102-104), discarding totalElements/totalPages. It then re-slices the single 20-item server page client-side (lines 125-128) and passes totalItems=filtered.length (max 20) to Pagination, which computes totalPages=1 — next button disabled, only page "1" rendered, so pages beyond 1 are unreachable (and the double-slice would render them empty anyway). calendarEvents (line 132) is built from the same single page; with slotStart ASC ordering, the visible 20 are the oldest meetings, so new/upcoming meetings silently vanish from both list and calendar once a tenant exceeds itemsPerPage, while the footer claims "Showing 1-20 of 20". The renter-portal page (dashboard/renter-portal/page.tsx:87-97) handles the same envelope correctly, confirming the contrast. Severity 'high' is appropriate: silent, guaranteed-with-growth invisibility of actionable meeting requests in the primary meetings UI; the 100-per-page selector is only a partial, undiscoverable mitigation. No security/data-integrity impact, so not critical.

findings.title: Manager app reads 'assignedToName' but DTO field is 'assigneeName' — every ticket appears unassigned
findings.evidence: MaintenanceTicketDTO.java:34 declares 'assigneeName' (set at MaintenanceTicketService.java:584-587). Manager tickets_screen.dart:652 reads ticket['assignedToName'] (always null → list rows render the 'Unassigned' branch, line 802), and ticket_detail_screen.dart:520-524 gates the assignee card on ticket['assignedToName'] != null, so the card never renders even for assigned tickets. The renter app defends correctly with ticket['assigneeName'] ?? ticket['assignedToName'] (renter ticket_detail_screen.dart:234-236, tickets_screen.dart:424).
findings.recommendation: Read 'assigneeName' (and 'assignedTo' for the id) in both manager screens.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend serializes 'assigneeName' (MaintenanceTicketDTO.java:34, plain Lombok @Data, no @JsonProperty renames; populated at MaintenanceTicketService.java:584-587 via dto::setAssigneeName); 'assignedToName' appears nowhere in the backend. The mobile transport does not fix it up: TicketService (rentaxis_core/lib/api/services/ticket_service.dart) returns raw response.data, and the Dio client's interceptors (Auth/Tenant/Log) touch only request headers. Manager tickets_screen.dart:652 reads ticket['assignedToName'] which is always null, so the assignee row (lines 750-790) never renders and ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS tickets fall through to the "Unassigned · raised X ago" text (lines 800-802) — affirmatively false info. ticket_detail_screen.dart:520-524 gates the assignee card on the same wrong key, so the assignee's identity is never visible anywhere in the manager app. The renter app's fallback (assigneeName ?? assignedToName) confirms the correct key. Minor mitigations that do not refute: the "assigned to me" filter uses the UUID key 'assignedTo' (correct) and status chips/counts still reflect ASSIGNED status — so managers can tell a ticket is assigned, just not to whom, while the card text simultaneously claims "Unassigned". Severity 'high' stands: display-only (no data corruption, assignment works), but core triage information is wrong/missing across every ticket in the primary ops app, likely to cause double-assignment and confusion.

findings.title: Backend leaks closureOtp to managers in every ticket response, defeating the renter-OTP close handshake
findings.evidence: mapToDTO unconditionally copies the secret: dto.setClosureOtp(ticket.getClosureOtp()) (MaintenanceTicketService.java:557), and GET /{id} / GET / are only @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()") (MaintenanceTicketController.java:33, 41). The OTP exists so the renter must confirm closure (PUT /{id}/close validates it, service lines 283-287, and notifies the reporter to 'share the OTP', line 234), but any PM/admin can read closureOtp straight from the ticket JSON and close the ticket without the renter. The web UI only *renders* it for renters (tickets/[id]/page.tsx:407) but the API itself returns it to everyone.
findings.recommendation: Null out closureOtp in mapToDTO unless the requester is the reporting renter (X-User-Id == reportedBy or role RENTER).

findings.title: Web ticket detail reads ticket.estimatedHours; DTO field is estimatedResolutionHours — ETA never displays
findings.evidence: The page's Ticket type declares estimatedHours (tickets/[id]/page.tsx:34) and renders '{ticket.estimatedHours && <DetailRow ... value={`${ticket.estimatedHours} hours`} />}' (line 509), but MaintenanceTicketDTO.java:22 names the field estimatedResolutionHours. estimatedHours is always undefined, so after a PM sets an ETA via PUT /{id}/estimate (handleSetEta, line 212-216 — which works) the ETA row still never appears. The same type also declares reporterId/assignedToId (lines 29-30) which don't exist in the DTO (reportedBy/assignedTo), though those are currently unread.
findings.recommendation: Rename the field reads to estimatedResolutionHours (and reportedBy/assignedTo) to match the DTO.

findings.title: Manager app 'On behalf of' sends renterId, which CreateTicketDTO does not have — selection silently discarded
findings.evidence: create_ticket_screen.dart:281 sends "if (_selectedRenterId != null) 'renterId': _selectedRenterId". CreateTicketDTO has no renterId field — the only related field is 'onBehalfOf' (String, free-text name, CreateTicketDTO.java:16), which is what web sends (tickets/page.tsx:207 'onBehalfOf: form.onBehalfOf || undefined'). Spring Boot's default fail-on-unknown-properties=false means the unknown key is silently dropped, so the manager's on-behalf-of choice never persists and no error is raised.
findings.recommendation: Send onBehalfOf with the selected renter's display name (or extend CreateTicketDTO with a renterId reference and map it server-side).

findings.title: Mobile meeting lists fetch a single page (size 50) and MeetingService discards pagination metadata — silent truncation
findings.evidence: Both endpoints return Page<MeetingDTO>. meeting_service.dart:13-34 returns only data['content'] and throws away totalPages/totalElements; manager meetings_screen.dart:132-133 calls svc.listMeetings() / svc.listMyMeetings(perspective: 'host') with the default size 50 and no paging UI, and renter meetings_screen.dart:36 does the same with perspective 'requester'. A tenant with more than 50 meetings silently sees only the first 50 (sorted slotStart ASC — so newest/furthest meetings vanish first).
findings.recommendation: Return the full page object (or expose totalPages) from MeetingService and add incremental loading, or request a sort/window that guarantees relevant items (e.g. upcoming-only).

findings.title: Mobile meeting creation collapses the 409 slot-conflict response (with nextAvailableSlot) into a generic failure
findings.evidence: The backend returns 409 with {error, nextAvailableSlot} on slot conflicts (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:24-30, thrown at MeetingService.java:79-83) and 400 with a message for past/out-of-window slots (MeetingService.java:60-70). Both mobile submit handlers catch every DioException identically: manager create_meeting_screen.dart:286-294 and renter create_meeting_screen.dart:212-218 show only a fixed 'Failed to create meeting'/'submitFailed' snackbar, discarding the reason and the suggested nextAvailableSlot. Web handles this correctly (CreateMeetingModal.tsx:384-390 reads err.error and err.nextAvailableSlot on 409). Since mobile only offers API-listed available slots, the 409 race is realistic (two users booking the same slot).
findings.recommendation: On DioException, inspect response.statusCode/response.data: for 409 show the conflict message and offer the nextAvailableSlot; for 400 surface the backend message.

findings.title: Web create-renter form (and ticket/meeting action buttons) swallow API errors — failed writes look like nothing happened
findings.endpoint: POST /api/v1/renters (pattern also on PUT /v1/tickets/{id}/* and PUT /v1/meetings/{id}/*)
findings.evidence: renters/page.tsx:73-99 handleSubmit only acts 'if (res.ok)'; a 400 (@Email validation) or a failure from portal-user creation (e.g. duplicate email — RenterService.java:63-80 aborts the whole transaction) produces no user feedback at all; the catch only console.errors. Same pattern on ticket actions (tickets/[id]/page.tsx:186-198 performAction ignores non-ok, so a 400 'Invalid OTP' from PUT /close or an invalid transition just does nothing) and meeting actions (meetings/[id]/page.tsx:98-109, e.g. 400 'Cannot approve meeting in status: ...'). The backend deliberately returns structured {message} bodies for these cases (GlobalExceptionHandler.java:41-48).
findings.recommendation: Read the error body's message on !res.ok and surface it (toast/inline), at minimum for create-renter (whose OTP/duplicate-email failures are common) and the OTP close action.

findings.title: Manager app history rows read item['description']; DTO field is 'notes' — descriptive history text never shown
findings.evidence: ticket_detail_screen.dart:1329 renders item['description'] ?? item['action'] ?? ''. TicketHistoryDTO has no 'description' — the human-readable text is 'notes' (TicketHistoryDTO.java:18, populated like 'Ticket assigned to <name>' / 'Status changed: X → Y' in MaintenanceTicketService.recordHistory). The manager app therefore always falls back to raw action codes ('STATUS_CHANGED') and also ignores performedByName. Web reads h.notes || h.action correctly (tickets/[id]/page.tsx:594).
findings.recommendation: Read item['notes'] ?? item['action'] and append item['performedByName'] like the web activity list.

findings.title: Ticket attachments endpoints return the raw JPA entity; mobile reads nonexistent 'name'/'fileName' keys
findings.evidence: getAttachments/uploadAttachment return List<TicketAttachment>/TicketAttachment entities directly (MaintenanceTicketController.java:98-110); TicketAttachment carries a non-@JsonIgnore'd lazy @ManyToOne ticket (TicketAttachment.java:20-24), so the payload serializes the whole nested ticket graph and its shape is an accident of entity structure rather than a contract. The entity has no 'name' field, yet manager _AttachmentThumb reads att['name'] ?? att['fileName'] (ticket_detail_screen.dart:1023) so every thumb is labelled the literal 'File'; web instead derives names from fileUrl (tickets/[id]/page.tsx:374) which works.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a TicketAttachmentDTO {id, fileUrl, fileType, fileSize, uploadedAt} (or @JsonIgnore the ticket field), and have the manager app derive the display name from fileUrl like web does.

findings.title: Mobile admin vendor creation sends 'name' instead of required 'nameEn' — guaranteed 400 on every create
findings.evidence: Backend: VendorController.java:34 `public ResponseEntity<Vendor> createVendor(@Valid @RequestBody Vendor vendor)` binds directly to the Vendor entity, whose only name field is Vendor.java:22-24 `@NotBlank(message = "Vendor name (English) is required") @Column(name = "name_en", nullable = false) private String nameEn;` (there is no `name` property). Frontend: vendors_screen.dart:217-227 builds the body as `await service.createVendor({ 'name': nameCtrl.text.trim(), if (...) 'email': ..., 'phone': ..., 'address': ..., 'trn': ... })`, sent via vendor_service.dart:18 `_dio.post('/v1/vendors', data: data)`. Jackson (Spring Boot default FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=false) silently drops the unknown `name` key, leaving nameEn null, so @Valid rejects with 400 'Vendor name (English) is required' on every submission. The catch block at vendors_screen.dart:230-236 shows the generic 'create failed' snackbar, so vendor creation from the manager app can never succeed. Web sends the correct field (`nameEn`) for the same endpoint at web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/finance/vendors/page.tsx:139, confirming the mobile payload is the wrong one.
findings.recommendation: Change the mobile payload key from 'name' to 'nameEn' in vendors_screen.dart:218 (and consider collecting nameAr too).

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Mobile: vendors_screen.dart:217-227 posts {'name': ...} via vendor_service.dart:18 to POST /api/v1/vendors; the only Dio interceptors (AuthInterceptor, TenantInterceptor in rentaxis_core/lib/api/interceptors/) add headers only and never rewrite the body. Backend: VendorController.createVendor(@Valid @RequestBody Vendor) binds directly to the Vendor entity, which has only nameEn (@NotBlank, name_en NOT NULL) and nameAr — no 'name' property, no @JsonAlias, no custom Jackson config (grep of backend/src/main found none), and BaseTenantEntity adds no name field. Jackson's Spring Boot default drops the unknown 'name' key, nameEn stays null, and @Valid rejects with 400 on every create; the catch block shows the generic 'Failed to create vendor' snackbar. Web (finance/vendors/page.tsx:139) correctly sends nameEn to the same endpoint, confirming the contract. Corroborating evidence the screen was built against a wrong contract: list rendering/search also read v['name'] (lines 60, 361) while the backend serializes nameEn, so vendor names display as 'Unknown'. Severity correction: this fully breaks vendor creation from the mobile admin app, but it is a single-feature functional defect in one client with no security/data-loss/tenant-isolation impact and a working web workaround — 'high', not 'critical'.

findings.title: Mobile admin reads nonexistent vendor field 'name' — every vendor renders as 'Unknown'/'-' and name search never matches
findings.evidence: The Vendor entity returned by GET /api/v1/vendors and /{id} serializes `nameEn`/`nameAr` (Vendor.java:22-27); there is no `name` property in the JSON. Mobile reads the nonexistent key in four places: vendors_screen.dart:361 `final name = (vendor['name'] ?? l.unknown).toString();` (every list card shows the 'Unknown' fallback), vendors_screen.dart:60 `final name = (v['name'] ?? '').toString().toLowerCase();` (search-by-name always matches empty string, so name search is broken), vendor_detail_screen.dart:79 `final name = (vendor['name'] ?? l.unknown).toString();` (detail header shows 'Unknown'), and finance_reports_screen.dart:228 passes `nameKey: 'name'` to the vendor picker whose renderer at line 617 does `final name = (item[nameKey] ?? '-').toString();`, so the vendor-ledger picker lists every vendor as '-'.
findings.recommendation: Read `nameEn` (with `nameAr` fallback for AR locale) in all four locations instead of `name`.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. VendorController returns the Vendor entity directly; Jackson serializes nameEn/nameAr (Lombok getters), with no 'name' property, no @JsonProperty alias, no getName() on the entity chain, and no ObjectMapper/naming-strategy customization. The mobile VendorService returns response.data verbatim and the shared Dio client's interceptors (AuthInterceptor, TenantInterceptor) are request-only header injectors — no response transformation or envelope unwrapping exists. All four cited call sites read the nonexistent 'name' key exactly as claimed: vendors_screen.dart:60 (name search always matches empty string), :361 (list cards show 'Unknown'), vendor_detail_screen.dart:79 (detail header shows 'Unknown'), and finance_reports_screen.dart's _showVendorPicker passes nameKey:'name' to _PickerDialog whose renderer falls back to '-', so every vendor-ledger picker row is an indistinguishable '-'. The web frontend corroborates the wire contract by reading nameEn/nameAr from the same endpoints. As a side effect the mobile create-vendor sheet also posts 'name', which the backend ignores, so nameEn stays null and @NotBlank rejects it — mobile vendor creation fails as well. Severity corrected from critical to high: the vendors feature in the mobile admin app is effectively unusable for identifying vendors, but there is no data loss, no security/tenant-isolation impact, no crash, and the web admin works correctly (email/phone/TRN still render and remain searchable on mobile).

findings.title: Web notifications 'Unread' filter sends unreadOnly param the backend does not implement — tab shows read notifications
findings.evidence: Backend: NotificationController.java:21-28 declares only `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "0") int page, @RequestParam(defaultValue = "20") int size` — a repo-wide grep for 'unreadOnly' in backend/src/main/java returns zero hits, so the parameter is silently ignored. Frontend: notifications/page.tsx:74-77 `let url = \`/api/proxy/v1/notifications?page=${page}&size=${itemsPerPage}\`; if (filter === "UNREAD") { url += "&unreadOnly=true"; }`. The response is rendered unfiltered (page.tsx:82 `setNotifications(data)`), so clicking the 'Unread' tab shows exactly the same list including read notifications — the filter visibly does nothing whenever any notification is read.
findings.recommendation: Either add an `unreadOnly` request param to NotificationController/NotificationService, or filter client-side (`data.filter(n => !n.isRead)`) until the backend supports it.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Frontend (web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/notifications/page.tsx:74-77) appends unreadOnly=true via raw fetch through the Next.js rewrite (/api/proxy/:path* -> backend /api/:path*, query string untouched, no interceptor). Backend NotificationController.java:23-27 declares only page/size, so Spring silently drops unreadOnly; NotificationService.getNotifications (NotificationService.java:223-230) calls NotificationRepository.findAllByUserIdUnfiltered, a native query with no is_read predicate. The repository even has an unused findUnreadByUserIdUnfiltered method, confirming the filter was never wired. The page renders the response with no client-side isRead filter, so the Unread tab shows the identical list as All. Severity downgraded from high to medium: it is a visibly broken filter but has no security/data impact, and unread items are still visually distinguished (bold, dot, tint) in the combined list, so user impact is an inconvenience rather than loss of functionality.

findings.title: Web notifications pagination sets totalItems to the returned page length — pages beyond the first are unreachable
findings.evidence: Backend returns a plain `List<NotificationDTO>` capped at `size` (NotificationController.java:23-27) with no total count. Frontend: notifications/page.tsx:81-83 `if (Array.isArray(data)) { setNotifications(data); setTotalItems(data.length); }` — totalItems is therefore always <= itemsPerPage. Pagination.tsx:24 computes `const totalPages = Math.ceil(totalItems / itemsPerPage);`, which is always 1 (e.g. 25 items / 25 per page), so no page-2 button ever renders and `onPageChange` can never fire. A user with more than 25 notifications can never see the older ones; the Page-shape fallback at page.tsx:85-86 (`data.content`/`data.totalElements`) handles a response shape this endpoint never returns.
findings.recommendation: Either return Spring's Page wrapper (content + totalElements) from the backend, or infer 'has more' client-side (returned length === size => enable next page) instead of using data.length as the total.

verdict.explanation: Confirmed end-to-end. Backend (NotificationController.java:21-28 + NotificationService.java:223-230) returns a plain List<NotificationDTO> capped via .skip(page*size).limit(size) with no total count. The /api/proxy path is a pure rewrite in web/next.config.ts (no transforming route handler exists), so notifications/page.tsx:81-83 always hits the Array.isArray branch and sets totalItems = data.length <= itemsPerPage; the Page-envelope fallback (lines 85-86) is dead code. Pagination.tsx:24 then computes totalPages = 1, renders only a page-1 button, and disables the next arrow (currentPage === totalPages), so onPageChange can never advance the page — notifications beyond the first page are unreachable. Severity corrected to medium: no data loss, security, or tenant-isolation impact; a partial workaround exists (per-page selector goes up to 100), and the impact is limited to browsing older notification history in the web dashboard.

findings.title: Manager app exposes Vendors to PROPERTY_MANAGER users but all vendor endpoints require SUPER_ADMIN/TENANT_ADMIN
findings.evidence: VendorController.java:14 has class-level `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN')")` — PROPERTY_MANAGER is excluded. The manager app is used by PROPERTY_MANAGER accounts (profile_screen.dart:650-651 renders labels for both 'TENANT_ADMIN' and 'PROPERTY_MANAGER'), yet the More menu shows the Vendors entry unconditionally (more_screen.dart:106-110 `_MenuRow(icon: Icons.store_outlined, label: l.vendors, onTap: () => context.push('/vendors'))`) and finance_reports_screen.dart:220 calls `getVendors()` for the vendor-ledger picker with no role gate. A PROPERTY_MANAGER user gets a 403 and only sees the generic ErrorState (vendors_screen.dart:56-57). The web frontend gates the same feature correctly: web/src/lib/rbac.ts:16 `canAccessFinance: ['SUPER_ADMIN', 'TENANT_ADMIN']` hides /dashboard/finance/vendors from PMs.
findings.recommendation: Either add PROPERTY_MANAGER to VendorController's @PreAuthorize (if PMs should manage vendors), or hide the Vendors menu row and vendor-ledger picker in the manager app when authState.role == 'PROPERTY_MANAGER', matching the web rbac gating.

findings.title: Portfolio import status polling never terminates on error responses — polls a dead job forever
findings.evidence: Backend returns 404 when the job is missing or belongs to another tenant (PortfolioImportController.java:71-76 `.filter(job -> job.getTenantId().equals(TenantContextHolder.getTenantId())) ... .orElse(ResponseEntity.notFound().build())`), and 401/403 on session expiry. Frontend: properties/page.tsx:257-271 `const interval = setInterval(async () => { ... const res = await fetch(...); if (!res.ok) return; ... }, 2000);` — a non-OK response just returns from the tick, and the catch block comment says 'keep polling', so on 404/401 the dialog spins on the 'processing' step forever with a request every 2 seconds and no timeout or error state. The happy-path terminal statuses do match the service ("COMPLETED"/"VALIDATION_FAILED"/"FAILED" at page.tsx:263 vs PortfolioImportService.java:622,636,645).
findings.recommendation: Treat 404/401/403 as terminal (clearInterval + show a failure state), and add a max-poll timeout as a safety net.

findings.title: Web vendor delete silently swallows the 400 'Cannot delete vendor with existing transactions' error
findings.evidence: Backend: VendorService.java:58-66 `deleteVendor` throws `BusinessRuleViolationException("Cannot delete vendor with existing transactions")`, mapped to HTTP 400 with a `message` field by GlobalExceptionHandler.java:41-47 (NotFoundException maps to 404 at lines 32-38). Frontend: vendors/page.tsx:187-197 `onConfirm: async () => { setConfirmDialog(null); try { const res = await fetch(\`/api/proxy/v1/vendors/${vendor.id}\`, { method: "DELETE" }); if (res.ok) fetchVendors(); } catch (err) { console.error(err); } }` — there is no else branch, so when a vendor has transactions (the common case for any vendor actually in use) the confirm dialog closes and nothing happens: no toast, no message, and the row stays with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: On !res.ok, parse the body and surface `message` (e.g. via the existing banner state) so the user learns why the delete was rejected.

findings.title: Web vendor create/update ignores validation failures — modal stays open with no error message
findings.evidence: Backend validates with @Valid: Vendor.java has `@NotBlank` nameEn, `@Email` email (line 33-34) and `@Size(max = 20)` phone (line 38-39), producing 400 MethodArgumentNotValidException responses. Frontend: vendors/page.tsx:162-178 `const res = await fetch(url, { method, headers..., body: JSON.stringify(body) }); if (res.ok) { setShowModal(false); ... fetchVendors(); }` — no else branch and the catch only logs, so a 400 (e.g. malformed email or 21+ char phone; the form fields have no client-side validation for these) leaves the modal open with the spinner stopped and zero feedback. The request payload itself is correct (nameEn at line 139, nested `payableAccount: { id }` at line 154 matching the @ManyToOne, and `active` matching Lombok's `isActive()`/`setActive()` Jackson property).
findings.recommendation: Add an error state to the modal: on !res.ok parse the validation body and display the message next to the submit button.

findings.title: Push-device registration endpoint is dead: registerDevice exists in the shared mobile service but is never called
findings.evidence: Backend: NotificationController.java:50-57 `@PostMapping("/devices/register") ... registerDevice(@RequestHeader("X-User-Id") UUID userId, @RequestBody Map<String, String> body)` reading body.get("token")/body.get("platform"). The shared client method exists (notification_service.dart:28-33 posts `{'token': token, 'platform': platform}` — a shape that matches), but a repo-wide grep shows zero call sites for `registerDevice` in manager, renter, or security apps and web, and no firebase_messaging/FCM integration in any app (only firebase_auth in the security app's phone login). Device tokens are therefore never registered and any push-notification sending path in NotificationService has no devices to target.
findings.recommendation: Either wire up FCM token registration at app startup/login in the mobile apps, or remove the endpoint and the dead service method to shrink the attack surface.

findings.title: Portfolio template download does not check res.ok — auth/server errors are saved as a corrupt .xlsx
findings.evidence: Backend can return 500 on template generation failure (PortfolioImportController.java:87-90 `return ResponseEntity.internalServerError().build();`) and 401/403 on expired sessions or PROPERTY_MANAGER role. Frontend: properties/page.tsx:275-284 `const res = await fetch("/api/proxy/v1/import/portfolio/template"); const blob = await res.blob(); ... a.download = "portfolio-import-template.xlsx"; a.click();` — no res.ok check, so an error body (JSON or empty) is downloaded as portfolio-import-template.xlsx that Excel cannot open, with no message to the user.
findings.recommendation: Guard with `if (!res.ok) { show error toast; return; }` before creating the blob URL.
